groups.md:
Read the following passage carefully and answer questions from 11 to 15 :

If India has to develop her internal strengths, the nation has to focus on the technological imperatives, keeping in mind three dynamic dimensions : the people, the overall economy and the strategic interests. These technological imperatives also take into account a 'fourth' dimension, time, an offshoot of modern day dynamism in business, trade, and technology that leads to continually shifting targets. We believe that technological strengths are especially crucial in dealing with this fourth dimension underlying continuous change in the aspirations of the people, the economy in the global context, and the strategic interests. The progress of technology lies at the heart of human history. Technological strengths are the key to creating more productive employment in an increasingly competitive market place and to continually upgrade human skills. Without a pervasive use of technologies, we cannot achieve overall development of our people in the years to come. The direct linkages of technology to the nation's strategic strengths are becoming more and more clear, especially since 1990s. India's own strength in a number of core areas still puts it in a position of reasonable strength in geo-political context. Any nation aspiring to become a developed one needs to have strengths in various strategic technologies and also the ability to continually upgrade them through its own creative strengths. For people-oriented actions as well, whether for the creation of large scale productive employment or for ensuring nutritional and health security for people, or for better living conditions, technology is the only vital input. The absence of greater technological impetus could lead to lower productivity and wastage of precious natural resources. Activities with low productivity or low value addition, in the final analysis hurt the poorest most. The technological imperatives to lift our people to a new life, and to a life they are entitled to is important. India, aspiring to become a major economic power in terms of trade and increase in GDP, cannot succeed on the strength of turnkey projects designed and built abroad or only through large-scale imports of plant machinery, equipment and know how. Even while being alive to the short-term realities, medium and long-term strategies to develop core technological strengths within our industry are vital for envisioning a developed India.

The table below embodies data on the production, exports and per capita consumption of rice in country P for the five years from 2012 to 2016. Answer questions 31 - 35 based on the data contained in the table.

**Year-wise Production, Exports and Per Capita Consumption of Rice**

| Year | Production (in million kg) | Exports (in million kg) | Per Capita Consumption (in kg) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2012 | 186.5 | 114 | 36.25 |
| 2013 | 202 | 114 | 35.2 |
| 2014 | 238 | 130 | 38.7 |
| 2015 | 221 | 116 | 40.5 |
| 2016 | 215 | 88 | 42 |

Where, Per Capita Consumption = (Consumption in million kg) ÷ (Population in million) and consumption (in million kg) = Production − Exports.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following set of statements best describes the nature and objectives of teaching ? Indicate your answer by selecting from the code.

(a) Teaching and learning are integrally related.
(b) There is no difference between teaching and training.
(c) Concern of all teaching is to ensure some kind of transformation in students.
(d) All good teaching is formal in nature.
(e) A teacher is a senior person.
(f) Teaching is a social act whereas learning is a personal act.

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
Good teaching always aims at learning and change in the learner.

- **(a) True.** Teaching has meaning only when it leads to learning. So the two go closely together.
- **(b) False.** Training builds fixed skills by practice. Teaching also builds understanding, values and thinking.
- **(c) True.** All teaching tries to bring some change in the student's knowledge, skill or attitude.
- **(d) False.** Good teaching can also be informal, for example a talk outside class.
- **(e) False.** Age or seniority does not make a person a teacher.
- **(f) True.** A teacher acts in a social setting with students. But each learner learns inside his or her own mind.

So the correct set is (a), (c) and (f). Every other code includes at least one false statement, such as (b) or (d).

questions.question_md: Which of the following learner characteristics is highly related to effectiveness of teaching ?
options: Educational status of the parents of the learner
Family size from which the learner comes.
questions.explanation:
Effective teaching starts from what the learner already knows. The prior experience of the learner gives the base for new learning. A teacher links new ideas to this old knowledge. This makes learning faster and deeper.

The other options are background factors.

- The education of the parents can affect the learner, but only in an indirect way.
- Peer groups (friends of the same age) can affect motivation, but they do not directly decide how well teaching works.
- Family size has an even weaker link with the effectiveness of teaching.

So prior experience has the closest link to effective teaching.

questions.question_md:
In the two sets given below **Set - I** indicates methods of teaching while **Set - II** provides the basic requirements for success/effectiveness. Match the two sets and indicate your answer by choosing from the code :

| Set - I (Method of teaching) | Set - II (Basic requirements for success/effectiveness) |
|---|---|
| (a) Lecturing | (i) Small step presentation with feedback provided |
| (b) Discussion in groups | (ii) Production of large number of ideas |
| (c) Brainstorming | (iii) Content delivery in a lucid language |
| (d) Programmed Instructional procedure | (iv) Use of teaching-aids |
| | (v) Theme based interaction among participants |
questions.explanation:
Match each method with the condition that makes it work.

- **(a) Lecturing – (iii).** In a lecture, the teacher mainly delivers content. Clear and simple language is the key need.
- **(b) Discussion in groups – (v).** A group discussion works when members interact on one theme.
- **(c) Brainstorming – (ii).** Brainstorming aims to produce a large number of ideas quickly. Members do not judge ideas at first.
- **(d) Programmed instruction – (i).** This method gives content in small steps. The learner gets feedback after each step.

Item (iv), teaching aids, is extra. It helps many methods, but it is not the basic need of any one of them. Only option (3) gives all four correct pairs.

questions.question_md:
From the list of evaluation procedures given below identify those which will be called 'formative evaluation'. Indicate your answer by choosing from the code :

(a) A teacher awards grades to students after having transacted the course work.
(b) During interaction with students in the classroom, the teacher provides corrective feedback.
(c) The teacher gives marks to students on a unit test.
(d) The teacher clarifies the doubts of students in the class itself.
(e) The overall performance of a students is reported to parents at every three months interval.
(f) The learner's motivation is raised by the teacher through a question-answer session.

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
Formative evaluation happens during teaching. Its aim is to improve learning while the course goes on. Summative evaluation comes at the end and gives grades or marks.

- **(a) Summative.** Grades after the course is over.
- **(b) Formative.** Corrective feedback during class interaction.
- **(c) Summative in nature.** The teacher gives marks on a unit test to judge results.
- **(d) Formative.** The teacher clears doubts on the spot.
- **(e) Summative.** A report of overall performance goes to parents.
- **(f) Formative.** A question-answer session raises motivation during learning.

So (b), (d) and (f) are formative. The other codes include grading or reporting, which are summative.

questions.question_md:
**Assertion (A) :** All teaching should aim at ensuring learning.

**Reason (R) :** All learning results from teaching.

Choose the **correct** answer from the following code :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** The purpose of teaching is learning. Teaching that does not lead to learning has failed.
- **(R) is false.** Not all learning comes from teaching. People also learn from experience, play, reading, observation and self-study.

So (A) is true, but (R) is false. Options (1) and (2) are wrong because they accept (R) as true. Option (4) is wrong because (A) is true.

questions.question_md:
There are two sets given below. **Set - I** specifies the types of research, while **Set - II** indicates their characteristics. Match the two and give your answer by selecting the appropriate code.

| Set - I (Research types) | Set - II (Characteristics) |
|---|---|
| (a) Fundamental research | (i) Finding out the extent of perceived impact of an intervention |
| (b) Applied research | (ii) Developing an effective explanation through theory building |
| (c) Action research | (iii) Improving an existing situation through use of interventions |
| (d) Evaluative research | (iv) Exploring the possibility of a theory for use in various situations |
| | (v) Enriching technological resources |
questions.explanation:
Match each research type with its main purpose.

- **(a) Fundamental research – (ii).** Basic research builds theory. It tries to explain things in a general way.
- **(b) Applied research – (iv).** Applied research tests how a theory can work in different real situations.
- **(c) Action research – (iii).** A teacher or worker uses an intervention (a planned change) to improve a local problem.
- **(d) Evaluative research – (i).** Evaluation research measures the impact of a programme or intervention.

Item (v), enriching technological resources, is extra. It does not define any of these four types. Only option (1) has all four pairs right.

questions.question_md: Which of the sets of activities best indicate the cyclic nature of action research strategy ?
questions.explanation:
Action research moves in a cycle. The common model, from Kemmis and McTaggart, has four steps:

1. **Plan** – decide on a change to solve a practical problem.
2. **Act** – put the plan into practice.
3. **Observe** – collect evidence about the effect of the action.
4. **Reflect** – think about the results.

After reflection, the researcher makes a new plan, and the cycle starts again. So the order is Plan, Act, Observe, Reflect.

The other options put the steps in a wrong order. For example, a researcher cannot act before planning.

questions.question_md: Which of the following sequences of research steps is nearer to scientific method ?
options: Suggested solution of the problem, Deducing the consequences of the solution, Perceiving the problem situation, Location of the difficulty and testing the solutions.
Perceiving the problem situation, Locating the actual problem and its definition, Hypothesizing, Deducing the consequences of the suggested solution and Testing the hypothesis in action.
Defining a problem, Identifying the causes of the problem, Defining a population, Drawing a sample, Collecting data and Analysing results.
Identifying the causal factors, Defining the problem, Developing a hypothesis, Selecting a sample, Collecting data and arriving at generalizations and Conclusions.
questions.explanation:
The scientific method follows the steps of reflective thinking that John Dewey described:

1. Feel or perceive a problem situation.
2. Locate and define the actual problem.
3. Suggest a hypothesis (a possible solution).
4. Deduce (work out) the results of this hypothesis.
5. Test the hypothesis in action.

Option (2) follows this order exactly.

- Option (1) puts the solution before the problem.
- Option (3) has no hypothesis step. It only lists survey steps.
- Option (4) identifies causes before it defines the problem, which is the wrong order.

questions.question_md: The problem of 'research ethics' is concerned with which aspect of research activities ?
options: Following the prescribed format of a thesis
Data analysis through qualitative or quantitative techniques
questions.explanation:
Research ethics means honest and fair conduct in research. A key part is honest reporting. The researcher must report only what the evidence shows. The researcher must not invent data, change data or copy the work of others.

So research ethics is about evidence-based research reporting.

- The format of a thesis is a matter of style, not ethics.
- The choice of qualitative or quantitative analysis is a technical choice.
- Defining the population is a step in research design.

These three are technical parts of research. They are not mainly ethical issues.

questions.question_md: In which of the following activities, potential for nurturing creative and critical thinking is relatively greater ?
questions.explanation:
A research conference brings together many researchers. A participant hears many papers on different topics. People ask questions, challenge ideas and defend their own views. This open debate builds critical thinking. Contact with new ideas also builds creative thinking.

The other activities have less scope:

- A research summary only restates work that is already done.
- A seminar paper usually has one presenter and a small audience.
- A workshop mainly trains people in a skill by practice.

So the examiner chose participation in a research conference as the best answer.

questions.question_md:
According to the above passage, which of the following are indicative of the fourth dimension ?

(a) Aspirations of people
(b) Modern day dynamism
(c) Economy in the global context
(d) Strategic interests

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
The passage says that technology helps to deal with the fourth dimension, time. This dimension underlies continuous change in three things:

- the **aspirations of the people** – (a)
- the **economy in the global context** – (c)
- the **strategic interests** – (d)

So (a), (c) and (d) indicate the fourth dimension.

Item (b), modern day dynamism, is tempting. But the passage calls the fourth dimension an "offshoot" of modern day dynamism. This means that dynamism is the source of the time dimension, not a sign of it. So codes with (b) are wrong.

questions.question_md: More productive employment demands :
questions.explanation:
The passage says that technological strengths are the key to more productive employment. It then adds: "Without a pervasive use of technologies, we cannot achieve overall development of our people." Pervasive means present everywhere.

So more productive employment needs the pervasive use of technology.

- The passage speaks of an increasingly competitive market. It does not ask us to limit competition.
- Geo-political ideas link to strategic strength, not to employment.
- The passage does not say that large industries create employment.

questions.question_md:
Absence of technology would lead to :

(a) Less pollution
(b) Wastage of precious natural resources
(c) Low value addition
(d) Hurting the poorest most

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
The passage says that the absence of a greater technological push "could lead to lower productivity and wastage of precious natural resources". It adds that activities with low productivity or low value addition "hurt the poorest most".

- **(b) Yes.** The passage states wastage of natural resources.
- **(c) Yes.** The passage states low value addition.
- **(d) Yes.** The passage states that low value addition hurts the poorest most.
- **(a) No.** The passage says nothing about less pollution.

So the answer is (b), (c) and (d) only. Every other code includes (a).

questions.question_md: The advantage of technological inputs would result in :
options: Lifting our people to a life of dignity
questions.explanation:
The passage says that technology can "lift our people to a new life, and to a life they are entitled to". A life that people have a right to is a life of dignity. So technological inputs help to lift people to a life of dignity.

- The passage does not support unbridled (uncontrolled) growth of technology.
- It warns against depending on imports of plant machinery.
- It does not ask us to sideline environmental issues. In fact, it worries about the waste of natural resources.

questions.question_md: Envisioning a developed India requires :
options: Aspiration to become a major economic player
questions.explanation:
The last sentence of the passage says that strategies "to develop core technological strengths within our industry are vital for envisioning a developed India".

So a developed India needs the development of core technological strengths.

- The passage mentions the aim to become a major economic power. But it says that this aim alone cannot succeed.
- It rejects dependence on turnkey projects designed and built abroad.
- It asks for medium-term and long-term strategies, not a focus on short-term projects.

questions.question_md: Differentiation between acceptance and non-acceptance of certain stimuli in classroom communication is the basis of :
questions.explanation:
In a classroom, students receive many stimuli (signals) at the same time. These include the teacher's voice, noise, pictures and other students. A student accepts some stimuli and ignores others. This process of choosing what to notice is **selective attention**.

- Selective expectation is about what a person expects to happen.
- Selective affiliation is about choosing friends or groups.
- Selective morality is about choosing moral rules.

None of these three explains how a student accepts or rejects stimuli.

questions.question_md:
**Assertion (A) :** The initial messages to students in the classroom by a teacher need not be critical to establish interactions later.

**Reason (R) :** More control over the communication process means more control over what the students are learning.

**Code :**
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is false.** The first messages of a teacher are very important. They set the tone of the class. They build trust and show students how to interact. So these first messages are critical for later interaction.
- **(R) is true.** A teacher who controls the flow of communication can guide what students attend to. So the teacher has more control over what students learn.

(A) is false and (R) is true. So options (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.

questions.question_md:
**Assertion (A) :** To communicate well in the classroom is a natural ability.

**Reason (R) :** Effective teaching in the classroom demands knowledge of the communication process.

**Code :**
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is false.** Good classroom communication is not a natural gift. It is a skill. A teacher learns it through study, practice and feedback.
- **(R) is true.** An effective teacher must understand the parts of communication: the sender, the message, the channel, the receiver, feedback and barriers. This knowledge helps the teacher to send clear messages.

(A) is false and (R) is true. In fact, (R) shows why (A) is false: communication needs knowledge, so it is not just a natural ability.

questions.question_md:
**Assertion (A) :** Classroom communication is a transactional process.

**Reason (R) :** A teacher does not operate under the assumption that students' responses are purposive.

Select the **correct** code for your answer :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** Classroom communication is transactional. This means that teacher and students send and receive messages at the same time. Each side affects the other.
- **(R) is false.** A good teacher assumes that student responses are purposive (they have a purpose or meaning). The teacher reads these responses as feedback and adjusts the lesson.

So (A) is true, but (R) is false. Options (1) and (2) are wrong because they accept (R). Option (4) is wrong because (A) is true.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following set of statements is **correct** for describing the human communication process ?

(a) Non-verbal communication can stimulate ideas.
(b) Communication is a learnt ability.
(c) Communication is not a universal panacea.
(d) Communication cannot break-down.
(e) More communication means more effective learning by students.
(f) Value of what is learnt through classroom communication is not an issue for students.

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
This question uses common ideas from communication textbooks about "myths" of communication.

- **(a) True.** Gestures, pictures and silence can stimulate ideas.
- **(b) True.** Communication is a learnt skill, not only a natural gift.
- **(c) True.** Communication is not a universal panacea (a cure for all problems). Some problems remain even after a lot of talk.
- **(d) True in this view.** Textbooks call "communication can break down" a myth. People always send some message, even by silence. So communication never fully stops.
- **(e) False.** More communication does not always mean better learning. Too much talk can confuse students.
- **(f) False.** Students care about the value of what they learn.

So the set is (a), (b), (c) and (d). The other codes include (e) or (f).

questions.question_md:
The next term in the series

−1, 5, 15, 29, ___?___, ...

is :
questions.explanation:
Find the differences between the terms.

- 5 − (−1) = 6
- 15 − 5 = 10
- 29 − 15 = 14

The differences go up by 4 each time: 6, 10, 14. The next difference is 14 + 4 = 18.

Next term = 29 + 18 = **47**.

The other options do not fit this pattern. For example, 36 gives a difference of only 7.

questions.question_md:
The next term in the series

ABD, DGK, HMS, MTB, SBL, ___?___, ...

is :
questions.explanation:
Look at each letter position on its own. Use A = 1, B = 2, … Z = 26. After Z, count again from A.

- **First letters:** A, D, H, M, S (1, 4, 8, 13, 19). The gaps are +3, +4, +5, +6. The next gap is +7. 19 + 7 = 26 = **Z**.
- **Second letters:** B, G, M, T, B (2, 7, 13, 20, 28 → 2). The gaps are +5, +6, +7, +8. The next gap is +9. 2 + 9 = 11 = **K**.
- **Third letters:** D, K, S, B, L. The gaps are +7, +8, +9, +10. The next gap is +11. L (12) + 11 = 23 = **W**.

The next term is **ZKW**. ZKU has the wrong third letter. KZU starts with K, not Z.

questions.question_md: If VARANASI is coded as WCUESGZQ, then the code of KOLKATA will be :
questions.explanation:
Compare each letter of VARANASI with its code WCUESGZQ.

- V → W (+1), A → C (+2), R → U (+3), A → E (+4)
- N → S (+5), A → G (+6), S → Z (+7), I → Q (+8)

The first letter moves 1 step forward, the second moves 2 steps, and so on.

Apply the same rule to KOLKATA:

- K + 1 = **L**
- O + 2 = **Q**
- L + 3 = **O**
- K + 4 = **O**
- A + 5 = **F**
- T + 6 = **Z**
- A + 7 = **H**

The code is **LQOOFZH**. The other options do not follow this rule.

questions.question_md: Introducing Rakesh to her husband a women said, "His brother's father is the only son of my grandfather". The woman is related to Rakesh as :
questions.explanation:
Break the statement into parts.

- "His brother's father" is Rakesh's father.
- "The only son of my grandfather" is the woman's father. Her grandfather has only one son, so this son must be her father.

So Rakesh's father and the woman's father are the same person. Rakesh and the woman have the same father. So the woman is Rakesh's **sister**.

They share a father, so they are in the same generation. So she cannot be his aunt, mother or daughter.

questions.question_md: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 5. If 16 is added to both the numbers, their ratio becomes 1 : 2. The numbers are :
questions.explanation:
Let the numbers be 2x and 5x.

After we add 16 to each number, the ratio becomes 1 : 2:

(2x + 16) ÷ (5x + 16) = 1 ÷ 2

Cross-multiply: 2(2x + 16) = 5x + 16

4x + 32 = 5x + 16

x = 16

So the numbers are 2 × 16 = **32** and 5 × 16 = **80**.

Check: 32 + 16 = 48 and 80 + 16 = 96. The ratio 48 : 96 = 1 : 2.

The other pairs fail. For example, 16 + 16 = 32 and 40 + 16 = 56, and 32 : 56 is not 1 : 2.

questions.question_md:
Superiority of intellect depends upon its power of concentration on one theme in the same way as a concave mirror collects all the rays that strike upon it into one point.

What type of reasoning is entailed in the above statement ?
questions.explanation:
The statement compares two different things. A strong mind focuses on one theme. A concave mirror collects all light rays into one point. The statement says that the mind works "in the same way" as the mirror.

Reasoning that compares two things because they are similar in some way is **analogical reasoning** (reasoning by analogy).

- The statement has no numbers or calculation, so it is not mathematical.
- It talks about the mind, but its form is a comparison, not a psychological argument.
- It does not draw a necessary conclusion from general premises, so it is not deductive.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two premises (A and B). Four conclusions are drawn from them. Select the code that states validly drawn conclusion(s) (taking the premises individually or jointly).

**Premises :**

(A) Most of the dancers are physically fit.
(B) Most of the singers are dancers.

**Conclusions :**

(a) Most of the singers are physically fit.
(b) Most of the dancers are singers.
(c) Most of the physically fit persons are dancers.
(d) Most of the physically fit persons are singers.

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
Strictly, "most" premises like these do not give any valid conclusion. But the examiner treats "most" as a particular (some) proposition. We can convert a particular affirmative proposition. This means that we swap the subject and the predicate.

- **(b)** is the converse of premise (B): "Most singers are dancers" → "dancers are singers".
- **(c)** is the converse of premise (A): "Most dancers are physically fit" → "physically fit persons are dancers".
- **(a)** does not follow. The singers who are dancers may all be in the group of dancers who are not fit.
- **(d)** does not follow for the same reason.

So the examiner's answer is (b) and (c). Note that the word "most" makes even the converse doubtful. The examiner reads it in the weaker sense of "some".

questions.question_md: Which one among the following is a presupposition in inductive reasoning ?
questions.explanation:
Inductive reasoning moves from observed cases to a general rule. For example, we see that metals expand when we heat them. Then we say that all metals expand when heated.

This step is safe only if nature behaves in the same way at all times and places. This basic belief is the **uniformity of nature**. Inductive reasoning presupposes (takes for granted) this principle.

- The law of identity (A is A) is a law of thought used in deductive logic.
- "Unchangeability in nature" is wrong, because nature changes. Only its laws stay the same.
- "Harmony in nature" is not a standard principle of induction.

questions.question_md:
If the proposition 'domestic animals are hardly ferocious' is taken to be false, which of the following proposition/propositions can be claimed to be certainly true ? Select the **correct** code :

**Propositions :**

(a) All domestic animals are ferocious.
(b) Most of the domestic animals are ferocious.
(c) No domestic animal is ferocious.
(d) Some domestic animals are non-ferocious.

**Code :**
questions.explanation:
The examiner reads "domestic animals are hardly ferocious" as a negative claim. It means "Some (or many) domestic animals are not ferocious". This is an O-type proposition (particular negative).

The proposition is false. So its contradictory must be true. The contradictory of an O-type proposition is the A-type: "All domestic animals are ferocious".

- **(a) True.** This is the contradictory, so it is certainly true.
- **(b) True.** If all domestic animals are ferocious, then most of them are ferocious.
- **(c) False.** It is the opposite of (a).
- **(d) False.** It says almost the same as the false statement.

So (a) and (b) are certainly true. This question depends on how we read the word "hardly". The answer follows the examiner's reading.

questions.question_md: Which one of the following statements is **not** correct in the context of Venn diagram method ?
options: It is a method of testing the validity of arguments.
It represents both the premises of a syllogism in one diagram.
It requires two overlapping circles for the two premises of a standard-form categorical syllogism.
It can be used to represent classes as well as propositions.
questions.explanation:
A standard-form categorical syllogism has three terms: the major term, the minor term and the middle term. The Venn diagram method needs one circle for each term. So it needs **three** overlapping circles, not two. That is why the statement in option (3) is not correct.

The other statements are correct.

- Venn diagrams test whether a syllogism is valid.
- We draw both premises in one diagram. Then we check whether the conclusion is already shown.
- Circles can stand for classes. Shading and marks can show propositions.

questions.question_md: The percentage increase in the consumption of rice over the previous year was the highest in which year ?
questions.explanation:
Consumption = Production − Exports.

- 2012: 186.5 − 114 = 72.5
- 2013: 202 − 114 = 88
- 2014: 238 − 130 = 108
- 2015: 221 − 116 = 105
- 2016: 215 − 88 = 127

Now find the percentage increase over the previous year.

- 2013: (88 − 72.5) ÷ 72.5 = 15.5 ÷ 72.5 ≈ 21.4%
- 2014: (108 − 88) ÷ 88 = 20 ÷ 88 ≈ **22.7%**
- 2015: consumption falls from 108 to 105, so there is no increase.
- 2016: (127 − 105) ÷ 105 = 22 ÷ 105 ≈ 21.0%

The highest increase is in **2014**. Note that 2016 has the largest increase in million kg (22). But its base is larger, so its percentage is smaller.

questions.question_md: What is the population of the country in the year 2014 (in million) ?
questions.explanation:
Use the formula in the table note.

Population = Consumption ÷ Per capita consumption

For 2014:

- Consumption = 238 − 130 = 108 million kg
- Per capita consumption = 38.7 kg
- Population = 108 ÷ 38.7 ≈ **2.79 million**

Check: 38.7 × 2.79 ≈ 108. The other values give a wrong product. For example, 38.7 × 2.72 ≈ 105.3, which is too small.

questions.question_md: The ratio of exports to consumption in the given period was the highest in the year :
questions.explanation:
Consumption = Production − Exports. Divide exports by consumption for each year.

- 2012: 114 ÷ 72.5 ≈ **1.57**
- 2013: 114 ÷ 88 ≈ 1.30
- 2014: 130 ÷ 108 ≈ 1.20
- 2015: 116 ÷ 105 ≈ 1.10

The ratio is highest in **2012**. In 2012 and 2013, exports are the same (114). But consumption in 2012 is smaller, so the ratio is larger. In 2014, exports are highest, but consumption is also much higher.

questions.question_md: In which year, the population of country was the highest ?
questions.explanation:
Population = Consumption ÷ Per capita consumption. Consumption = Production − Exports.

- 2012: 72.5 ÷ 36.25 = 2.00 million
- 2013: 88 ÷ 35.2 = 2.50 million
- 2014: 108 ÷ 38.7 ≈ 2.79 million
- 2015: 105 ÷ 40.5 ≈ 2.59 million
- 2016: 127 ÷ 42 ≈ **3.02 million**

The population is highest in **2016**. Production was highest in 2014, but production alone does not decide the population.

questions.question_md: What is the average consumption of rice (in million kg) over the years 2012-2016 ?
questions.explanation:
Consumption = Production − Exports.

- 2012: 186.5 − 114 = 72.5
- 2013: 202 − 114 = 88
- 2014: 238 − 130 = 108
- 2015: 221 − 116 = 105
- 2016: 215 − 88 = 127

Total = 72.5 + 88 + 108 + 105 + 127 = 500.5 million kg

Average = 500.5 ÷ 5 = **100.1 million kg**

The other options do not match this total. For example, an average of 104 needs a total of 520.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements, regarding the term ICT is/are TRUE ?

**P :** ICT is an acronym that stands for Indian Classical Technology.

**Q :** Converging technologies that exemplify ICT include the merging of audio-visual, telephone and computer networks through a common cabling system.
questions.explanation:
- **P is false.** ICT stands for **Information and Communication Technology**. It does not mean "Indian Classical Technology".
- **Q is true.** ICT includes the convergence (joining together) of different networks. Audio-visual, telephone and computer networks can share one common cabling or link system. This convergence is a typical example of ICT.

So only Q is true.

questions.question_md:
A new Laptop has been produced that weighs less, is smaller and uses less power than previous Laptop models.

Which of the following technologies has been used to accomplish this ?
questions.explanation:
A solid state drive (SSD) stores data on flash memory chips. It has no moving parts such as spinning disks or a moving head. So an SSD is lighter and smaller than a normal hard disk. It also uses less power.

These features match the new laptop: less weight, smaller size and less power use.

- A USB mouse is an external device. It does not change the laptop's size or power use.
- Faster RAM increases speed, but it does not make the laptop much lighter or smaller.
- A Blu-ray drive adds weight and uses extra power.

questions.question_md:
Given the following email fields, which of the email addresses will 'swami' be able to see when he receives the message ?

| Field | Addresses |
|---|---|
| To… | ram@test.com |
| Cc… | raj@test.com; ravi@test.com |
| Bcc… | swami@test.com; rama@test.com |
questions.notes: The email-fields box has no header row in the source; 'Field / Addresses' header added for Markdown.
questions.explanation:
In email, each field works in a different way.

- **To:** main receivers. All receivers can see these addresses.
- **Cc (carbon copy):** other receivers. All receivers can also see these addresses.
- **Bcc (blind carbon copy):** hidden receivers. Nobody sees the Bcc addresses of other people.

Swami is in the Bcc field. He can see the To address (ram@test.com) and the Cc addresses (raj@test.com and ravi@test.com). He cannot see rama@test.com, because Rama is also in Bcc.

So options (3) and (4) are wrong, because they show rama@test.com. Option (1) is wrong, because it leaves out the Cc addresses.

questions.question_md:
Put the following units of storage into the correct order, starting with the smallest unit first and going down to the largest unit :

(a) Kilobyte
(b) Byte
(c) Megabyte
(d) Terabyte
(e) Gigabyte
(f) Bit

Give your answer from the following code :
questions.explanation:
The units of storage from smallest to largest are:

1. **Bit** – one binary digit, 0 or 1 (f)
2. **Byte** – 8 bits (b)
3. **Kilobyte** – 1024 bytes (a)
4. **Megabyte** – 1024 KB (c)
5. **Gigabyte** – 1024 MB (e)
6. **Terabyte** – 1024 GB (d)

So the order is (f), (b), (a), (c), (e), (d).

Option (1) puts terabyte before gigabyte. Options (2) and (4) place terabyte too early.

questions.question_md:
With regard to computer memory, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE ?

**P :** Read Only Memory (ROM) is 'volatile' memory.

**Q :** Random Access Memory (RAM) is 'volatile' memory.

**R :** Secondary Memory is 'volatile' memory.
questions.explanation:
Volatile memory loses its data when the power goes off.

- **P is false.** ROM (Read Only Memory) keeps its data without power. So ROM is non-volatile.
- **Q is true.** RAM (Random Access Memory) loses its data when you switch off the computer. So RAM is volatile.
- **R is false.** Secondary memory, such as a hard disk or a pen drive, keeps data for a long time. So it is non-volatile.

So only Q is true.

questions.question_md:
'Fly ash' produced in thermal power plants is an ecofriendly resource for use in :

(a) agriculture as micro-nutrient
(b) wasteland development
(c) dam and water holding structures
(d) brick industry

Choose the **correct** answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation:
Fly ash is the fine ash that remains after coal burns in thermal power plants. It is a waste product, but it has many good uses.

- **(a) Agriculture.** Fly ash can improve soil. It supplies some micro-nutrients (nutrients that plants need in small amounts).
- **(b) Wasteland development.** It helps to fill and reclaim low-lying land and waste land.
- **(c) Dams and water holding structures.** Builders mix fly ash in concrete and use it in embankments.
- **(d) Brick industry.** Fly ash bricks are a common building material.

So all four uses are correct. Each of the other codes leaves out one correct use.

questions.question_md: Which of the following types of natural disasters has no definite beginning and end ?
questions.explanation:
A drought develops slowly. It comes from a long period of low rainfall. Nobody can say the exact day when it starts. Its effects can also continue for a long time after rain returns. So scientists call drought a "creeping" disaster, because it has no definite beginning and end.

The other disasters have a clear start and end.

- An earthquake lasts for seconds or minutes.
- A landslide happens suddenly.
- A hurricane forms, moves and then ends. Weather services can track its path.

questions.question_md:
**Assertion (A) :** Indoor air pollution is a serious health hazard.

**Reason (R) :** The dispersal of air pollutants is rather limited in indoor environment.

Choose the **correct** answer from the code given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** Indoor air pollution is a serious health hazard. In many Indian homes, people burn wood, cow dung and coal for cooking. The smoke causes lung and heart diseases. Women and children suffer most.
- **(R) is true.** Inside a house, air does not move freely. So the pollutants do not spread out and become thin. Their level stays high.

(R) explains (A). Pollutants stay at a high level indoors because they cannot disperse. So indoor air pollution becomes a serious hazard.

questions.question_md: In terms of their contribution to the total power generation in India, identify the correct sequence of energy sources - Thermal Power Plants (TPP), Large Hydropower Projects (LHP), Nuclear Energy (NE) and Renewable Energy (RE) which includes solar energy, wind energy, biomass and small hydropower projects.
questions.explanation:
The examiner's answer matches installed capacity (the total size of power plants) around 2018.

- **Thermal power plants** (coal, gas and diesel) had about 220 GW. This was by far the largest share.
- **Renewable energy** (solar, wind, biomass and small hydro) had about 69 GW.
- **Large hydropower** had about 45 GW.
- **Nuclear energy** had less than 7 GW.

So the order is TPP > RE > LHP > NE.

The word "generation" makes this question debatable. Solar and wind plants do not run all the time. So, in yearly units of electricity, large hydro was still a little ahead of renewables around 2017–18. The examiner used installed capacity.

questions.question_md: Which of the following is considered as major source of pollution in rivers of India ?
questions.explanation:
Untreated sewage is the main source of pollution in Indian rivers. Cities and towns produce a large amount of domestic wastewater every day. Treatment plants can treat only a part of it. The rest flows into rivers without treatment.

Studies by the Central Pollution Control Board show that domestic sewage forms the largest part of the pollution load.

- Industries also pollute rivers, but their share is smaller.
- Agricultural run-off brings fertilisers and pesticides, but it is a lesser source.
- Thermal power plants mainly cause air pollution and heat in water.

questions.question_md:
India has the largest Higher Education System in the World after :

(a) The United States of America
(b) Australia
(c) China
(d) United Kingdom (U.K.)

Select the **correct** answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation:
India has the third largest higher education system in the world. Only the United States of America and China have larger systems. This is true by the number of students and institutions.

- **(a) USA – yes.**
- **(c) China – yes.**
- **(b) Australia – no.** Australia has a much smaller population and fewer students.
- **(d) UK – no.** The UK system is also much smaller than India's system.

So the answer is (a) and (c) only.

questions.question_md: Prime Minister Research Fellowship is for students pursuing Ph.D programme in :
options: Central Universities, IISc, IITs, NITs, IISERs and IIITs
IISc, IITs, NITs, IISERs, IIITs, State and Central Universities
questions.explanation:
The Government of India started the Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF) in 2018. At the start, the fellows had to join a Ph.D programme in the **IITs and IISc** (Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru).

Options (2) and (3) are tempting. Students from IISERs, NITs and IIITs could apply if they met the rules. But the Ph.D itself had to be in an IIT or IISc.

Later, the government widened the list of institutions. But at the time of this exam, the answer was IITs and IISc.

questions.question_md:
Leader of the Opposition is a member of committees which select :

(a) the Central Information Commissioner
(b) the Central Vigilance Commissioner
(c) the Chairperson of National Human Rights Commission
(d) the Chairperson of National Commission for Women

Select the **correct** answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation:
The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member of several selection committees.

- **(a) Central Information Commissioner – yes.** The committee has the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister.
- **(b) Central Vigilance Commissioner – yes.** The committee has the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Leader of the Opposition.
- **(c) Chairperson of NHRC – yes.** The committee includes the Prime Minister, the Speaker and the Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses.
- **(d) Chairperson of NCW – no.** The Central Government nominates the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women. There is no such committee.

So the answer is (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements are **correct** about gender budgeting ?

(a) It is a separate budget addressing the specific needs of women.
(b) It assesses the impact of government budget on women.
(c) It is an accounting exercise.
(d) It is another budgeting innovation.

Select the **correct** answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation:
Gender budgeting is a way to look at the whole government budget from the point of view of women and gender equality.

- **(a) False.** It is not a separate budget for women. It studies the normal budget.
- **(b) True.** It assesses how government spending and taxes affect women.
- **(c) False.** It is not just an accounting exercise. It aims to change policies and the use of money.
- **(d) True.** It is a newer tool, or innovation, in budgeting. India has published a Gender Budget Statement with the Union Budget since 2005–06.

So (b) and (d) only are correct.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are the barriers to citizen-centric administration in India ?

(a) Wooden and inflexible attitude of the civil servants
(b) Ineffective implementation of laws and rules
(c) Awareness of rights and duties of citizens
(d) Lack of job opportunities for the youth

Select the **correct** answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation:
Citizen-centric administration puts the needs of citizens at the centre of government work.

- **(a) A barrier.** A rigid and wooden attitude of civil servants makes them less helpful to citizens.
- **(b) A barrier.** If laws and rules are not implemented well, citizens do not get their rights and services.
- **(c) Not a barrier.** Awareness of rights and duties helps citizens. In fact, a **lack** of awareness is the barrier.
- **(d) Not a barrier to administration.** Lack of jobs is an economic problem. It is not a problem in how the administration serves citizens.

So the answer is (a) and (b) only.

papers.instructions_note: 50 compulsory questions, 2 marks each (questions 1-50 of the combined NTA paper)

groups.md:
Read the following passage carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.

For all the disagreement in the industry about the future of aviation, there is perfect accord on one point : There is going to be a lot more of it. The world's air passengers flew a combined 7.64 trillion kilometers in 2017. By 2037, that will rise to 18.97 trillion kilometers, with about 40% of the increase happening within five intra-regional markets : China, India, North-America, Europe and South-east Asia. That is sparking a battle over the biggest bottleneck holding back this growth : airports. The governments that still own many of them should be more open to privatisation to cover a $ 78 billion funding gap in needed capital investments. Airlines, airports' biggest customers, see things differently. Costs at privatised terminals are higher and governments should be cautious about such actions in the interests of expanding the aviation sector as a whole. Privatising an airport does not necessarily make it more efficient. A study has found there was little difference between the performance of airports 100% owned by commercially-oriented government corporations and those majority controlled by private businesses. The key is instead to avoid structures where the incentives for managers are confused or misaligned, such as where private companies are brought in as minority investors or where managers are essentially bureaucrats swayed by political imperatives. There is a better solution out there, but it is not likely to be very attractive to incumbent airlines, airports, or passengers enamoured of the current generation of gleaming terminals : build more, cheaper airports.
