groups.md:
The following table presents the data on the number of vehicles of three different types (A, B and C) produced by a company during seven different years from 2012 to 2018. Based on the data in the table, answer the questions 1- 5 :

**Year – wise production of three types of vehicles**

| Year ↓ / Vehicle → | A - Type | B - Type | C - Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2012 | 5000 | 20000 | 15000 |
| 2013 | 15,000 | 10000 | 22500 |
| 2014 | 10,000 | 15000 | 30000 |
| 2015 | 17,500 | 15000 | 23000 |
| 2016 | 25,000 | 20,000 | 15000 |
| 2017 | 13,000 | 25,000 | 20000 |
| 2018 | 30,000 | 35,000 | 25000 |

Read the following passage and answer questions which follow.

Eventhough globalisation is one of the most discussed topics in the contemporary world, it is not altogether a well defined concept. A multitude of global interactions are put under the broad heading of globalisation, varying from the expansion of cultural and scientific influences across borders to the enlargement of economic and business relations throughout the world. A wholesale rejection of globalisation would not only go against global business, it would also cut out movements of ideas, understanding, and knowledge that can help all the people of the world, including the most disadvantaged members of the world population. A comprehensive rejection of globalisation can thus be powerfully counterproductive. There is a strong need to separate out the different questions that appear merged together in the rhetoric of the antiglobalisation protests. The globalisation of knowledge deserves a particularly high profile recognition, despite all the good things that can be rightly said about the importance of "Local knowledge".

Globalisation is often seen, both in journalistic discussions and in remarkably many academic writings, as a process of westernization. Indeed, some who take an upbeat view of the phenomenon even sees it as a contribution of Western civilization to the world.

questions.question_md: By what percentage did the production of B-type vehicles increase from 2016 to 2017?
questions.notes: Translated from the Hindi version (no English in source). The English version of this question in the source shows only the data table (no question text); the question is taken from the Hindi version. Cancelled by NTA in the final answer key (marks awarded to all).
questions.explanation:
Read the B-type column of the table.

- 2016: 20,000 vehicles.
- 2017: 25,000 vehicles.
- Increase = 25,000 − 20,000 = 5,000.
- Percentage increase = 5,000 ÷ 20,000 × 100 = **25%**.

The other values come from common mistakes. For example, 20% is 5,000 ÷ 25,000, which uses the wrong base. Always divide by the old value (2016).

NTA dropped this question and gave marks to all candidates. The likely reason is a printing error. The English version showed only the data table and no question text. Only the Hindi version had the question.

questions.question_md: The number of A – type vehicles produced in the year 2014 was what percent (%) of the number of C-type vehicles produced in the year 2016?
questions.explanation:
Take the two values from the table.

- A-type vehicles in 2014: 10,000.
- C-type vehicles in 2016: 15,000.

Percentage = 10,000 ÷ 15,000 × 100 = 2/3 × 100 ≈ **66.67%**.

The trap is to divide the other way round. 15,000 ÷ 10,000 gives 150%, which is not an option. 33.33% is the remaining part (100% − 66.67%), not the answer.

questions.question_md: In how many years was the production of A – type vehicles less than its average production over the given years?
questions.explanation:
First find the average production of A-type vehicles.

- Values: 5,000; 15,000; 10,000; 17,500; 25,000; 13,000; 30,000.
- Sum = 1,15,500.
- Average = 1,15,500 ÷ 7 = **16,500**.

Now count the years with production below 16,500:

- 2012 (5,000), 2013 (15,000), 2014 (10,000) and 2017 (13,000).

That is **4 years**. The years 2015 (17,500), 2016 (25,000) and 2018 (30,000) are above the average.

questions.question_md: What was the average number of B – type vehicles produced by the company over the years?
questions.explanation:
Add the B-type values for all seven years.

- 20,000 + 10,000 + 15,000 + 15,000 + 20,000 + 25,000 + 35,000 = 1,40,000.

Average = 1,40,000 ÷ 7 = **20,000**.

The other options are single values from the table (15,000, 25,000) or a guess (30,000). They are not the average of all seven years.

questions.question_md: In which of the following years was the total production of all the three types of vehicles 60000?
By selling 70 pencils for Rs.90/- a person makes a loss of 25%. How many pencils should be sold for Rs.234 to have a profit of 30%?
questions.explanation:
First find the cost price (CP).

- 70 pencils sell for Rs. 90 at a loss of 25%.
- So Rs. 90 is 75% of the CP. CP of 70 pencils = 90 ÷ 0.75 = Rs. 120.
- CP of one pencil = 120 ÷ 70 = Rs. 12/7.

Now find the selling price (SP) for a 30% profit.

- SP of one pencil = 12/7 × 1.3 = Rs. 15.6/7.
- Number of pencils for Rs. 234 = 234 ÷ (15.6/7) = 234 × 7 ÷ 15.6 = **105**.

Check: CP of 105 pencils = 105 × 12/7 = Rs. 180. Then 180 × 1.3 = Rs. 234. This is correct.

questions.question_md: In what ratio must a vendor mix two varieties of sugar worth Rs.60 per kg and Rs.78 per kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs.76.8 per kg, the vendor gains 20%?
questions.explanation:
First find the cost price of the mixture.

- The vendor sells at Rs. 76.8 per kg and gains 20%.
- Cost price = 76.8 ÷ 1.2 = **Rs. 64 per kg**.

Now use the rule of alligation (a quick method to find the mixing ratio).

- Cheap sugar (Rs. 60): its share = 78 − 64 = 14.
- Dear sugar (Rs. 78): its share = 64 − 60 = 4.
- Ratio = 14 : 4 = **7 : 2**.

Check: (7 × 60 + 2 × 78) ÷ 9 = (420 + 156) ÷ 9 = 576 ÷ 9 = 64. This is correct.

A common mistake is to use Rs. 76.8 as the cost price. Remember to remove the 20% profit first.

questions.question_md:
Which given of the following sets of letters when sequentially placed at the gaps in the letter series below shall complete it?

bb \_\_\_ b \_\_\_ ab \_\_\_ cbba \_\_\_ bcbb \_\_\_
questions.explanation:
Put the letters c, b, b, b, a into the five gaps in order.

- bb **c** b **b** ab **b** cbba **b** bcbb **a**

The full series is: bbcbba bbcbba bbcbba.

The block "bbcbba" repeats three times. So this set completes the series.

Test the other sets in the same way. They do not give a repeating block. For example, "a c b a c" gives "bbabcab…", which does not repeat.

questions.question_md: Out of a total of 10 students, the average weight of 9 students is 60 kg. If the weight of the 10ᵗʰ student is 9 kg more than the average weight of all the 10 students, then the weight of the 10ᵗʰ student would be :
questions.explanation:
Let the average weight of all 10 students be x kg.

- The 9 students weigh 9 × 60 = 540 kg in total.
- The 10th student weighs (x + 9) kg.
- Total weight of 10 students = 10x.

So 10x = 540 + x + 9.
Then 9x = 549, and x = 61 kg.

Weight of the 10th student = 61 + 9 = **70 kg**.

The option 61 kg is the new average, not the weight of the 10th student. The option 69 kg comes from adding 9 to the old average of 60.

questions.question_md: Which of the following was not a Millennium Development Goal (MDG)?
options: Ensure healthy lives and promote well being for all at all ages
questions.explanation:
The UN set eight Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) for the period 2000–2015. They included:

- eradicate extreme poverty and hunger,
- achieve universal primary education,
- promote gender equality,
- reduce child mortality,
- **improve maternal health**,
- combat HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases,
- **ensure environmental sustainability**,
- develop a global partnership for development.

"Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages" is not an MDG. It is Goal 3 of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The SDGs replaced the MDGs in 2015 and run to 2030.

questions.question_md: Choose the person who has control over self, mode of communication and method of delivery in class room from the following :
questions.explanation:
In a classroom, the **teacher** is the source of the message. The teacher controls his or her own behaviour (self). The teacher also chooses how to communicate, for example speech, board or slides. The teacher also decides the method of delivery, for example lecture or discussion.

The students are the receivers. They respond to the message, but they do not plan how the lesson is delivered. "Audience" and "visitor" are also receivers, not the person in control.

questions.question_md: Select the period in which India became a centre of higher learning.
questions.explanation:
The Gupta period (about 4th to 6th century CE) is often called the "Golden Age" of ancient India. In this period, the university of **Nalanda** was founded, under Kumaragupta I. Students came to Nalanda from China, Korea, Tibet and other countries. So India became a centre of higher learning for the world.

Learning also grew in other periods. Takshashila (Taxila) was famous before the Guptas. But the examiner links large, organised centres of higher learning with the Gupta age.

In the Mughal and British periods, India had schools and colleges. However, India was not the main world centre of higher learning in those periods.

questions.question_md: Which of the following groups has the components of paralanguage communication?
questions.explanation:
**Paralanguage** means the non-word parts of the voice. It is about *how* a person says something, not *what* the person says.

Its main components are:

- **voice** qualities, such as pitch, tone, volume and speed,
- **emphasis** (stress on some words),
- the **impression** that the voice creates in the listener.

The other options contain "social space" or "expression".

- Social space is about the distance between people. Its study is called proxemics.
- Facial expression is a part of body language (kinesics).

Both are non-verbal communication, but they are not paralanguage.

questions.question_md: How many National Parks and Wildlife Sancturies were there in India till March 2011?
questions.explanation:
Official data of the Ministry of Environment and Forests for March 2011 gave these numbers:

- **102** National Parks,
- **515** Wildlife Sanctuaries.

These two numbers formed the main Protected Area network of India at that time.

The other pairs do not match these official figures. Since 2011, the numbers have grown, because the government has declared new protected areas.

questions.question_md: Which one of the following is signified by Udāharana of Anumāna (Inference) in Indian Logic?
options: Universal proposition along with an instance
questions.explanation:
In Nyāya logic, an Anumāna (inference) for others has five parts (avayava):

- **Pratijñā**: the proposition to be proved. "The hill has fire."
- **Hetu**: the reason. "Because it has smoke."
- **Udāharaṇa**: the example. "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen."
- **Upanaya**: the application. "The hill has smoke of this kind."
- **Nigamana**: the conclusion. "So the hill has fire."

The Udāharaṇa states the universal rule (vyāpti, the fixed link between smoke and fire). It also gives an instance, the kitchen. So it is a universal proposition along with an instance.

The other options describe Hetu, Pratijñā and Nigamana.

questions.question_md:
Devdatta is fat and he does not eat during the day. Therefore, Devadatta is eating during the night.

The above example, in classical Indian School of Logic, is a case of :
questions.explanation:
This is the standard example of **Arthāpatti** (implication or postulation). The Mīmāṃsā school accepts it as a separate pramāṇa (source of valid knowledge).

Two facts seem to conflict. Devadatta is fat, but he does not eat in the day. The only way to explain both facts is to assume that he eats at night. Arthāpatti is this assumption of a missing fact.

- **Perception** does not work, because nobody sees him eat at night.
- **Comparison** (Upamāna) gives knowledge from similarity. There is no similarity here.
- **Verbal testimony** (Śabda) comes from a reliable person's words. Nobody tells us the fact here.

questions.question_md: As per the classical square of opposition, if 'A' proposition is given as true, then which one of the following is correct?
options: "E" proposition is false, "I" proposition is true and "O" proposition is false
"E" proposition is true, "I" proposition is true and "O" proposition is true
"E" proposition is false, "I" proposition is false and "O" proposition is true
"E" proposition is true, "I" proposition is false and "O" proposition is false
questions.explanation:
In the square of opposition, the four forms are:

- A: All S are P.
- E: No S are P.
- I: Some S are P.
- O: Some S are not P.

If A is true:

- **E is false**. A and E are contraries, so they cannot both be true.
- **I is true**. I is the subaltern of A. If "all" is true, "some" is also true.
- **O is false**. A and O are contradictories, so they always have opposite truth values.

So E is false, I is true and O is false. The other options make E true or O true. This is not possible when A is true.

questions.question_md: Which one of the following propositions is a contrary to "All poets are dreamers"?
questions.explanation:
Contrary propositions are an A and an E proposition with the **same subject and the same predicate**. They cannot both be true, but they can both be false.

- The A proposition is "All poets are dreamers".
- Its contrary E proposition is "**No poets are dreamers**".

The other options:

- "Some poets are dreamers" is the I form. It is the subaltern of A.
- "Some poets are not dreamers" is the O form. It is the contradictory of A.
- "No dreamers are poets" means the same thing as the E form. But it changes the order of subject and predicate. So in the strict square of opposition, it is not the contrary of the given proposition.

questions.question_md: Which among the following is NOT a component of effective teaching?
options: Questioning to check for the understanding of students
Being flexible about how long it takes to learn
questions.explanation:
Effective teaching needs a **proactive** teacher. Such a teacher plans ahead and prevents problems before they start. A "reactive" teacher only responds after students behave in some way. So a reactive mode is not a component of effective teaching.

The other options are good teaching practices:

- **Questioning** checks if students understand the lesson.
- **Feedback** tells students what they did well and what to improve.
- **Flexibility about time** accepts that students learn at different speeds. This idea comes from mastery learning.

questions.question_md: Which among the following factors doesn't contribute to assessment bias?
options: When language of the test and the tester is different from the languages of the students
Answers that support middle – class values
If assessment procedures are flexible and diverse to make disadvantaged students comfortable
Objective test for assessing abstract reasoning of the student.
questions.explanation:
**Assessment bias** happens when a test is unfair to some groups of students. These students then get lower marks for reasons not linked to their real ability.

Factors that **cause** bias:

- The language of the test or tester is different from the students' language.
- The test rewards answers that support middle-class values.
- An objective test of abstract reasoning can favour students from some backgrounds.

**Flexible and diverse** assessment procedures do the opposite. They help disadvantaged students to show what they know. So they reduce bias and do not add to it.

questions.question_md: Which among the following is NOT related to qualitative research?
questions.explanation:
**Qualitative research** studies meanings, experiences and words. It uses small samples and deep study.

- **Thematic analysis** finds themes (repeated ideas) in interview or text data. It is qualitative.
- **Case study** studies one case in depth. It is mostly qualitative.
- **Discourse analysis** studies how language builds meaning. It is qualitative.

The **survey method** usually collects data with structured questionnaires from large samples. The data is turned into numbers and analysed with statistics. So it belongs mainly to quantitative research.

questions.question_md: In Social Sciences, a central issue is the question of whether the social world can be studied using the methods of natural sciences. This statement refers to the issue of :
questions.explanation:
**Epistemology** is the study of knowledge. It asks: what counts as acceptable knowledge in a field?

The question of whether we can study the social world with the methods of natural science is an epistemological issue. Two positions answer it:

- **Positivism** says yes. Social science can use the methods of natural science.
- **Interpretivism** says no. Human action has meaning, so it needs different methods.

The other options:

- **Ontology** asks about the nature of social reality itself.
- **Axiology** is the study of values.
- **Etymology** is the study of the origin of words.

questions.question_md: Which among the following is not the outcome of grounded theory research?
questions.explanation:
**Grounded theory** builds theory from data. The researcher collects and codes data, and the ideas grow from the data step by step.

The main outcomes of grounded theory are:

- **concepts** (labels for things in the data),
- **categories** (groups of concepts),
- properties of categories,
- **hypotheses** (relations between categories),
- substantive and formal theory.

A **narrative** is a story told by a person. Narrative analysis is a different qualitative method. It is not an outcome of grounded theory.

questions.question_md:
Identify the factors that do not contribute to the effectiveness of teaching from the options given below :

(a) Socio – economic background of Teacher

(b) Teacher's skill in pleasing the students

(c) Teacher's subject knowledge

(d) Teacher's personal contact with students

Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation:
The question asks for factors that do **not** help teaching to be effective.

- (a) **Socio-economic background of the teacher**: does not contribute. A teacher's family income or class does not make teaching better.
- (b) **Skill in pleasing students**: does not contribute. Pleasing students is not the same as helping them learn.
- (c) **Subject knowledge**: contributes. A teacher must know the subject well.
- (d) **Personal contact with students**: the examiner treats this as not contributing. Private personal contact is not a part of good classroom teaching. Good rapport in class is useful, but this item means personal ties.

So (a), (b) and (d) are the answer. Any option with (c) is wrong, because subject knowledge is a key factor.

questions.question_md:
Select the alternative features from the following, which make open universities as non-traditional universities :

(a) Innovative method of teaching and learning

(b) Innovative method of admission, curriculum and evaluation

(c) Modern communication techniques

(d) Teacher's friendly approaches

Select the correct option :
questions.explanation:
An open university is "non-traditional" because it works in new ways.

- (a) **Innovative methods of teaching and learning**: yes. It uses self-learning material and distance study.
- (b) **Innovative admission, curriculum and evaluation**: yes. Admission is open and flexible, with few entry conditions.
- (c) **Modern communication techniques**: yes. It uses radio, TV, internet and other media.
- (d) **Teacher-friendly approach**: no. An open university is learner-centred, not teacher-centred. A friendly teacher is also common in traditional universities.

So (a), (b) and (c) are the features. Options with (d) are wrong.

questions.question_md:
Regarding E-governance, which of the following statements is / are correct?

(a) Decreasing transparency is an ICT enabled advantage of E-Governance.

(b) E-governance is related to the implementation of ICT in the government processes and functions.

(c) Common Service Centres (CSCs) help in providing and using E-Governance related services.

Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation:
E-governance means the use of ICT (information and communication technology) in government work.

- (a) **False.** E-governance **increases** transparency. People can see information and track their requests online.
- (b) **True.** E-governance applies ICT to government processes and functions.
- (c) **True.** Common Service Centres (CSCs) are local access points. People in villages use them to get e-governance services.

So only (b) and (c) are correct. Any option with (a) is wrong.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements is / are correct?

(a) Software is loaded into secondary storage from RAM and is then executed by the CPU.

(b) A search engine is a software system that is designed to search for information on the www.

Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation:
- (a) **False.** The direction is wrong. Software is stored in secondary storage, such as a hard disk. To run it, the computer loads it **from secondary storage into RAM**. Then the CPU executes it.
- (b) **True.** A search engine is a software system. It searches for information on the World Wide Web. Google and Bing are examples.

So only (b) is correct.

questions.question_md:
Given below is a question followed by three statements. Identify the statements that are necessary to answer the question.

**Question :** What is the percentage profit gained by a vendor when he sells an article?

**Statements :**

(a) He gives a 10% discount on the marked price.

(b) He would have earned 25% profit if he did not give any discount.

(c) The cost price of the article is Rs.8000.

Choose the correct option from those given below :
questions.explanation:
Let the marked price (MP) be M.

- From (a): selling price (SP) = 90% of M = 0.9M.
- From (b): with no discount, SP would be M and the profit would be 25%. So M = 1.25 × cost price (CP). Then CP = M ÷ 1.25 = 0.8M.

Profit = 0.9M − 0.8M = 0.1M.
Profit % = 0.1M ÷ 0.8M × 100 = **12.5%**.

We found the answer with (a) and (b) only. The value of M does not matter, because it cancels out. So statement (c), the cost price of Rs. 8000, is not necessary.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements are true about a fuel cell?

(a) It is a device that uses electrochemical reactions to produce electric current

(b) It consists of a positive electrode and a negative electrode separated by an electrolyte

(c) Just like batteries it needs to be recharged with an electric current

Choose the correct option from those given below :
questions.explanation:
A fuel cell makes electricity from a chemical reaction. A common example uses hydrogen and oxygen.

- (a) **True.** It uses electrochemical reactions to produce electric current.
- (b) **True.** It has two electrodes, the anode (negative) and the cathode (positive). An electrolyte separates them.
- (c) **False.** A fuel cell does not need recharging with electric current. It keeps working as long as fuel and oxygen flow into it. A rechargeable battery is different, because it stores a fixed amount of energy.

So only (a) and (b) are true.

questions.question_md:
Consider the following statements with reference to the proposition "Some girls are not students"

(a) Subject term students is distributed

(b) Predicate term girls is undistributed

(c) Predicate term students is distributed

(d) Subject term girls is undistributed

Choose the correct option from those given below:
questions.explanation:
"Some girls are not students" is an **O proposition** (particular negative).

- The subject is "girls". The predicate is "students".
- In an O proposition, the subject is **undistributed**. The statement does not speak about all girls.
- The predicate is **distributed**. The statement excludes the girls from the whole class of students.

Check each statement:

- (a) **Wrong.** "Students" is the predicate, not the subject.
- (b) **Wrong.** "Girls" is the subject, not the predicate.
- (c) **Correct.** The predicate "students" is distributed.
- (d) **Correct.** The subject "girls" is undistributed.

So only (c) and (d) are correct.

questions.question_md:
Choose two factors that do NOT affect the academic performance of students adversely :

(a) Low self – efficacy belief

(b) Belief in God

(c) Indifferent attitude towards politics

(d) Teacher's low expectation from students

Choose the correct option :
questions.notes: The Hindi version asks for factors that DO adversely affect academic performance (no 'NOT').
questions.explanation:
The question asks for factors that do **not** harm academic performance.

- (a) **Low self-efficacy belief**: harms performance. Self-efficacy is a student's belief in his or her own ability. Low belief reduces effort.
- (b) **Belief in God**: does not harm performance. It is a personal faith and is not linked to poor results.
- (c) **Indifferent attitude towards politics**: does not harm performance. Lack of interest in politics has no direct effect on study.
- (d) **Teacher's low expectation**: harms performance. Students often perform at the level the teacher expects. This is called the Pygmalion effect.

So (b) and (c) are the answer. The Hindi version of the paper asks the opposite, but no option has (a) and (d). So the English reading fits the key.

questions.question_md:
Which of the two statements from the following statements are correct?

(a) Sampling – related error is subsumed under the category non-sampling error

(b) Sampling error doesn't occur in multi-stage cluster sampling

(c) Inaccurate sampling frame and non-response are examples of sampling – related error.

(d) There is an inverse relation between heterogeneity of population and sampling error.

Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation:
These statements use the error types from Bryman's book on social research.

- (a) **Correct.** Non-sampling error is a broad category. It includes sampling-related error, data collection error and data processing error.
- (b) **Wrong.** Sampling error can occur in any probability sample. In multi-stage cluster sampling, it is often larger than in a simple random sample.
- (c) **Correct.** An inaccurate sampling frame (the list from which the sample is drawn) is a sampling-related error. Non-response is another one.
- (d) **Wrong.** The relation is direct, not inverse. A more heterogeneous (varied) population gives a larger sampling error.

So (a) and (c) are correct.

questions.question_md:
Match the following historic places with their distinguishing discipline of learning

| List I (Historic places) | List II (Discipline) |
|---|---|
| (a) Takshila | (i) Astronomy |
| (b) Ujjain | (ii) Buddhism |
| (c) Sarnath | (iii) Art, Architecture and Painting |
| (d) Ajanta | (iv) Medicine |

Choose the correct option from those given below :
questions.explanation:
Each ancient place was famous for one field of learning.

- (a) **Takshila – Medicine (iv).** Takshashila was famous for medicine. Jivaka, the physician of the Buddha's time, studied there.
- (b) **Ujjain – Astronomy (i).** Ujjain was a major centre of astronomy. Indian astronomers used it as the prime meridian (zero longitude line).
- (c) **Sarnath – Buddhism (ii).** The Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath.
- (d) **Ajanta – Art, architecture and painting (iii).** The Ajanta caves have famous rock-cut halls and wall paintings.

Only option (4) has all four pairs right.

questions.question_md:
Match the following soil orders with their descriptions

| Soil order | Description |
|---|---|
| (a) Histosols | (i) Soil order that includes soils formed on volcanic ash |
| (b) Andisols | (ii) Soil order of cold regions including soils underlain by permafrost |
| (c) Gelisols | (iii) Soil order consisting of soils of dry climates |
| (d) Aridsols | (iv) Soil order consisting of soils with a thick upper layer of organic matter. |

Choose the correct option from those given below :
questions.notes: The source gives no column headings for the two lists.
questions.explanation:
These are soil orders in the USDA Soil Taxonomy (the US system for naming soils).

- (a) **Histosols – (iv)** thick upper layer of organic matter. "Histos" means tissue. These are peat and bog soils.
- (b) **Andisols – (i)** soils formed on volcanic ash. The name comes from "andesite", a volcanic rock.
- (c) **Gelisols – (ii)** soils of cold regions with permafrost (ground that stays frozen). "Gelare" means to freeze.
- (d) **Aridisols – (iii)** soils of dry climates. "Aridus" means dry.

Only option (1) has all four pairs right.

questions.question_md:
Match List – I with List - II

| List I (Digital Initative) | List II (Purpose) |
|---|---|
| (a) UMANG | (i) G2B Services |
| (b) BHIM | (ii) Learning platform |
| (c) eBiz | (iii) Unified payment interface |
| (d) SWAYAM | (iv) Single point of access to all government services. |

Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation:
- (a) **UMANG – (iv).** UMANG means Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance. It is one app for many government services.
- (b) **BHIM – (iii).** BHIM is a payment app based on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).
- (c) **eBiz – (i).** eBiz is a portal for G2B (government-to-business) services, such as licences for businesses.
- (d) **SWAYAM – (ii).** SWAYAM is the national platform for online courses (MOOCs).

Only option (3) has all four pairs right.

questions.question_md:
Match correctly the items of Column I with the items of column II

| Column I | Column II |
|---|---|
| (a) Ontology | (i) Ideographic |
| (b) Epistemology | (ii) Realism |
| (c) Methodolgy | (iii) Survey |
| (d) Method | (iv) Positivism |

Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation:
Research has four levels. Each level has a typical example.

- (a) **Ontology – Realism (ii).** Ontology asks what reality is. Realism says reality exists apart from our minds.
- (b) **Epistemology – Positivism (iv).** Epistemology asks how we know. Positivism says we know through observation and the methods of science.
- (c) **Methodology – Ideographic (i).** Methodology is the overall strategy of research. An ideographic (idiographic) approach studies unique cases in depth.
- (d) **Method – Survey (iii).** A method is a tool to collect data. A survey is such a tool.

Only option (4) has all four pairs right.

questions.question_md: Select the advantage of feedback in the process of communication, from the following :
options: It is beneficial in understanding of the subject matter
It diagnoses the defects in receiver
It explores the defects in receiver
questions.explanation:
**Feedback** is the response of the receiver to the sender. It shows the sender how the receiver understood the message. If there is a mistake, the sender can correct it. So feedback **clarifies** the communication and makes it a two-way process.

The other options are weaker:

- Better understanding of the subject can follow from feedback, but it is not the main purpose of feedback in communication.
- Feedback does not aim to find "defects in the receiver". It checks the success of the whole message, not the faults of one person.

questions.question_md:
Match the following values with their distinguishing functions :

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| (a) Sacrifice | (i) Working in a stipulated time |
| (b) Sincerity | (ii) Confinement of individual mind on action |
| (c) Self control | (iii) Showing love and affection |
| (d) Altruism | (iv) Helping without selfish motives |

Choose the correct option from those given below :
questions.explanation:
Start with the clear pairs.

- (b) **Sincerity – (i)** working in a stipulated time. A sincere person does the work on time and with care.
- (c) **Self-control – (ii)** confinement of the mind on action. Self-control keeps the mind on the task.

Only option (2) has both (b)-(i) and (c)-(ii). So it is the answer. It also gives:

- (a) **Sacrifice – (iv)** helping without selfish motives. A person gives up his or her own gain to help others.
- (d) **Altruism – (iii)** showing love and affection. Altruism means care and concern for others.

Pairs (a) and (d) are close in meaning. However, the elimination with (b) and (c) leaves only one option.

questions.question_md: Select the option that lists components for a cyberspace address (URL) in the correct order from beginning to end?
options: Protocol, domain name of the host, path / file
Path / file, protocol, domain name of the host
Protocol, path /file, domain name of the host
Domain name of the host, protocol, path / file
questions.explanation:
A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a resource on the web. Its parts come in this order:

1. **Protocol**, such as https://
2. **Domain name of the host**, such as www.ugc.gov.in
3. **Path / file**, such as /page/index.html

Example: https://www.ugc.gov.in/page/index.html

The protocol always comes first. The path always comes after the domain name. The other options break this order.

questions.question_md: Which of the following sequence represents the correct order of soil particles arranged in terms of particle size from the smallest to the largest?
questions.explanation:
Soil particles are grouped by size. The usual limits (USDA system) are:

- **Clay**: smaller than 0.002 mm.
- **Silt**: 0.002 mm to 0.05 mm.
- **Sand**: 0.05 mm to 2 mm.
- **Gravel**: larger than 2 mm.

So the order from smallest to largest is **clay, silt, sand, gravel**.

A common mistake is to put silt before clay. Clay particles are the finest of all. Gravel is the coarsest.

questions.question_md: Arrange the steps of research in the sequence in which they are presented in the thesis
options: Discussion, Review of Literature, Results, Conceptual Framework, Problem
Review of Literature, Problem, Conceptual Framework, Result, Discussion
Problem, Review of Literature, Conceptual Framework, Results, Discussion
Problem, Review of Literature, Conceptual Framework, Results, Discussion
questions.notes: Options (3) and (4) are identical in the source; NTA's key accepts both.
questions.explanation:
A thesis follows the order in which research is done.

1. **Problem**: state the research problem first.
2. **Review of literature**: study what earlier work says about the problem.
3. **Conceptual framework**: build the framework of concepts and variables from the review.
4. **Results**: report the findings after collecting and analysing data.
5. **Discussion**: explain what the results mean and link them to earlier work.

Options (3) and (4) give exactly the same order in the source paper. This was a printing error. So NTA's key accepts both options.

The other options are wrong. One starts with discussion, and the other puts the review of literature before the problem.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements - one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other is labeled as Reason (R):

**Assertion (A) :** Through on-line teaching a large number of students can be taught by very competent faculty.

**Reason (R) :** On-line teaching helps students in developing critical thinking more than the Off –line teaching can do.

In the light of the above two statements choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** Online teaching can reach very many students at the same time. So one competent teacher can teach a large number of learners. MOOCs on SWAYAM are an example.
- **(R) is false.** There is no proof that online teaching builds critical thinking **more** than classroom teaching. Critical thinking grows through discussion, debate and close guidance. These are often easier in a face-to-face class.

So (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements - one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other is labeled as Reason (R):

**Assertion (A) :** A blog is a form of social media.

**Reason (R) :** A blog allows anyone to communicate to a public audience.

In the light of the above two statements, choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are ture and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** A blog is a website where a person posts articles. Readers can comment and share the posts. So a blog is a form of social media.
- **(R) is true.** Anyone can create a blog and publish to a public audience. No editor or publisher needs to approve the post.
- **(R) explains (A).** Social media lets users create content and share it with the public. A blog does exactly this. So (R) gives the reason why a blog is social media.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements - one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other is labeled as Reason (R):

**Assertion (A) :** Skill development is a key feature in every individual's life.

**Reason (R) :** An individual who wants to get employed, needs to possess good education only.

In the context of above two statements, choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** Skills help a person to get a job, to work well and to grow in life. India's Skill India mission is based on this idea.
- **(R) is false.** The word "only" makes it wrong. Good education alone is not enough to get a job. Employers also want practical, technical and soft skills, such as communication and teamwork.

So (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements - one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other is labeled as Reason (R):

**Assertion (A) :** Government of India established higher educational statutory bodies to ensure quality of education.

**Reason (R) :** There are some educational institutions in India which do not provide quality education.

In the context of above two statements, choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is true.** The Government of India set up statutory bodies by Acts of Parliament. Examples are the UGC (University Grants Commission) and the AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education). They set standards and check the quality of higher education.
- **(R) is true.** Some institutions in India do not give good quality education.
- **(R) explains (A).** Quality is uneven across institutions. This is why the government needs bodies that set and keep standards.

So both are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_md: According to the passage, which one of the following is not a well defined concept?
questions.explanation:
The passage opens with this idea. It says that globalisation is much discussed, but "it is not altogether a well defined concept". It then explains why. Many different kinds of global interactions are put under this one heading.

The other options:

- **Multiculturalism** and **identity** do not appear in the passage.
- **Local knowledge** appears, but the passage does not say that it is badly defined. It says that local knowledge is important.

questions.question_md: According to the passage, which one of the following is counter productive?
options: Comprehensive rejection of anti – globalisation protests
questions.explanation:
The passage says: "A comprehensive rejection of globalisation can thus be powerfully counterproductive." Just before this, it uses the words "wholesale rejection of globalisation". Both phrases mean the same thing: rejecting globalisation completely.

The other options:

- The author does not call **support** for globalisation counterproductive.
- The passage does not ask us to reject the anti-globalisation protests completely. It asks us to separate the different questions in them.
- The passage values **local knowledge**. It does not say that recognising it is harmful.

questions.question_md: According to the passage, globalisation is perceived often by media and academia as :
options: A process of facilitating global bussiness
questions.explanation:
The second paragraph says that globalisation is often seen "as a process of westernization". It says that this view appears in journalistic discussions and in many academic writings. Journalistic discussions are the media. Academic writings come from academia. So the answer is **a process of westernisation**.

The other options:

- The passage does not say that media or academia see globalisation as supporting or harming local knowledge.
- Global business is one part of globalisation. But the passage does not say that media and academia see it in this way.

questions.question_md: The attempt of the author in the passage is :
options: Unconditioned rejection of local knowledge systems
questions.explanation:
The author does not take one side completely.

- The author says that a wholesale rejection of globalisation is counterproductive. So the author is not against it.
- The author also wants to "separate out the different questions" in the debate. So the author does not support it without conditions either.
- The author praises the globalisation of knowledge, but also respects local knowledge.

This is a balanced approach. So the attempt is an **unbiased evaluation of globalisation**.

The "unconditioned" options are wrong. The author places conditions and makes distinctions throughout the passage.

questions.question_md:
As per the passage, a wholesale rejection of globalisation would result in affecting

(a) Global businesses

(b) Movement of Ideas

(c) Local knowledge systems

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The passage says that a wholesale rejection of globalisation "would not only go against global business". It adds that it "would also cut out movements of ideas, understanding, and knowledge".

- (a) **Global businesses**: yes, the passage names this.
- (b) **Movement of ideas**: yes, the passage names this.
- (c) **Local knowledge systems**: no. The passage mentions local knowledge in another sentence. It does not say that rejection of globalisation would affect it.

So only (a) and (b) are correct.
