Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Municipal solid waste includes Garbage and Rubbish.

**Statement II :** Garbage consists of both combustible and non combustible materials.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** Municipal solid waste (MSW) is the waste from homes, shops and offices in a town. It includes garbage, rubbish, ashes and other waste.
- **Statement II is false.** **Garbage** is the putrescible part of waste. It is food and kitchen waste that rots. **Rubbish** is the non-putrescible part. Rubbish has combustible items (paper, wood, cloth) and non-combustible items (glass, metal, tins).

Statement II describes rubbish, not garbage. So Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** In many cases, both organisms and human infrastructure will not be able to move or adapt quickly enough to changing climate.

**Statement II :** Infectious diseases are likely to increase as a result of global warming.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** Climate is changing fast. Many plants and animals cannot move to new areas or adapt quickly enough. Roads, buildings, ports and water systems were built for the old climate. They also cannot change fast.
- **Statement II is true.** Warmer temperatures help mosquitoes and other disease carriers spread to new areas. So diseases like malaria and dengue are likely to increase. Floods also help water-borne diseases spread.

Both statements are true.

questions.question_md: Major contributor to carbon monoxide emissions in metropolitan areas of India is/are:
questions.explanation:
Carbon monoxide (CO) forms when fuel burns without enough oxygen (incomplete combustion).

In Indian metro cities, the main source of CO is the **transport sector**. Cars, two-wheelers, buses and trucks burn petrol and diesel. Traffic jams and slow driving increase incomplete burning.

- Industry is a major source of sulphur dioxide and particulate matter. Most large industry is outside the city centre.
- Domestic sources (cooking fuel) are important in rural areas. In metros, most homes use LPG, which burns cleanly.
- Agriculture adds CO mainly through crop burning in rural areas.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

**Assertion A :** Although internal-combustion engines used in today's vehicles can be adapted to burn hydrogen, hydrogen powered combustion engines probably are not the future of hydrogen fuelled vehicles.

**Reason R :** It is more efficient to convert hydrogen energy directly to electricity using fuel cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Assertion A is true.** Engineers can adapt internal-combustion engines to burn hydrogen. But experts expect future hydrogen vehicles to use fuel cells instead.
- **Reason R is true.** A fuel cell converts the chemical energy of hydrogen directly into electricity. An engine first makes heat and then motion. A lot of energy is lost as heat. So the fuel cell is more efficient.

R explains A. Hydrogen combustion engines are probably not the future *because* fuel cells use hydrogen more efficiently. So both are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_md:
While planning for higher education development in India in the twenty first century, the guiding principles should be :

A. Access

B. Empathy

C. Equity

D. Accountability

E. Quality

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Higher education planning in India rests on a few main principles. NEP 2020 calls them the foundational pillars: **Access, Equity, Quality, Affordability and Accountability**.

- **A. Access** – yes.
- **B. Empathy** – a good personal value, but not a planning principle. No.
- **C. Equity** – yes.
- **D. Accountability** – yes.
- **E. Quality** – yes.

So the answer is A, C, D and E only. Every other option includes Empathy.

questions.question_md: Which of the following ancient systems is focussed on laws of matter and force and of combination and disintegration?
questions.explanation:
**Vaiśeṣika** is one of the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy. Kaṇāda founded it. It teaches that all matter is made of eternal atoms (paramāṇu). Atoms combine to form objects, and objects break down into atoms. So it deals with the laws of matter, force, combination and disintegration.

- **Nirukta** is the study of the origin and meaning of words (etymology). It is a Vedāṅga.
- **Chhanda** is the study of Vedic metre. It is also a Vedāṅga.
- **Gṛhya Sūtras** give rules for household rituals.

questions.question_md: According to NEP 2020, what percentage of learners of schools and higher education system shall have exposure to vocational education by 2025.
questions.explanation:
NEP 2020 (National Education Policy) wants to bring vocational education into the main system. The policy sets a clear target. By **2025**, at least **50% of learners** in school and higher education should have exposure to vocational education.

The other figures (40%, 35% and 30%) do not appear as this target in NEP 2020.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are the characteristics of non-conventional learning ?

A. No fixed curriculum

B. Teacher-centred learning

C. Cost-effective

D. Require regular attendance

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Non-conventional learning includes open learning, distance learning and online learning. It is flexible.

- **A. No fixed curriculum** – learners can choose courses and pace. Yes.
- **B. Teacher-centred learning** – this is a feature of conventional classrooms. Non-conventional learning is learner-centred. No.
- **C. Cost-effective** – one course can reach many learners at low cost. Yes.
- **D. Require regular attendance** – this is a feature of conventional schools and colleges. No.

So the answer is A and C only.

questions.question_md: The Sanskrit-Sahitya parishat whose aim and objectives are to disseminate Sanskrit learning and research in different branches of indological studies and to store and maintain the ancient Indian cultural and glories of India was established in the year :
questions.explanation:
The **Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat** in Kolkata was established in **1916**. Its first name was Vangiya Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat. It spreads Sanskrit learning and supports research in Indology (the study of Indian history, culture and texts). It also keeps manuscripts and books on ancient Indian culture.

The question repeats the aims from the institution's own description. The other years (1906, 1961 and 1964) are distractors. The years 1961 and 1916 use the same digits, so read them with care.

questions.question_md: What has been done to describe the role of online tutors?
options: Provide them with a warning system
Clarify their duties in fields other than education
questions.explanation:
The passage starts with this question: what should online tutors do? Then it says that some people tried to answer by the "**adoption of particular metaphors**". Examples are moderator, mentor and facilitator. They use these metaphors "to describe the tutor's role".

So people describe the tutor's role through metaphors.

- The passage says that these terms "warn us to stand aside". But a warning system is not what people did to describe the role.
- The passage does not talk about adding value to guidance or about duties outside education.

questions.question_md: What will inhibit student's contribution to tutorial discussions?
options: Too much contribution of the tutor
questions.explanation:
The passage says: "too much or inappropriate, contribution to tutorial discussion by the tutor can inhibit contributions by the students."

So when the tutor talks too much, the students talk less.

- The passage does not mention disruption, internal divisions or outside intervention.
- These options sound reasonable, but the answer must come from the passage.

questions.question_md: The rhetoric of moderators has the intention to :
options: Liberate students for their own learning
questions.explanation:
The passage says that this rhetoric "speaks of a duty to **liberate the students**". It also wants to "empower them to participate in their own learning".

So the aim is to free students to take part in their own learning.

- "Displace teachers from teaching" goes too far. The tutor moves from the centre but still teaches.
- "Strengthen the authority of teachers" is the opposite. The passage says that this view seeks to *remove* the teacher's authority.
- "Avoid critical pedagogy" is wrong. The passage says that this rhetoric has "the ring of critical pedagogy".

questions.question_md: The discourse of participatory learning may result in:
options: Abandonment of the online tutorial system
Emergence of dos and don'ts guidelines
questions.explanation:
The passage says that these formulations (moderator, facilitator) "guide us about what we **shouldn't do**, but remain rather silent about what we **should be doing**".

So the language of participatory learning gives guidelines of the "dos and don'ts" type. It mostly tells tutors what not to do.

- The passage does not say that online tutorials will be abandoned.
- It does not mention student protests. The word "protestations" in the passage refers to claims of equality, not to protests.
- It does not give students a supervisory role.

questions.question_md: The passage is an analysis of:
questions.explanation:
The passage asks what online tutors should do. It looks at the metaphors of moderator, mentor and facilitator. It points out problems: these terms say what not to do, and the claim of equality fails when assessment comes in. It ends with: "There are **paradoxes** here."

So the passage analyses the paradoxes of online tutoring.

- It is about online learning, not the traditional system.
- Assessment comes up only once. The passage does not discuss a new assessment method.
- It does not talk about Indian vocational education.

papers.instructions_note: 50 compulsory questions, 2 marks each

groups.md:
The following table shows population of five villages A-E and percentage distribution of males (M), females (F) and transgenders (T) among them. Based on the data in the table, answer the questions :

**Village - wise Distribution of Population**

| Village | Total Population | Distribution (%): M | F | T |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 12,000 | 46% | (-) | 22% |
| B | 16,000 | (-) | 33% | 27% |
| C | 18,000 | 32% | 36% | (-) |
| D | 24,000 | 36% | (-) | 20% |
| E | 25,000 | (-) | 30% | 25% |

Note : In table (-) denotes missing value (%), which is to be computed whenever required.

Read the following passage and answer the question.

Gordon Childe used the term urban revolution to describe the change in society marked by the emergence of the first cities some 5500 years ago. The areas that first witnessed this profound social economic change were :

- Mesopotamia - the valleys of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers
- The lower Nile valley.
- The plains of the river Indus.

Later, urban civilisations developed around the Mediterranean, in the Yellow River valley of China, in South East Asia and in the Americas. Thus the first cities mainly emerged in areas that are now considered to be LICs.

The catalyst for this period of rapid change change was the Neolithic Revolution, which occurred about 8000 BCE. This was when sedentary agriculture, based on the domestication of animals and cereal farming, steadily replaced a nomadic way of life. As farming advanced, irrigation techniques were developed. Other major advances that followed were the ox-drawn plough, the wheeled cart, the sailing boat and metallurgy. However, arguably the most important development was the invention of writing in about 4000 BCE, for it was in the millennium after this that some of the villages on the alluvial plains between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers increased in size and changed in function so as to merit the classification of urban.

Considerably later than the first cities, trading centres began to develop, The Minoan civilisation cities of Knossos and Phaistos, which flourished in Crete during the first half of the second millennium BCE, derived their wealth form maritime trade. Next it was the turn of the Greeks and then the Romans to develop urban and trading systems on a scale larger than ever before.

questions.question_md: Transgender population in Village - A is ______% of the female population in Village - B.
questions.explanation:
Use the given percentages for the two groups.

- Village A has 12,000 people. Transgenders are 22%, so they number **2,640**.
- Village B has 16,000 people. Females are 33%, so they number **5,280**.

Now compare: 2,640 ÷ 5,280 × 100 = **50%**.

So the transgender population of A is exactly half of the female population of B, or 50%. The other values (75, 33.33, 66.66) come from using wrong rows or wrong percentages.

questions.question_md: Find the difference between male population in Village - E and female population in Village - D.
questions.explanation:
In each village, M + F + T = 100%. Use this rule to find the missing values.

- Village E: M = 100 − 30 − 25 = 45%. Males = 45% of 25,000 = **11,250**.
- Village D: F = 100 − 36 − 20 = 44%. Females = 44% of 24,000 = **10,560**.

Difference = 11,250 − 10,560 = **690**.

A quick check: 45% of 25,000 and 44% of 24,000 differ only a little, so the answer must be small. Only 690 fits the exact calculation.

questions.question_md: Find the ratio of population of transgenders in Village - C to population of males in Village - B.
questions.explanation:
In each village, M + F + T = 100%.

- Village C: T = 100 − 32 − 36 = 32%. Transgenders = 32% of 18,000 = **5,760**.
- Village B: M = 100 − 33 − 27 = 40%. Males = 40% of 16,000 = **6,400**.

Ratio = 5,760 : 6,400. Divide both by 640. The result is **9 : 10**.

The ratio 27 : 32 would come from 27% of B against 32% of B. That uses the wrong village and the wrong group.

questions.question_md: What is the difference between number of males and females in Village - A ?
questions.explanation:
In Village A, F = 100 − 46 − 22 = 32%.

- Males = 46% of 12,000 = 5,520.
- Females = 32% of 12,000 = 3,840.

Difference = 5,520 − 3,840 = **1,680**.

A shorter way: the gap in percentages is 46 − 32 = 14%. Then 14% of 12,000 = 1,680.

The value 1,920 would come from 16% of 12,000. That uses a wrong female percentage.

questions.question_md: Total number of females in Villages B and D together is ________% more than the number of males in Village - C.
questions.explanation:
Find the missing percentages first. In each village, M + F + T = 100%.

- Females in B = 33% of 16,000 = 5,280.
- Females in D: F = 100 − 36 − 20 = 44%. So 44% of 24,000 = 10,560.
- Total females in B and D = 5,280 + 10,560 = **15,840**.
- Males in C = 32% of 18,000 = **5,760**.

"Percent more" = (difference ÷ base) × 100.

- Difference = 15,840 − 5,760 = 10,080.
- 10,080 ÷ 5,760 × 100 = **175%**.

The value 275% is the total as a percent of the base (15,840 ÷ 5,760 = 2.75). The question asks how much **more**, so we subtract 100%.

questions.question_md: In ADDIE model of instructional design framework, the letters I and E in the acronym ADDIE pertain to
questions.explanation:
ADDIE is a common model for instructional design (planning a course or lesson). It has five stages:

- **A** – Analysis: find learner needs and goals.
- **D** – Design: plan objectives, content and methods.
- **D** – Development: make the materials.
- **I** – Implementation: deliver the course to learners.
- **E** – Evaluation: check if the course worked and improve it.

So I stands for Implementation and E stands for Evaluation. "Identification" and "Examination" are not stages of ADDIE.

questions.question_md: Students participating in online classes are taught by an instructor. Following the lesson, the instructor intends to incorporate reading materials (e-content, Power point presentation, etc.) that can be viewed by the students. What option would instructor choose ?
questions.explanation:
A **Learning Management System (LMS)** is software for running online courses. Examples are Moodle and Google Classroom. The teacher can upload e-content, slides and readings in one place. Students log in and view them at any time. The LMS also tracks who has viewed or submitted the work.

- Content creation tools (such as PowerPoint) help to **make** the material. They do not share it with a class in an organised way.
- Networking tools connect people. They do not manage course content.
- Links to websites give only scattered access. They cannot hold the teacher's own files or track students.

questions.question_md: Which of the following does not come under primary laws of learning ?
questions.explanation:
E. L. Thorndike gave three **primary laws** of learning:

- **Law of Readiness**: a learner learns best when he or she is ready to act.
- **Law of Exercise**: practice makes a connection stronger.
- **Law of Effect**: a satisfying result makes a response stronger.

Thorndike also gave **secondary (subsidiary) laws**. These include multiple response, set or attitude, partial activity, assimilation and associative shifting.

The Law of Multiple Response says that a learner tries many responses until one works. It is a secondary law, so it does not come under the primary laws.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Project method is best associated with the Philosophy of John Dewey.

**Statement II :** The strength of Project method lies in social participation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is correct.** W. H. Kilpatrick developed the Project method. He was a student of John Dewey. The method uses Dewey's pragmatism, which says that children learn by doing real tasks.
- **Statement II is correct.** In a project, students plan and work together on a real problem. They share tasks, discuss and help each other. This social participation is the main strength of the method. It also builds cooperation and responsibility.

Both statements are correct.

questions.question_md:
For Undergraduate educational programmes, courses on SWAYAM Platform have been developed by :

A. NPTEL

B. IIM Ahmedabad

C. AICTE

D. CEC

E. IIM Bangalore

F. UGC

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: A, C, D and E Only
A, D, E and F Only
questions.explanation:
SWAYAM is India's national platform for online courses. The Ministry of Education appointed **national coordinators** for different types of courses:

- **NPTEL** – engineering courses (A).
- **AICTE** – self-paced and international courses (C).
- **CEC** (Consortium for Educational Communication) – undergraduate courses (D).
- **IIM Bangalore** – management courses (E).
- **UGC** – postgraduate courses in non-technical subjects (F).
- NCERT, NIOS, IGNOU and NITTTR handle school, out-of-school and teacher-training courses.

IIM Ahmedabad (B) is not a SWAYAM national coordinator. UGC (F) handles postgraduate courses, not undergraduate courses. So the best set is **A, C, D and E**.

questions.question_md: While reading research paper or research reports, often one comes across the abbreviation 'viz', which means
questions.explanation:
"Viz." is a short form of the Latin word *videlicet*. It means "**namely**" or "that is to say". Writers use it before a list or an exact detail.

Example: "We used two methods, viz. survey and interview."

- "For example" is "e.g." (*exempli gratia*). It gives only some examples, not the full list.
- "Against" is "vs." or "v.".
- "Refer to" is "see" or "cf." (compare).

questions.question_md: A student submits Ph.D. thesis in a university. Upon scrutiny, it is found that his/her thesis has a similarity content of 35%. This would fall in which of the following categories of plagiarism according to UGC regulations ?
questions.explanation:
The UGC (Promotion of Academic Integrity and Prevention of Plagiarism in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2018 set four levels of similarity:

- **Level 0**: up to 10% – minor, no penalty.
- **Level 1**: above 10% and up to 40%.
- **Level 2**: above 40% and up to 60%.
- **Level 3**: above 60%.

A similarity of 35% is more than 10% and not more than 40%. So it falls in **Level 1**. At this level, the student must submit a revised thesis within a fixed time.

questions.question_md: The part of research paper that gives an overview of the field to be investigated and the investigator's hypotheses about the research outcome, is called
questions.explanation:
The **Introduction** of a research paper does three main jobs:

- It gives the background of the field.
- It reviews earlier work and shows the gap.
- It states the research problem and the **hypotheses** (expected results).

- The **Abstract** is a short summary of the whole paper. It is not a full overview of the field.
- The **Method** section tells how the researcher did the study.
- The **Results** section reports what the study found.

questions.question_md: A study in which a group of participants is observed and measured over a period of time, refers to
questions.explanation:
In **longitudinal research**, the researcher studies the **same** group of people again and again over a long time. For example, a researcher measures the same children at ages 5, 10 and 15. This shows how people change over time.

- **Cross-sectional research** studies different groups at **one** point in time.
- **Archival research** uses records that already exist, such as old files or census data.
- **Correlational research** measures the relation between two variables. It does not need repeated measures over time.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** In case of qualitative phenomena, we have data on the basis of presence or absence of an attribute or more than one attribute.

**Statement II :** With such data as mentioned in Statement I above the sampling distribution may take the form of a Binomial probability distribution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** We cannot measure qualitative data (attributes) in numbers. We only note if an attribute is present or absent. Examples are "literate or not" and "male or female". We can also use more than one attribute.
- **Statement II is true.** Each case has only two outcomes: the attribute is present or absent. When we count "successes" in many such cases, the count follows a **Binomial distribution**. So the sampling distribution of such data can take a Binomial form.

This idea comes from standard research methodology texts, such as C. R. Kothari's book on sampling of attributes.

questions.question_md: Every society, because of communication, reflects a sense of _____ to most extent.
questions.explanation:
Communication means "to make common". People share ideas, values, language and customs through communication. This sharing creates a sense of **commonality** (shared identity) in a society.

- **Doubt** and **indifference** (lack of interest) do not come from communication as a rule.
- **Animus** means hostility or ill will. It is the opposite of the bond that communication builds.

So every society, because of communication, mostly reflects a sense of commonality.

questions.question_md:
On the negative side, communicative language is used to :

A. Extend democratic debates

B. Suppress truth

C. Divide the society

D. Permeate ethnocentrism

E. Support global peace efforts

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The question asks about the **negative** uses of communicative language. Check each item:

- A. Extend democratic debates – this is a **positive** use.
- B. Suppress truth – **negative**. Propaganda and misinformation hide the truth.
- C. Divide the society – **negative**. Hate speech can divide groups.
- D. Permeate ethnocentrism – **negative**. Ethnocentrism means to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture. Language can spread this bias.
- E. Support global peace efforts – this is a **positive** use.

So the negative uses are **B, C and D**.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Communication, culture and power are inter-related.

**Statement II :** Socio-cultural values when communicated do not have any weightage of power.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** Communication carries culture from one person to another. Groups that control the media and language can shape the culture. So communication, culture and power are connected to each other.
- **Statement II is false.** Socio-cultural values always carry some power. Dominant groups spread their values through communication. These values then shape how people think and act. Thinkers such as Gramsci call this cultural **hegemony** (control through ideas).

So Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

questions.question_md:
Modern communication technology has converted words into

A. A tool of equality

B. Time

C. A tool of unwarranted peace

D. Money

E. Power

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Modern communication technology has changed the value of words. Check each item:

- B. **Time** – words now travel at once across the world. Speed of messages has become very important.
- D. **Money** – words and information are now sold. Advertising, data and content earn money.
- E. **Power** – those who control information and media can influence people and governments.
- A. A tool of equality – access to technology is not equal. The digital divide shows this, so this is not the best choice.
- C. A tool of unwarranted peace – this has no clear meaning here.

So the best set is **B, D and E**.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** The semantic code in communication deals with character and characterisation.

**Statement II :** Roland Barthes describes this code as the voice of the person.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
Roland Barthes was a French thinker. In his book *S/Z* (1970), he described **five codes** that give meaning to a text. Each code has a "voice":

- Hermeneutic code – the voice of truth (mystery and its answer).
- Proairetic code – the voice of empirics (actions).
- **Semantic code** – the **voice of the person**.
- Symbolic code – the voice of the symbol.
- Cultural code – the voice of science (shared knowledge).

- **Statement I is true.** The semantic code works through connotations (extra meanings). These meanings collect around characters and build characterisation.
- **Statement II is true.** Barthes himself calls the semantic code "the voice of the person".

questions.question_md: A shopkeeper purchases a packet of 60 pens at Rs. 10 per pen. He sells a part of the packet at a profit of 40%. On the remaining part, he bears a loss of 20%. If his overall profit on the whole packet is 20% of , find the number of pens he sold at profit.
questions.explanation:
Cost price of the packet = 60 × Rs 10 = **Rs 600**. The overall profit is 20%, so profit = 20% of 600 = **Rs 120**.

Let x pens be sold at a 40% profit.

- Profit on each such pen = 40% of 10 = Rs 4. Total profit = 4x.
- The other (60 − x) pens give a 20% loss. Loss on each pen = Rs 2. Total loss = 2(60 − x).

Net profit: 4x − 2(60 − x) = 120.

- 4x − 120 + 2x = 120
- 6x = 240
- x = **40**

Check: 40 pens give Rs 160 profit. 20 pens give Rs 40 loss. Net profit = Rs 120, which is 20% of 600.

questions.question_md: A batsman scored 98 runs in his 17th match . As a result his average runs per match increased by 2.5. What was his average before playing 17ᵗʰ match ?
questions.explanation:
Let the average after 16 matches be **a**. Total runs after 16 matches = 16a.

After the 17th match, the average becomes a + 2.5. So total runs = 17(a + 2.5).

The 17th match adds 98 runs:

- 16a + 98 = 17(a + 2.5)
- 16a + 98 = 17a + 42.5
- a = 98 − 42.5 = **55.5**

Check: the new average is 58. Then 17 × 58 = 986 and 16 × 55.5 = 888. The difference is 98, which matches.

The value 58.5 is close to the new average, not the old one.

questions.question_md: Water level of a river increases and decreases by 10% on alternate days in the rainy season. What shall be the increase or decrease in the water level at the end of second day, as compared to the initial water level ?
questions.explanation:
Let the starting level be 100.

- Day 1: the level rises by 10%. 100 × 1.10 = 110.
- Day 2: the level falls by 10%. 110 × 0.90 = 99.

The final level is 99. This is **1% less** than the start.

The rise and the fall have the same percentage. But the fall applies to a bigger base (110). So the net result is always a decrease. Shortcut: net change = −(10 × 10) ÷ 100 = −1%.

The order of rise and fall does not matter. 100 × 0.90 × 1.10 also gives 99.

questions.question_md: There are two numbers such that the sum of twice the first number and thrice the 2ⁿᵈ number is 39. Also the sum of thrice the first number and twice the 2nd number is 36. The largest of the two numbers is ?
questions.explanation:
Let the numbers be x (first) and y (second).

- 2x + 3y = 39
- 3x + 2y = 36

Add the two equations: 5x + 5y = 75. So x + y = 15.

Subtract the second from the first: −x + y = 3. So y − x = 3.

Now solve: y = 9 and x = 6.

Check: 2(6) + 3(9) = 12 + 27 = 39. And 3(6) + 2(9) = 18 + 18 = 36.

The larger number is **9**. The value 15 is the sum of the two numbers, not one of them.

questions.question_md: If SEARCH is coded as 214673 and CHART is coded as 73465, then what will be the code for TEACHER ?
questions.explanation:
Each letter has a fixed digit. Match the letters with the digits.

- SEARCH = 2 1 4 6 7 3. So S = 2, E = 1, A = 4, R = 6, C = 7, H = 3.
- CHART = 7 3 4 6 5. This confirms C = 7, H = 3, A = 4, R = 6. It also gives T = 5.

Now code TEACHER letter by letter:

T = 5, E = 1, A = 4, C = 7, H = 3, E = 1, R = 6.

So TEACHER = **5147316**. The other options have the right digits in a wrong order.

questions.question_md: "Today on average we can look forward to a longer life span than the generation before us. It is obvious that it has been possible only and only because of the millions of dedicated doctors who have ensured our good health". Identify the fallacy committee in the above argument from the following options ?
questions.explanation:
The argument says that longer life is possible "only and only" because of doctors. This ignores many other causes. Examples are better food, clean water, sanitation, vaccines, housing and higher income.

The fallacy of **False Cause** happens when we name one thing as the cause without enough proof. It also happens when we treat one factor as the only cause. So this is a false cause.

- **Hasty generalisation** draws a general rule from too few cases. The argument does not do this.
- **Slippery slope** says that one step will lead to a chain of bad events. There is no such chain here.
- **Appeal to unqualified authority** quotes a person who is not an expert. The argument quotes no authority.

questions.question_md:
If the statement 'All cricketers are rich persons' is given as true which of the following statements can be inferred to be false ?

A. No cricketers are rich persons.

B. Some cricketers are rich persons.

C. Some cricketers are not rich persons.

D. Some rich persons are cricketers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
"All cricketers are rich persons" is an **A** proposition (universal affirmative). Use the square of opposition.

- A. "No cricketers are rich persons" is the **E** form. A and E are **contraries**. They cannot both be true. So E is **false**.
- B. "Some cricketers are rich persons" is the **I** form. It is the subaltern of A. If A is true, I is **true**.
- C. "Some cricketers are not rich persons" is the **O** form. A and O are **contradictories**. If A is true, O is **false**.
- D. "Some rich persons are cricketers" is the converse of B. It is also **true**.

So the false statements are **A and C**.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following propositions are so related that they cannot both be true, although they both may be false ?

A. All football players are rich persons.

B. No football players are rich persons.

C. Some football players are rich persons.

D. Some football players are not rich persons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Two propositions that cannot both be true, but can both be false, are **contraries**. In the square of opposition, only the **A** and **E** forms are contraries.

- A. "All football players are rich persons" – **A** form.
- B. "No football players are rich persons" – **E** form.
- C. "Some football players are rich persons" – **I** form.
- D. "Some football players are not rich persons" – **O** form.

A and B cannot both be true. But both can be false, for example if only some players are rich.

- A and D (A and O) are contradictories. Exactly one of them is true.
- C and D (I and O) are subcontraries. They cannot both be false.
- B and C (E and I) are also contradictories.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following propositions are logically equivalent ?

A. No dogs are aggressive animals.

B. No aggressive animals are dogs.

C. All dogs are non-aggressive.

D. Some dogs are not aggressive animals.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Logically equivalent propositions always have the same truth value.

- A. "No dogs are aggressive animals" is an **E** proposition.
- B. "No aggressive animals are dogs" is the **converse** of A. The conversion of an E proposition is valid. So B is equivalent to A.
- C. "All dogs are non-aggressive" is the **obverse** of A. To obvert, change the quality (No → All) and negate the predicate. Obversion is always valid. So C is equivalent to A.
- D. "Some dogs are not aggressive animals" is an **O** proposition. It follows from A, but A does not follow from D. So D is not equivalent.

So **A, B and C** are equivalent.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two Statements :

**Statement I :** According to classical Indian school of Logic, namely ,Nyaya, we ascertain the relation of universal concomitance between x and y by perceiving that in all cases the presence of x is accompanied by presence of y, and not perceiving any instances to the contrary.

**Statement II :** Classical Indian materialists argue that universal relation between two events cannot be established, there being always a room for doubt about the unobserved cases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
Vyāpti means universal concomitance, the fixed relation between two things. An example is "wherever there is smoke, there is fire".

- **Statement I is true.** The Nyāya school (Indian logic) gets vyāpti in this way. We see that x and y always occur together. This is **anvaya** (agreement in presence). We also see no case of x without y. This is the non-observation of contrary cases. Nyāya also uses absence cases (vyatireka) and tarka (indirect reasoning) to support this.
- **Statement II is true.** The Cārvāka school (Indian materialists) accepts only perception. They say that we can never observe all cases. So some doubt always remains about unseen cases. For this reason, vyāpti and inference cannot be fully certain.

Both statements are true.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following applications A-C are built on top of open-source digital platforms ?

A. Aadhar

B. Adobe Reader

C. COWIN

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **A. Aadhaar is correct.** The Aadhaar system uses an open technology stack. It uses open-source software and open standards to avoid dependence on one vendor.
- **B. Adobe Reader is wrong.** It is free to download, but it is **proprietary** software. Adobe owns its code, and the source code is not open.
- **C. CoWIN is correct.** India built CoWIN on an open-source digital platform for vaccination and certificates.

So **A and C only** are built on open-source platforms. "Free of cost" is different from "open source". This difference makes Adobe Reader the trap.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** IBM was the most valuable worldwide IT brand in 2022.

**Statement II :** TCS and Infosys were the second and the third most valuable Indian brands respectively in the IT services sector globally in 2022.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II is false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
This question uses the Brand Finance ranking of IT services brands for 2022.

- **Statement I is false.** **Accenture** was the most valuable IT services brand in the world in 2022, not IBM.
- **Statement II is true.** TCS was the second most valuable IT services brand. Infosys was third. Both are Indian companies.

So Statement I is false and Statement II is true. Questions like this depend on a ranking for one particular year. Rankings change, so note the year carefully.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements (A-C) are correct with reference to "Software as a Service (SaaS)" in cloud computing ?

A. SaaS users can access their data from any Internet-Connected computer on mobile device.

B. A web-based email service such as Outlook, Hotmail or Yahoo! Mail is a form of SaaS.

C. SaaS buyers can customize the user interface to change the look and feel of the software, as well as modify specific areas, such as a data fields.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Software as a Service (SaaS) means that the provider runs the software on its own servers. Users use it through the Internet, usually with a web browser.

- **A is correct.** The data and software stay in the cloud. So users can reach them from any computer or mobile device with Internet.
- **B is correct.** Web email such as Outlook, Hotmail or Yahoo! Mail is a common example of SaaS. The user installs nothing.
- **C is correct.** Many SaaS products let buyers customise the interface. Buyers can change the look and feel and some data fields. They cannot change the core program code.

So **A, B and C** are all correct.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following communication technologies A-C are considered as short-range devices/technologies ?

A. CCTV

B. RFID

C. WLAN

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
**Short-range devices (SRDs)** are low-power radio devices. They work over a short distance, from a few centimetres to a few hundred metres. Regulators such as ETSI list many types of SRDs.

- **A. CCTV**: wireless CCTV cameras send video over short-range radio links. The SRD lists include such video devices.
- **B. RFID** (Radio Frequency Identification): tags work from a few centimetres to a few metres. It is a classic SRD.
- **C. WLAN** (Wireless LAN or Wi-Fi): it covers a home, office or campus. It is also a short-range technology.

So **A, B and C** are all short-range devices or technologies.

questions.question_md: In India, the term "Public Key Infrastructure" is used in the context of
questions.explanation:
**Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)** is a system for **digital security**. It uses a pair of keys: a public key and a private key. It also uses **digital certificates** to prove who a person or website is.

In India, the Information Technology Act, 2000 gives legal status to digital signatures. The **Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)** runs the PKI in India. Licensed Certifying Authorities issue Digital Signature Certificates.

People use PKI for e-filing of tax returns, e-tenders, secure e-mail and online banking. It has no link with food security, health care, education or transport.

questions.question_md:
What is the correct sequence of steps in Risk assessment related to environmental hazards ?

A. Risk characterization

B. Exposure assessment

C. Hazard Identification

D. Risk Management

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Environmental risk assessment follows a fixed order:

1. **Hazard identification (C)**: find out if a chemical or agent can cause harm.
2. **Exposure assessment (B)**: find out how much people come in contact with it, and for how long.
3. **Risk characterisation (A)**: combine the earlier steps to estimate the size of the risk.
4. **Risk management (D)**: decide what action to take to reduce the risk.

(The full model also has a dose–response step after hazard identification. It is not in this list.)

So the order is **C, B, A, D**. Risk characterisation needs the exposure data first, so A cannot come before B.

questions.question_md: National Solar Mission, one of the missions of National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) was launched in the year
questions.explanation:
India released its **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** in 2008. It has eight national missions. The **National Solar Mission** is one of them. Its full name is the **Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission (JNNSM)**.

The Union Cabinet approved the mission in late 2009. The Government formally **launched** it in **January 2010**.

So the year of launch is **2010**. The option 2009 is a trap because the approval came in that year.

questions.question_md: Which one of the following has contributed maximum in sea level rise so far in the context of climate change ?
questions.explanation:
Sea level rises for two main reasons:

- Ocean water **expands** when it gets warmer. This is **thermal expansion**.
- Ice on land melts, and the water flows into the sea.

The IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) reports that thermal expansion has been the **largest single** contributor so far. The oceans absorb most of the extra heat from global warming. This warms a huge volume of water.

Melting of mountain glaciers is the next big cause. The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets contribute less so far, but their share is now growing fast.

questions.question_md:
Out of different oxides of nitrogen which of the following are considered as Air Pollutants and known as NOx ?

A. NO (Nitric Oxide)

B. NO₂ (Nitrogen dioxide)

C. NO₃ (Nitrogen trioxide)

D. N₂O (Nitrous oxide)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
In air pollution studies, **NOx** means the sum of two gases:

- **A. NO (nitric oxide)** – it forms in vehicle engines and power plants when fuel burns at high temperature.
- **B. NO₂ (nitrogen dioxide)** – it forms when NO reacts with oxygen. It is a brown, toxic gas. It helps to form smog and acid rain.

The other oxides are not part of NOx:

- C. NO₃ is a short-lived radical. It is not a main air pollutant.
- D. N₂O (nitrous oxide) is a **greenhouse gas**. It is also called "laughing gas". Experts count it separately from NOx.

So the answer is **A and B only**.

questions.question_md:
The advantages of biodiesel over conventional petro diesel are :

A. Biodiesel produces significantly lesser CO₂ and SO₂.

B. It is non-renewable

C. It has higher octane number

D. It can be used in any ratio with petro-diesel

E. It has lower flash point.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Check each statement:

- **A. Correct.** Biodiesel has almost no sulphur, so it gives very little SO₂. Plants absorb CO₂ as they grow. So the net CO₂ over the life cycle is much lower.
- **B. Wrong.** Biodiesel comes from plant oils and animal fats. It is **renewable**.
- **C. Accepted as correct.** We measure diesel fuel quality by the **cetane** number, not the octane number. Biodiesel has a higher cetane number than petro-diesel. The examiner clearly meant this.
- **D. Correct.** Biodiesel mixes with petro-diesel in any ratio, such as B5, B20 or B100.
- **E. Wrong.** Biodiesel has a **higher** flash point (the lowest temperature at which its vapour can catch fire). This makes it safer to store.

So the advantages are **A, C and D**.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following names of technology platforms has been mentioned in NEP-2020 through which online training of teachers will be encouraged ?

A. SWAYAM

B. AYUSH

C. PARAKH

D. DIKSHA

E. NIT

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 wants teachers to keep learning. It names technology platforms for the online training of teachers. These are:

- **A. SWAYAM** – the national platform for online courses (MOOCs).
- **D. DIKSHA** – the national digital platform for school teachers.

The NEP says that platforms such as SWAYAM and DIKSHA will help to give standard training to many teachers in a short time.

- **AYUSH** is the Ministry for traditional systems of medicine.
- **PARAKH** is the national assessment centre in NEP 2020. It sets norms for testing students, not for training teachers.
- **NIT** means National Institute of Technology. It is not a platform.

questions.question_md:
In 1904, Curzon was the moving force behind the enactment of the Indian University Act which intended to introduce radical changes into which of the following universities :

A. Calcutta

B. Bombay

C. Madras

D. Punjab (in Lahore)

E. Allahabad

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: A, C, D and E Only
A, B, C, D and E
questions.explanation:
Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905. He set up the Indian Universities Commission in 1902. After its report, the Government passed the **Indian Universities Act of 1904**.

In 1904, India had five universities:

- **Calcutta, Bombay and Madras** – started in 1857.
- **Punjab (Lahore)** – started in 1882.
- **Allahabad** – started in 1887.

The Act applied to all five. It increased government control over the senates, affiliation of colleges and inspection. Indian nationalists criticised it as an attempt to control higher education.

So the answer is **A, B, C, D and E**.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** UGC is a central government organization established by an Act of Parliament in 1956.

**Statement II :** UGC has established five regional centres in order to ensure proper functioning.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
The official key marks **both statements as incorrect**.

- **Statement II is clearly incorrect.** The UGC has **six** regional centres, not five. They are at Pune, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Bhopal, Guwahati and Bengaluru.
- **Statement I** is the debatable part. The UGC first came into being on **28 December 1953**. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad inaugurated it. The **UGC Act of 1956** only made it a **statutory body**. It is also an autonomous body, not a government department. The examiner seems to treat "established in 1956" and "central government organisation" as wrong for these reasons.

Many books say "UGC was established by an Act of Parliament in 1956". So some students may judge Statement I as correct. But the official key, issued after challenges, accepts that both statements are incorrect.

questions.question_md: Ministry of Environment and Forests, Govt. of India with the help of centre for Environment Education (CEE), _______ launched a National Environmental Awareness campaign (NEAC) in 1986 to increase awareness about the environment in various target groups in the country.
questions.explanation:
The **Centre for Environment Education (CEE)** has its head office in **Ahmedabad**, Gujarat. It started in 1984 as a centre of excellence of the Ministry of Environment and Forests.

In 1986, the Ministry started the **National Environment Awareness Campaign (NEAC)**. CEE was the national coordinating agency. NEAC supports NGOs, schools and other groups. They run awareness activities on environmental issues every year.

Chennai, Delhi and Hyderabad are not the headquarters of CEE. CEE has regional offices in some other cities, but its main centre is Ahmedabad.

questions.question_md: Which of the following is an important archaeological site declared by UNESCO as a world Heritage site in 1980 ?
questions.explanation:
**Taxila (Takshashila)** is an ancient city and centre of learning. Today it is in Punjab province, Pakistan. UNESCO declared Taxila a **World Heritage Site in 1980**. It has remains from many periods: Persian, Greek, Mauryan, Kushan and Buddhist.

- **Nalanda** (Bihar) became a World Heritage Site much later, in **2016**.
- **Vallabhi** (Gujarat) and **Mithila** (Bihar–Nepal region) are historic places, but they are not World Heritage Sites.

questions.question_md:
Based on the information given in the passage, arrange the following events in correct chronological order.

A. Emergence of the first cities

B. Neolithic Revolution

C. Invention of writing

D. The Minoan civilisation cities which flourished in Crete

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Take the dates from the passage:

- **B. Neolithic Revolution** – about 8000 BCE.
- **C. Invention of writing** – about 4000 BCE.
- **A. First cities** – about 5500 years ago, which is about 3500 BCE. The passage says that villages became urban "in the millennium after" writing.
- **D. Minoan cities of Crete** – first half of the second millennium BCE (about 2000–1500 BCE).

So the strict order is **B, C, A, D**. This order is **not among the options**.

The key gives B, A, C, D. This is the nearest option. It puts the Neolithic Revolution first and Crete last, and it only swaps two close events. The examiner probably linked "first cities" closely with the Neolithic Revolution, which the passage calls their catalyst. B, C, D, A is far worse, because it puts the first cities after Crete.

questions.question_md: The term LICs in the passage most likely represents
questions.explanation:
The passage says that the first cities grew in Mesopotamia (Iraq), the lower Nile valley (Egypt) and the Indus plains (Pakistan and India). It then says that these areas "are now considered to be LICs".

**LIC** is a standard term in geography and economics. It means **Low Income Country**. Many of these regions are now poorer, developing countries. The passage makes a contrast: ancient cities started there, but these areas are not rich today.

- "Lower Indo-China", "Later Indus and China" and "Laos, India and China" do not fit. Mesopotamia and Egypt are not in Asia's Indo-China region.

questions.question_md: Which major development led to the transformation of villages in the plains between Euphrates and Tigris, into urban centres ?
questions.explanation:
The passage lists many advances after the Neolithic Revolution: irrigation, the ox-drawn plough, the wheeled cart, the sailing boat and metallurgy (working with metals).

Then it says that "arguably the most important development was the **invention of writing**". In the millennium after writing, villages between the Tigris and Euphrates grew in size and changed in function. They became **urban** centres.

- The **Neolithic Revolution** was the catalyst for the whole period. It started farming, not cities directly.
- The **wheeled cart** and **metallurgy** were advances, but the passage does not link them directly to the change into cities.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following places where urban centres developed, in correct chronological order.

A. Greece

B. Crete

C. Rome

D. The plains of river Indus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Use the order given in the passage:

- **D. Plains of the river Indus** – one of the first areas of the urban revolution, about 5500 years ago.
- **B. Crete** – Minoan cities (Knossos and Phaistos) grew in the first half of the second millennium BCE. The passage says that this was "considerably later than the first cities".
- **A. Greece** – "Next it was the turn of the Greeks".
- **C. Rome** – "and then the Romans".

So the order is **D, B, A, C**. Options that start with Greece are wrong, because Greece came long after the Indus cities.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Urban centres in China developed before they developed in the plains of Indus river.

**Statement II :** Trading centres developed much later than the first cities.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** The passage lists the Indus plains among the **first** areas of urban change. It says that cities "later" developed in the Yellow River valley of China. So Chinese cities came **after** the Indus cities.
- **Statement II is true.** The passage says: "Considerably later than the first cities, trading centres began to develop". Examples are the Minoan cities of Crete, and later Greek and Roman cities.

So Statement I is false and Statement II is true.

groups.md:
**The following table shows the percentage (%) distribution of wheat production in seven different countries, namely, India, China, Japan, Srilanka, Indonesia, Pakistan and Bangladesh by deploying Scientific Method and Conventional Method. Total production of wheat in these countries is 50 lakh tonnes. Based on the data in the table, answer the questions that follow**

Country-wise Distribution of Wheat Production

| Country | Distribution (%) of Wheat Production (out of 50 lakh tonnes) | Distribution (%) of Wheat Production: Scientific Method | Distribution (%) of Wheat Production: Conventional Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| India | 18% | 32% | 68% |
| China | 22% | 70% | 30% |
| Japan | 20% | 78% | 22% |
| Srilanka | 13% | 60% | 40% |
| Indonesia | 10% | 73% | 27% |
| Pakistan | 9% | 66% | 34% |
| Bangladesh | 8% | 20% | 80% |

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:

In 1882 the Punjab University was established by a Special Act of Incorporation and in 1887 another Special Act of Incorporation established the fifth Indian university at Allahabad. The general framework of these two Special Acts of Incorporation was similar to the Acts of 1857 though power was given to the Senates of the Punjab and the Allahabad Universities "to appoint or provide for the appointment of Professor and Lecturers"- a privilege which was denied by the Acts of Incorporation to the first three universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras in 1857. The first three universities were deliberately intended to be examining universities only, in the same manner and on the same model as the then University of London. Thereby it ignored an important suggestion of the Education Despatch of 1854 which suggested possible institution of "professorships for the purpose of the delivery of lectures in various branches of learning for the acquisition of which, at any rate in an advanced degree, facilities do not now exist in other institutions in India." When Lahore and Allahabad got this privilege in 1882 and 1887, respectively, The Indians had asked for its extension to Calcutta, Bombay and Madras but European officials closely connected with the university contested it on two grounds.

questions.question_md: The difference between the production of wheat by the Scientific Method and the Conventional Method in Indonesia is ______ lakh tonnes.
questions.explanation:
Total production is 50 lakh tonnes. Indonesia has 10% of it.

- Indonesia total = 10% of 50 = **5 lakh tonnes**.
- Scientific Method = 73% of 5 = **3.65** lakh tonnes.
- Conventional Method = 27% of 5 = **1.35** lakh tonnes.
- Difference = 3.65 − 1.35 = **2.3** lakh tonnes.

A short way: the gap between the two methods is 73% − 27% = 46%. Then 46% of 5 = 2.3.

questions.question_md: The approximate average production of wheat (in lakh tonnes) by the Scientific Method for all the seven countries is
questions.explanation:
First find each country's total. Then take the Scientific Method share.

- India: 9 × 0.32 = 2.88
- China: 11 × 0.70 = 7.70
- Japan: 10 × 0.78 = 7.80
- Srilanka: 6.5 × 0.60 = 3.90
- Indonesia: 5 × 0.73 = 3.65
- Pakistan: 4.5 × 0.66 = 2.97
- Bangladesh: 4 × 0.20 = 0.80

The sum is **29.70** lakh tonnes. The average is 29.70 ÷ 7 ≈ **4.24** lakh tonnes.

The value 4.12 is close, but it comes from a small error in the sum. The values 3.06 and 3.16 are far too low.

questions.question_md: The ratio of production of wheat by Conventional Method in Pakistan to that by the Scientific Method in Japan is -
questions.explanation:
Find the two amounts first.

- Pakistan total = 9% of 50 = 4.5 lakh tonnes. Conventional Method = 34% of 4.5 = **1.53**.
- Japan total = 20% of 50 = 10 lakh tonnes. Scientific Method = 78% of 10 = **7.8**.

Ratio = 1.53 : 7.8 = 153 : 780. Divide both by 3. The ratio is **51 : 260**.

The ratio 99 : 260 uses Pakistan's Scientific share (66%) by mistake. Check: 66% of 4.5 = 2.97, and 297 : 780 = 99 : 260.

questions.question_md: Production of wheat in Srilanka by the Conventional Method is approximately _____ times the production of wheat in India by the Scientific Method.
questions.explanation:
Find the two amounts first.

- Srilanka total = 13% of 50 = 6.5 lakh tonnes. Conventional Method = 40% of 6.5 = **2.6**.
- India total = 18% of 50 = 9 lakh tonnes. Scientific Method = 32% of 9 = **2.88**.

Times = 2.6 ÷ 2.88 ≈ **0.90**.

Srilanka's amount is a little smaller than India's amount. So the answer must be less than 1. Only 0.9 is less than 1.

questions.question_md: Production of wheat in India by the Scientific Method is approximately _____% more than the production of wheat in Pakistan by the Conventional Method.
questions.explanation:
Find the two amounts first.

- India, Scientific Method = 32% of 9 = **2.88** lakh tonnes.
- Pakistan, Conventional Method = 34% of 4.5 = **1.53** lakh tonnes.

Percentage more = (2.88 − 1.53) ÷ 1.53 × 100 = 1.35 ÷ 1.53 × 100 ≈ **88.24%**.

Use Pakistan's value as the base, because the question asks "more than" Pakistan. If you divide by 2.88, you get about 46.9%. That is a common mistake.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following softwares can be used to develop quizzes?

A. Wakelet

B. Learning Pod

C. Pixton

D. Hot Potatoes

E. Socrative

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
options: B, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Check what each tool does.

- **A. Wakelet**: no. It is a tool to collect and organise web links, videos and notes.
- **B. Learning Pod**: yes. It gives practice questions and quizzes.
- **C. Pixton**: no. It is a tool to make comics and storyboards.
- **D. Hot Potatoes**: yes. It is a free tool to make quizzes, crosswords and matching exercises.
- **E. Socrative**: yes. Teachers use it for live quizzes and quick checks in class.

So B, D and E are quiz tools. Options with A or C are wrong.

questions.question_md: What are the learning styles according to Fleming's VARK model of learning?
questions.explanation:
Neil Fleming made the VARK model in 1987. VARK is a short form of the four learning styles:

- **V – Visual**: learning from charts, maps and diagrams.
- **A – Auditory** (aural): learning by listening and talking.
- **R – Reading/writing**: learning from written text.
- **K – Kinesthetic**: learning by doing and by real experience.

The other options use wrong words such as "Verbal", "Auxiliary" or "Augmentative". These words do not form the VARK model.

questions.question_md: Rahul was trying to solve some mathematics problems related to trigonometry. He tried many times but failed. His teacher helped him, which led him to follow right approach and he succeeded to solve these problems. This is an example of-
questions.explanation:
Lev Vygotsky gave the idea of the **Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)**. The ZPD is the gap between two things:

- what a learner can do alone, and
- what the learner can do with help from a more skilled person.

Rahul could not solve the problems alone. With his teacher's help, he succeeded. This help is called scaffolding (temporary support). So the case shows the ZPD.

Schemas, assimilation and equilibrium are ideas from Jean Piaget. They describe how a child builds and changes mental structures. They do not focus on help from a teacher.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following curriculum development models come under Non technical, Non-scientific models?

A. Open Classroom Model

B. Goodlad's Model

C. Roger's Model of Interpersonal Relations

D. Weinstein and Fantini Model

E. Taba's Model

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Curriculum models are often put into two groups (Ornstein and Hunkins).

- **Technical-scientific models** use clear, step-by-step planning. Examples: Tyler, **Taba** and **Goodlad**.
- **Non-technical, non-scientific models** focus on the learner, feelings and personal growth. The plan is flexible.

Check each item:

- **A. Open Classroom Model**: non-technical. Learners choose and explore freely.
- **B. Goodlad's Model**: technical-scientific.
- **C. Roger's Model of Interpersonal Relations**: non-technical. It focuses on personal growth.
- **D. Weinstein and Fantini Model**: non-technical. It is a humanistic model about the learner's concerns.
- **E. Taba's Model**: technical-scientific. It is a step-by-step "grassroots" model.

So A, C and D are correct.

questions.question_md: SWAYAM is a platform that facilitates hosting of all the courses, taught in classrooms from ----- to be accessed by anyone, anywhere at any time.
options: class 7ᵗʰ till the post- doctoral degree
questions.explanation:
SWAYAM is the Government of India's free online course platform. Its official aim is to host courses taught in classrooms from **class 9 till post-graduation**. Anyone can use these courses at any place and at any time.

School courses on SWAYAM come from NIOS and NCERT. Higher education courses come from bodies such as UGC, CEC and IITs.

The other options give the wrong start class or the wrong end level.

questions.question_md: Which of the following scales of measurement contains an absolute zero?
questions.explanation:
An **absolute zero** (true zero) means "none of the quantity". For example, 0 kg means no weight at all.

- **Nominal** scale: only names or groups. It has no zero.
- **Ordinal** scale: only rank order. It has no true zero.
- **Interval** scale: equal gaps, but the zero is arbitrary (chosen by people). For example, 0 °C does not mean "no heat".
- **Ratio** scale: equal gaps and a true zero. Examples are height, weight and income.

Only the ratio scale has a true zero. So you can say "twice as heavy" only on a ratio scale.

questions.question_md: Robustness is concerned with
questions.explanation:
**Robustness** means that a result stays the same under different conditions. These conditions can be different samples, places, times or methods.

If a result is robust, we can apply it outside the original study. This is the idea of **external validity** (how well results generalise to other people and settings).

Internal validity is about cause and effect inside the study. Measurement and construct validity are about whether a tool measures the right concept. These are not the main concern of robustness.

questions.question_md: A sampling technique in which initially sampled respondents contact and recruit others in their social network for participation in the research is called
questions.explanation:
In **snowball sampling**, the researcher first finds a few respondents. These respondents then contact and recruit other people from their social network. The sample grows like a rolling snowball.

Researchers use it for hidden or hard-to-reach groups, such as drug users.

- Convenience sampling: the researcher takes people who are easy to reach.
- Quota sampling: the researcher fills fixed numbers for each group.
- Systematic sampling: the researcher picks every k-th person from a list.

None of these three uses referrals from respondents.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following components of a research paper written in APA style, in correct order

A. Tables

B. Abstract

C. References

D. Figures

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
APA style (American Psychological Association) gives a fixed order for the parts of a paper:

1. Title page
2. **Abstract**
3. Main text
4. **References**
5. **Tables**
6. **Figures**
7. Appendices

So the order of the given parts is Abstract, References, Tables, Figures (B, C, A, D).

In APA style, tables and figures come after the reference list. So options that put tables before references are wrong.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** Debriefing of participants takes place at the beginning of a study.

**Statement II:** Deception is the practice of giving false information to research participants about some aspect of the study.

In light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate** answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is incorrect.** Debriefing takes place at the **end** of a study. The researcher tells participants the true aim of the study. The researcher also explains any deception and answers questions.
- **Statement II is correct.** Deception means giving participants false or incomplete information about some part of the study. Researchers use it only when it is necessary. They must then explain it in the debriefing.

So Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.question_md: The linear model of communication can be described as
questions.explanation:
A **linear model** of communication shows a one-way flow. The sender sends a message, and the receiver only receives it. There is no feedback from the receiver. Examples are the Shannon–Weaver model and Lasswell's model.

The sender has all the control, and the receiver is passive. So we can call this model **authoritarian** (top-down).

- "Participatory" describes two-way, interactive models.
- "Liberal" and "confessional" are not normal terms for a model of communication.

questions.question_md: Studying the practical use of signs and their impact on everyday life is called
questions.notes: Dropped in the official NTA final answer key (marks awarded to all who attempted).
questions.explanation:
Charles Morris divided semiotics (the study of signs) into three branches:

- **Syntactics**: the relation of signs to other signs (the rules of form).
- **Semantics**: the relation of signs to their meanings.
- **Pragmatics**: the relation of signs to their users. It studies how people use signs in real life and how signs affect them.

The question asks about the practical use of signs in everyday life. So **Pragmatics** is the best answer. Linguistics is the whole study of language, not one branch of semiotics.

NTA dropped this question and gave marks to all candidates. The official reason is not known. A possible reason is a problem in the wording or in the Hindi version.

questions.question_md:
What factors are responsible for ineffective listening in a classroom?

A. Contextualisation of message

B. Attention-triggers

C. Physical or mental fatigue

D. Lack of incentive

E. Insufficient preparation

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Ineffective listening means the student does not hear or understand the message well. Check each factor:

- **A. Contextualisation of message**: helps listening. A message linked to a known context is easier to follow.
- **B. Attention-triggers**: help listening. Things such as questions or examples catch attention.
- **C. Physical or mental fatigue**: a barrier. A tired student cannot focus.
- **D. Lack of incentive**: a barrier. The student sees no reason to listen.
- **E. Insufficient preparation**: a barrier. The student lacks the background to follow the lesson.

So C, D and E cause ineffective listening. Options with A or B are wrong.

questions.question_md:
The mechanical model of mass communication is characterised by

A. Multiple ways flow

B. One-way flow

C. From one-to-many

D. Can be anonymous

E. Active audience

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
The **mechanical model** (transmission model) treats mass communication like a machine. A message moves from a source to a receiver.

- **A. Multiple ways flow**: no. The flow is not interactive.
- **B. One-way flow**: yes. The message goes only from the sender to the audience.
- **C. From one-to-many**: yes. One source sends to a large audience.
- **D. Can be anonymous**: yes. The audience is large and unknown to the sender.
- **E. Active audience**: no. This model treats the audience as passive.

So B, C and D are correct.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** In the earlier days of mass communication, content creators played an important role in the society.

**Statement II:** They represented and defined reality by authoring narratives to explain to the audience.

In light of the above statements, choose the *correct* answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** In the early days of mass media, only a few people created content. They were journalists, writers and broadcasters. They had great influence on society.
- **Statement II is true.** These creators wrote narratives (stories and explanations) for the audience. In this way, they decided how the audience saw reality. The audience could not easily answer back.

So both statements are true. Today, social media lets audiences also create content. But the question is about the earlier days.

questions.question_md: A family comprises of 3 persons A, B and C. The age of A is four times that of B. In four years time, A will be 40 years old. The age of C was half the age of A four years ago. Find the present age of B and C (in years), respectively.
questions.explanation:
Find A first. In four years, A will be 40. So A is now 40 − 4 = **36**.

- B: A is four times B. So B = 36 ÷ 4 = **9**.
- C: Read the sentence as "four years ago, C's age was half of A's age". Four years ago, A was 32. So C was 16 at that time. Now C is 16 + 4 = **20**.

So B and C are 9 and 20 years old.

The tempting answer is 9 and 16. It takes 16 as C's present age. But the verb "was" shows that 16 was C's age four years ago.

questions.question_md: While pointing towards a picture, a man says "This girl is the wife of the grand-son of my mother". How is the man related to the girl in the picture?
questions.explanation:
Solve the relation step by step.

- The man's mother's grandson is a son of the man (or of his brother or sister).
- The simplest reading is that the grandson is the **man's son**.
- The girl is the wife of the man's son. So she is the man's **daughter-in-law**.

So the man is the girl's **father-in-law**.

The other options do not fit. A brother or brother-in-law is in the same generation as the girl. The man is one generation above her. He is not her father, because she is the wife of his son.

questions.question_md: A man starts from a point X and walks 20 meters to reach a point Y in the north-east direction. He then turns right and walks 20 meters again to reach a point Z. How far is the point Z from point X?
questions.explanation:
Draw the path.

- From X, the man walks 20 m **north-east** to Y.
- He turns right. Right of north-east is **south-east**. He walks 20 m to Z.

North-east and south-east are at 90° to each other. So X, Y and Z make a right-angled triangle with the right angle at Y.

By Pythagoras' rule: XZ = √(20² + 20²) = √800 = **20√2 m**.

The answer 20 m would be correct only if the angle at Y were 60°. That is not the case here.

questions.question_md: A man invests some amount of money for some time period. This amount of money becomes ₹4500 at the rate of 7% simple interest. However, if invested at 5% per annum simple interest, the same amount becomes ₹3500. Find out the amount of money and the time period.
questions.explanation:
Use Amount = P + (P × R × T ÷ 100). P is the money invested and T is the time in years.

- At 7%: P + 7PT/100 = 4500.
- At 5%: P + 5PT/100 = 3500.

Subtract the second line from the first: 2PT/100 = 1000. So **PT = 50,000**.

Put this in the second line: P + (5 × 50,000)/100 = 3500. So P + 2500 = 3500, and **P = ₹1000**.

Then T = 50,000 ÷ 1000 = **50 years**.

Check at 7%: interest = 1000 × 7 × 50 ÷ 100 = 3500. Amount = 4500. This is correct.

questions.question_md:
What number should replace question mark (?) in the series given below:

12, 12, 24, 72, 288, ?, 8640
questions.explanation:
Each term is the previous term multiplied by the next whole number.

- 12 × 1 = 12
- 12 × 2 = 24
- 24 × 3 = 72
- 72 × 4 = 288
- 288 × 5 = **1440**
- 1440 × 6 = 8640

The last step confirms the answer, because 1440 × 6 = 8640. The other values do not give 8640 when multiplied by 6.

questions.question_md:
If 'No metals are gases' is given as false, then which of the following statements can be immediately inferred to be true?

A. All gases are metals.

B. All metals are gases.

C. Some metals are not gases.

D. Some metals are gases.

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
"No metals are gases" is an **E** proposition (universal negative). It is given as **false**.

Use the square of opposition:

- **D. Some metals are gases** (I) is the contradictory of E. If E is false, I must be **true**.
- **B. All metals are gases** (A): when E is false, A is undetermined (we do not know).
- **C. Some metals are not gases** (O): also undetermined.
- **A. All gases are metals**: this changes the subject and the predicate. We cannot infer it.

So only D is certainly true.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements are so related that they can not both be false, although they may both be true?

A. All metals are gases.

B. Some metals are gases.

C. Some metals are not gases.

D. No metals are gases.

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Two statements that **cannot both be false but can both be true** are **subcontraries**. On the square of opposition, the I and O propositions are subcontraries.

- **B. Some metals are gases** is I.
- **C. Some metals are not gases** is O.

So B and C are the answer.

- A and D (All… / No…) are **contraries**. They cannot both be true, but they can both be false.
- A and B are in **subalternation**. Both can be false.
- C and D are also in subalternation. Both can be false.

questions.question_md: "The last time I stretched my arms first and my legs second, I won my race, So that stretching sequence must have increased my speed." Which informal fallacy is committed in the above statement?
questions.explanation:
The speaker says that the stretching came first and the win came after. Then he says the stretching caused the win. This is the **post hoc** fallacy ("after this, therefore because of this"). An event that only comes before another event is not proof of cause.

- **Hasty generalisation** draws a general rule from a few cases. Here the main error is about cause, not about a general rule.
- **False alternative** gives only two choices when more exist.
- **Slippery slope** says one step will lead to a chain of bad results.

Neither of the last two fits the argument.

questions.question_md: Which of the following statements is logically equivalent to the statement -' No metals are gases'?
questions.explanation:
"No metals are gases" is an **E** proposition. An E proposition can be **converted** simply. You swap the subject and the predicate, and the meaning stays the same.

So "No gases are metals" is logically equivalent.

- "All metals are non-gases" (the obverse) is also equivalent, but it is not an option.
- "No metals are non-gases" means "All metals are gases". That is the opposite idea.
- "All non-gases are non-metals" is not equivalent. Some non-gases (for example, solid metals) are metals.
- "All non-metals are gases" does not follow at all.
