groups.md:
The table given below shows the distribution percentage of number of candidates qualifying a Common Entrance Test (CET) in six cities A-F during the year 2020 and 2021, along with the ratio of males (M) to females (F) among the qualified candidates. The total number of qualified candidates in all the six cities together during 2020 and 2021 are 3800 and 4600 respectively. Based on the data in the table, answer the question that follows:

**City-wise Distribution of CET Qualified Candidates.**

| City | 2020: (Distribution % of Qualified Candidates | 2020: Ratio M:F | 2021: (Distribution % of Qualified Candidates | 2021: Ratio M:F |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 13% | 8:5 | 24% | 5:7 |
| B | 27% | 11:8 | 15% | 12:11 |
| C | 11% | 7:4 | 23% | 15:8 |
| D | 20% | 2:3 | 17% | 8:9 |
| E | 8% | 5:3 | 8% | 1:3 |
| F | 21% | 13:8 | 13% | 5:8 |

Read the passage and answer the question given below:

Alternatives are not lacking in the world. What is indeed missing is an alternative thinking of alternatives, whenever it is said that there ar[e] very interesting things happening in Asia, Africa and Latin America, the Western answer is that developed countries do not have same problems. As such, the West does not need their kinds of solutions. There are two inferences from this: First, the understanding of the world is much broader than the western understanding of the world. This means that the progressive transformation of the world may als[o] occur in ways not foreseen by western thinking. It includes critical western thinking. Second, the diversity of the world is infinite. It is a diversity that encompasses very distinct modes of being, thinking and feeling: ways of conceiving of time and the relations among huma[n] beings and between humans and non-humans, ways of facing the past and the future and of collectively organizing life, the production of goods and services, as well as leisure. This immensity of alternatives of life, comforts and interaction with the world is largely wasted because the theories and concepts developed in the global North and employed in the entire academic world do not identify such alternatives. When they do, they do not valorize them as being valid contributions towards constructing a better society. The knowledge o[f] the south is dubbed as outmoded and considered as no knowledge at all.

questions.question_md: The difference between the number of male candidates qualified from City-B in 2020 and City-A in 2021 is
questions.explanation:
Find each group of candidates first. Then find the males with the M:F ratio.

- City-B in 2020: 27% of 3800 = 1026. The ratio is 11:8, so males = 1026 × 11/19 = **594**.
- City-A in 2021: 24% of 4600 = 1104. The ratio is 5:7, so there are 12 parts. Males = 1104 × 5/12 = **460**.

Difference = 594 − 460 = **134**.

Use the correct year for each city. The two years have different totals (3800 and 4600). If you mix them up, you get one of the wrong options.

questions.question_md: The ratio of number of females qualified from City-D in 2020 to that of City-E in 2021 is
questions.explanation:
Find the females in each city with the M:F ratio.

- City-D in 2020: 20% of 3800 = 760. The ratio is 2:3, so females = 760 × 3/5 = **456**.
- City-E in 2021: 8% of 4600 = 368. The ratio is 1:3, so females = 368 × 3/4 = **276**.

Ratio = 456 : 276. Divide both numbers by 12. The result is **38 : 23**.

The other ratios do not come from these two numbers. For example, 35:23 would need 420 females in City-D.

questions.question_md: The number of females qualified from City-F in 2020 is ________% of the number of candidates qualified from City-E in the same yea[r]
questions.notes: The letter in [brackets] is cut off at the page edge in the source.
questions.explanation:
Both numbers are from 2020, so use the total 3800.

- City-F: 21% of 3800 = 798 candidates. The ratio M:F is 13:8, so females = 798 × 8/21 = **304**.
- City-E: 8% of 3800 = **304** candidates.

Percentage = (304 ÷ 304) × 100 = **100%**.

The two numbers are equal. The options 60, 75 and 80 would need fewer females in City-F than candidates in City-E.

questions.question_md: The number of females qualified from City-B in 2021 is approximately ________% more than the number of males qualified from City-E in the year 2020
questions.explanation:
Find the two numbers first.

- Females in City-B, 2021: 15% of 4600 = 690. The ratio is 12:11, so females = 690 × 11/23 = **330**.
- Males in City-E, 2020: 8% of 3800 = 304. The ratio is 5:3, so males = 304 × 5/8 = **190**.

"How much % more" uses the smaller number (190) as the base.

- Difference = 330 − 190 = 140.
- Percentage = (140 ÷ 190) × 100 ≈ **73.68%**.

If you divide by 330 instead, you get about 42%. That is not an option, so the base must be 190.

questions.question_md: The average of the number of females qualified from all the six cities together in 2021 is
questions.explanation:
All numbers are for 2021, so use the total 4600. Find the females in each city.

- A: 24% = 1104; females = 1104 × 7/12 = 644
- B: 15% = 690; females = 690 × 11/23 = 330
- C: 23% = 1058; females = 1058 × 8/23 = 368
- D: 17% = 782; females = 782 × 9/17 = 414
- E: 8% = 368; females = 368 × 3/4 = 276
- F: 13% = 598; females = 598 × 8/13 = 368

Total females = 644 + 330 + 368 + 414 + 276 + 368 = 2400.

Average = 2400 ÷ 6 = **400**.

A small error in one city changes the total. Check each ratio carefully: the second number in M:F is the female part.

questions.question_md: In MOOCs (Massive Open Online Courses), an initiative under NME-ICT Programme, the fourth quadrant is related to:
questions.explanation:
MOOCs on the SWAYAM platform use a four-quadrant approach. Each quadrant is one part of a course.

- Quadrant I: e-Tutorial (video lectures).
- Quadrant II: e-Content (reading material, PDFs, case studies).
- Quadrant III: Web Resources (links, articles, further reading).
- Quadrant IV: **Self-Assessment** (quizzes, tests, assignments).

So the fourth quadrant is self-assessment. The other three options are the first three quadrants. They are not the fourth.

questions.question_md:
Match List I with List II

| LIST I (Type of learning theory) | LIST II (Theorist) |
|---|---|
| A. Behavioral theory of learning | I. Albert Bandura |
| B. Individual constructivist theory of learning | II. Lev Vygotsky |
| C. Social constructivist theory of learning | III. J. Piaget |
| D. Social cognitive theory of learning | IV. B.F. Skinner |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Match each theory with its main thinker.

- **A. Behavioral theory – IV. B.F. Skinner.** Skinner explained learning through operant conditioning, reward and reinforcement.
- **B. Individual constructivist theory – III. J. Piaget.** Piaget said each child builds knowledge through his or her own mental stages.
- **C. Social constructivist theory – II. Lev Vygotsky.** Vygotsky said learning comes from social interaction, for example in the zone of proximal development.
- **D. Social cognitive theory – I. Albert Bandura.** Bandura showed that people learn by watching models.

The other options mix up Piaget and Vygotsky, or Bandura and Skinner.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In explicit long term memory bits of information may be stored and interrelated in terms of propositional networks.

Statement II: Implicit long term/ memories are out-of-awareness memories that can't affect thinking and behavior.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is icorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.notes: Option 4 'icorrect' and 'long term/ memories' are as printed in the source.
questions.explanation:
Long-term memory has two main types.

- **Statement I is correct.** Explicit (conscious) memory stores facts and meanings. Psychologists describe this store as a network of linked ideas, called propositional networks.
- **Statement II is incorrect.** Implicit memories are out of awareness, but they **do** affect thinking and behaviour. Examples are skills, habits and priming. Priming means that an earlier experience changes a later response without our knowledge.

So the first statement is true and the second is false. The word "can't" makes Statement II wrong.

questions.question_md: A teacher is preparing a course of science. He/She wants to add an exercise that promotes collaboration and problem solving among learners. What kind of group should he/she form?
questions.explanation:
The teacher wants collaboration and problem solving. In a **student-centric group**, the learners lead the work. They share ideas, discuss and solve the problem together. The teacher only guides.

- An independent student assignment has no collaboration.
- A teacher-centric group depends on the teacher. Students mostly listen and follow.
- A social group is a general term. It does not have a learning or problem-solving purpose.

So the student-centric group fits the aim best.

questions.question_md: A teacher divided the students of a class into four small groups and in each group three students are present. They have to complete a project in online mode by adding all the related material. Which tool is most appropriate according to you?
questions.explanation:
The students work in small groups. They must collect related material online and build one project together. **Padlet** is an online board for this purpose. Many users can add text, links, images and videos to the same board at the same time.

- A camera only takes photos or videos.
- Quizzes test learners. They do not help to collect material.
- Screencast-O-Matic records the computer screen. It is useful for video lessons, but not for shared group work.

So Padlet is the most suitable tool.

questions.question_md: One of the characteristics of probability sampling is
questions.explanation:
In probability sampling, every member of the population has a known chance of selection. The researcher usually selects members by **random selection**. Examples are simple random, stratified and cluster sampling.

- Population bias and sampling bias are errors. Probability sampling tries to reduce bias.
- Accidental selection is a non-probability method. The researcher picks whoever is easy to reach. It is also called convenience sampling.

So random selection is the key characteristic.

questions.question_md: Covert research in ethnography is beset with
questions.explanation:
In covert ethnography, the researcher hides his or her identity and purpose from the people under study. The people do not know that someone is studying them.

This raises **ethical issues**:

- There is no informed consent.
- The researcher deceives the group.
- The research can harm privacy and trust.

Personal, political or historical problems can also happen. But the main criticism of covert research in methods books is ethical. So "ethical issues" is the best answer.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are characteristics of qualitative interview?

A. It is less structured.

B. It reflects researcher's concerns.

C. The interview is allowed to ramble.

D. The interview has standardized questions.

E. It is flexible in approach.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the questions given below:
questions.explanation:
A qualitative interview is open and loose. Check each feature.

- **A. Less structured – yes.** The interviewer does not follow a fixed list.
- **B. Reflects the researcher's concerns – no.** This is true of a quantitative interview. A qualitative interview focuses on the interviewee's point of view.
- **C. Allowed to ramble – yes.** Rambling can show what the interviewee thinks is important.
- **D. Standardized questions – no.** Standard questions belong to structured (quantitative) interviews.
- **E. Flexible – yes.** The interviewer can change the order and add new questions.

So A, C and E are correct. Options with B or D include a feature of the quantitative interview.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following factors must be taken into account in quantitative research?

A. Measurement

B. Causality

C. Replication

D. Exclusion of statistical analysis

E. Less importance to standarisation

Choose the most appropriate answer from the questions given below:
questions.explanation:
Quantitative research uses numbers. Its main concerns are measurement, causality, generalization and replication.

- **A. Measurement – yes.** The researcher measures concepts with numbers.
- **B. Causality – yes.** The researcher tries to explain why things happen, that is, cause and effect.
- **C. Replication – yes.** Another researcher must be able to repeat the study and check the result.
- **D. Exclusion of statistical analysis – no.** Quantitative research depends on statistics.
- **E. Less importance to standardisation – no.** Quantitative research gives high importance to standard methods.

So only A, B and C are correct.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Gaining access to a public or social setting is an important issue in ethnographic research.

Statement II: There is no distinction between overt and covert ethnography in terms of access and participation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** In ethnography, the researcher must first get access to the group or setting. This is often difficult. Gatekeepers, who control entry, can refuse access. So access is a central issue.
- **Statement II is false.** Overt and covert ethnography differ clearly in access and participation. In overt research, the group knows the researcher's role and must agree. In covert research, the researcher hides the role. So covert access avoids permission but raises ethical problems.

So Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

questions.question_md: In Communication, metanyms reflect
questions.notes: 'metanyms' is as printed in the source (the Hindi version reads मेटानिमस). Dropped in the NTA final answer key.
questions.explanation:
The printed word "metanyms" is a misspelling of **metonyms**. A metonym uses one part or one linked thing to stand for the whole. For example, a news photo of one burning bus can stand for a whole riot.

In semiotics (the study of signs), writers such as John Fiske say metonyms are strong carriers of **reality**. The audience takes the part as a true sample of the real event. A metaphor works differently. It moves meaning to another plane, which is closer to imagination.

So "Reality" is the best answer. Artificiality, fantasy and hidden secrets do not describe how metonyms work.

NTA dropped this question and gave marks to all. The spelling error probably made the term unclear. The idea is also a narrow point of theory, so candidates could challenge it.

questions.question_md: Mass media mostly operate in
questions.explanation:
The **public sphere** is the space where people discuss common matters and form public opinion. Jürgen Habermas made this idea well known. Mass media such as newspapers, radio and television send messages to large public audiences. So they mostly work in the public sphere.

- The personal sphere covers private life and one-to-one talk.
- The bureaucratic sphere covers government offices and official rules.
- "Ethical sphere" is not a usual term for where media work.

questions.question_md:
The criteria for good public service communication by media are:

A. Limit on audience action and reaction

B. Subjective slant

C. Evenhandedness

D. Avoidance of rancour

E. Separating facts from opinion

Choose the most appropriate answer from the questions given below:
questions.explanation:
Good public service communication should be fair and factual. Check each item.

- **A. Limit on audience action and reaction – no.** Public service media should invite audience response, not limit it.
- **B. Subjective slant – no.** A personal bias goes against fairness.
- **C. Evenhandedness – yes.** The media should treat all sides equally.
- **D. Avoidance of rancour – yes.** The media should avoid bitter and hostile language.
- **E. Separating facts from opinion – yes.** Readers must know what is a fact and what is a view.

So C, D and E are correct. Every other option includes A or B.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A large portion of mediated cultural transmission involves traditions, language, beliefs, attitudes and values from one generation to another.

Statement II: Such a process will contribute for the unconscious cultural development of individuals in the society.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** Media carry much of a society's culture. They pass traditions, language, beliefs, attitudes and values from one generation to the next. This is cultural transmission through media.
- **Statement II is true.** People absorb this culture slowly and often without noticing it. So media add to the unconscious cultural development of individuals. This is part of socialization, which means learning the ways of one's society.

Both statements are true, and Statement II follows from Statement I.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The circular model of communication does not favour feedback.

Statement II: The linear model of communication demands continuity of communication and enables immediate feedback.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** The circular model (for example, Osgood–Schramm) shows communication as a two-way cycle. The receiver also becomes a sender. So this model is built on feedback.
- **Statement II is false.** The linear model (for example, Shannon–Weaver or Lasswell) shows a one-way flow from sender to receiver. It ends when the message arrives. It has no continuity and no immediate feedback.

The two statements swap the features of the two models. So both are false.

questions.question_md:
Find the next term in the series given below:

2, 6, 12, 20.....
questions.explanation:
Look at the differences between the terms.

- 6 − 2 = 4
- 12 − 6 = 6
- 20 − 12 = 8

The difference grows by 2 each time. The next difference is 10. So the next term is 20 + 10 = **30**.

Another way: each term is n × (n + 1). The terms are 1×2, 2×3, 3×4, 4×5. The next term is 5×6 = 30.

24 and 28 come from wrong differences (4 and 8). 36 is 6×6, which does not fit the pattern.

questions.question_md: 12 Men are assigned a job to be finished in 30 days. After 10 days it is observed that only 1/6<sup>th</sup> of the job is completed. How many extra men are required to be deployed to do the rest of the job so that the job is completed within scheduled time?
questions.explanation:
Use man-days (men × days) as the unit of work.

- In 10 days, 12 men do 12 × 10 = 120 man-days.
- This is 1/6 of the job. So the whole job = 120 × 6 = 720 man-days.
- Work left = 720 − 120 = 600 man-days.
- Days left = 30 − 10 = 20 days.
- Men needed = 600 ÷ 20 = 30 men.

Extra men = 30 − 12 = **18**.

The question asks for **extra** men, not total men. 30 is the total, so subtract the 12 who are already working.

questions.question_md: A batsman has a certain average of runs for 16 innings. In the 17<sup>th</sup> inning he makes a score of 85 runs, thus increasing his average by 3 runs. What is average of the batsman after 17<sup>th</sup> innings?
questions.explanation:
Let the new average after 17 innings be x. The old average after 16 innings is then x − 3.

- Old total runs = 16 × (x − 3) = 16x − 48.
- New total runs = 16x − 48 + 85 = 16x + 37.
- New total also = 17x.

So 17x = 16x + 37, and x = **37**.

Check: the old average is 34. The old total is 16 × 34 = 544. The new total is 544 + 85 = 629. Then 629 ÷ 17 = 37.

34 is the old average, not the new one. 40 and 45 do not satisfy the equation.

questions.question_md: Find a single discount equivalent to a series discount of 20%, 10% and 5%
questions.explanation:
Series discounts apply one after another, not by simple addition. Start with a price of 100.

- After 20% off: 100 × 0.80 = 80
- After 10% off: 80 × 0.90 = 72
- After 5% off: 72 × 0.95 = 68.40

The final price is 68.40. So the total discount = 100 − 68.40 = **31.6%**.

Simple addition gives 20 + 10 + 5 = 35%, but that is wrong. Each later discount applies to a smaller price. So the total is less than 35%. The options 30%, 30.6% and 32% come from calculation errors.

questions.question_md: A man walks 1km towards east and then turns southwards and walks 5 km. Again he turns to east and walks 2 kms. After this he turns to the north and walks 9 kms. How far is the man from his starting point?
questions.explanation:
Add the moves in each direction.

- East: 1 km + 2 km = 3 km east.
- North–south: 5 km south, then 9 km north. Net = 9 − 5 = 4 km north.

The man is 3 km east and 4 km north of the start. These two sides form a right angle. Use the Pythagoras theorem:

Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = **5 km**.

7 km is 3 + 4, but that adds the sides instead of using the straight line.

questions.question_md: Which informal fallacy is committed in the following statements- " Your argument that I should stop stealing chocolates from the corner store is no good. You told me yourself just a month ago that you, too, stole chocolates when you were a kid".
questions.explanation:
The speaker rejects the argument because of the arguer's own past behaviour. This is **ad hominem**, which means "against the person". This special form is called *tu quoque* ("you too").

The arguer's past theft does not make the argument wrong. Stealing is still wrong.

- Red herring: the speaker brings in an unrelated topic to distract.
- Strawman: the speaker twists the opponent's argument into a weaker one and attacks that.
- Missing the point: the premises support a different conclusion.

Here the speaker attacks the person, so ad hominem fits best.

questions.question_md: Which of the following statements is contrapositive of "All whales are mammals"?
questions.explanation:
To form the contrapositive of an A proposition ("All S are P"), take two steps:

1. Swap the subject and the predicate.
2. Replace each term with its complement (add "non-").

"All whales are mammals" becomes "**All non-mammals are non-whales**." For A propositions, the contrapositive is valid. Anything that is not a mammal cannot be a whale.

- "Some mammals are whales" is the converse by limitation.
- "All mammals are whales" is an invalid simple converse.
- "Some whales are mammals" is the subaltern, not the contrapositive.

questions.question_md: Which of the following is contradictory to the statement- "No birds are mammals"?
questions.explanation:
"No birds are mammals" is an **E** proposition (universal negative). In the square of opposition, the contradictory of E is **I** (particular affirmative). Contradictory statements always have opposite truth values.

So the contradictory is "**Some birds are mammals**."

- "Some birds are not mammals" is an O proposition. It is the subaltern of E.
- "All birds are mammals" is an A proposition. It is the contrary of E. Both can be false together.
- "All mammals are birds" has different terms, so it is not part of this square.

questions.question_md: If the statement "Some animals are birds" is given as true. Which of the following statements can be immediately inferred to be false?
questions.explanation:
"Some animals are birds" is an **I** proposition. Its contradictory is the **E** proposition "No animals are birds." When I is true, its contradictory E must be false.

- "All animals are birds" (A) is undetermined. A true I does not tell us if A is true.
- "Some animals are not birds" (O) is the subcontrary of I. Both can be true, so O is undetermined.
- "All animals cannot fly" has new terms. It does not follow from the given statement.

So only "No animals are birds" is surely false.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to Classical Indian School of logic (Nyaya) the middle term must be present in the minor term.

Statement II: According to Nyaya School the middle term must be absent in all negative instances in which the major term is absent.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
In Nyāya logic, a valid middle term (hetu, the reason) has five marks. Two of them are:

- **Pakṣadharmatā:** the middle term must be present in the minor term (pakṣa, the subject). In "The hill has fire because it has smoke", smoke must be on the hill. So **Statement I is correct.**
- **Vipakṣāsattva:** the middle term must be absent in all negative instances (vipakṣa). Those are cases where the major term (sādhya) is absent. For example, there is no smoke in a lake, where there is no fire. So **Statement II is correct.**

Both statements describe real Nyāya rules.

questions.question_md: In 1965, Gardon Moore, Co-founder of Intel, made a prediction about the future of computer processing. What does his prediction, know[n] as Moore's Law, say?
options: As technology continues to advance, computer chips will become obsolete.
Computer processing power will double every 18 months to two year.
There will eventually be no need for transistors in high tech electronics.
As the number of transistors increases, computer processing power will be reduced by half every two years.
questions.notes: The letter in [brackets] is cut off at the page edge in the source. 'Gardon Moore' is as printed.
questions.explanation:
Gordon Moore predicted that the number of transistors on a chip would double at regular intervals. In 1965 he said every year. In 1975 he changed it to every two years. More transistors give more processing power. So people often state Moore's Law as: **processing power doubles every 18 months to two years.**

- Chips have not become obsolete. They keep improving.
- Transistors are still the basic part of chips.
- Power does not fall by half. The law predicts growth, not decline.

questions.question_md: The action of illegally installing malicious code which redirects a person to a fraudulent website with the purpose of obtaining that person's bank details is called
questions.explanation:
**Pharming** installs malicious code on a computer or on a server. The code redirects the user to a fake website, even when the user types the correct address. The fake site then collects bank details.

- Phishing uses fake emails. The user must click a link in the email.
- Spamming sends unwanted bulk messages.
- Smishing is phishing through SMS text messages.

The key words are "installing malicious code" and "redirects". These words describe pharming, not phishing.

questions.question_md:
Both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth offer wireless communication between devices. Bluetooth is useful when

A. Transferring data between two or more devices which are less than 30 meters apart.

B. The speed of data transmission is not critical.

C. Using high bandwidth applications (for example, sending music files from a mobile phone to a headset).

Choose the most appropriate answer from the questions given below
questions.explanation:
Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology with low bandwidth.

- **A – yes.** Bluetooth works when devices are close, usually within about 30 m or less.
- **B – yes.** Bluetooth is slower than Wi-Fi. It suits jobs where speed is not critical.
- **C – no.** Bluetooth suits **low**-bandwidth jobs, such as sending music to a headset. High-bandwidth jobs need Wi-Fi.

So only A and B are correct. Statement C calls the headset example "high bandwidth". That is the error in it.

questions.question_md:
Match List I with List II

| LIST I (Question) | LIST II (Value) |
|---|---|
| A. If the broadband data download rate is 40 megabits per second, then how many seconds will it takes to download a 60 megabytes file? | I. 64000 |
| B. Base -10 (denary) value of the binary number: 1000001 | II. 12 |
| C. Number of 8 megabyte files that can be stored on a backup memory device having 500 gigabyte of storage. | III. 17 |
| D. What hexadecimal value is obtained when the two hexadecimal digits B and C are added together? | IV. 65 |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Solve each part.

- **A – II (12).** 60 megabytes = 60 × 8 = 480 megabits. Time = 480 ÷ 40 = 12 seconds.
- **B – IV (65).** Binary 1000001 = 64 + 1 = 65.
- **C – I (64000).** 500 GB = 500 × 1024 MB = 512000 MB. Number of files = 512000 ÷ 8 = 64000.
- **D – III (17).** B = 11 and C = 12 in decimal. 11 + 12 = 23. In hexadecimal, 23 = 1 × 16 + 7, which is written as 17.

So the match is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III. In part A, remember that 1 byte = 8 bits. If you forget this, you get 1.5 seconds.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: .mp4 and .gif are two file extensions used with files containing moving images.

Statement II: .rar and .zip are two file extensions used with files containing compressed data.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is [false] but Statement II is [true].
questions.notes: In the English source, option 4 repeats option 3 ('Statement I is true but Statement II is false.'). The words in [brackets] are corrected from the Hindi version of option 4 (कथन I असत्य है, लेकिन कथन II सत्य है).
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is true.** .mp4 is a video format. .gif can store animated images, which are short moving pictures. So both extensions can hold moving images.
- **Statement II is true.** .rar and .zip are archive formats. They compress one or more files into a smaller file.

So both statements are true.

Some students think .gif holds only still images. GIF files can hold several frames, so they can show animation.

questions.question_md: Which of the following activities has contributed maximum to global warming?
questions.explanation:
Carbon dioxide is the main greenhouse gas. Most of it comes from **burning fossil fuels**: coal, oil and natural gas. Power plants, transport and industry burn these fuels. The IPCC reports name fossil fuel combustion as the largest source of human greenhouse gas emissions.

- Deforestation adds CO₂ and removes carbon sinks, but it adds less.
- Agriculture adds methane and nitrous oxide, but it adds less in total.
- Industrial processes such as cement making add some CO₂. Their share is also smaller.

questions.question_md: A 30 dB increase in noise pollution level represents:
questions.explanation:
The decibel (dB) scale is logarithmic. Each 10 dB increase means a 10-fold increase in sound intensity.

- +10 dB = 10 times
- +20 dB = 10 × 10 = 100 times
- +30 dB = 10 × 10 × 10 = **1000 times**

The formula is: intensity ratio = 10^(dB change ÷ 10) = 10^3 = 1000.

"30-fold" treats the scale as linear, which is wrong. "100-fold" is the value for 20 dB.

questions.question_md: Turbidity, one of the important water quality parameters, is measured in
questions.explanation:
Turbidity means the cloudiness of water. Suspended particles such as clay, silt and microbes cause it. Scientists measure turbidity with a nephelometer. This instrument measures the light that the particles scatter. The unit is **NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Unit)**.

- Color units measure the colour of water, not cloudiness.
- pH units measure acidity.
- µg/m³ is a unit for the concentration of air pollutants, such as PM2.5.

questions.question_md: In case of nuclear energy, the objective of enrichment process is
options: Separation of Uranium from its ores
questions.explanation:
Natural uranium has about 99.3% U-238 and only about 0.7% **U-235**. Only U-235 is fissile. That means slow neutrons can split it and keep a chain reaction going. Most reactors need about 3–5% U-235. So **enrichment** raises the share of U-235.

- Separating uranium from its ore is mining and milling. That step comes before enrichment.
- Enrichment lowers the share of U-238. It does not raise it.
- A moderator (water or graphite) slows neutrons. It has no link to enrichment.

questions.question_md: International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched in the year
questions.explanation:
India and France launched the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** on 30 November **2015**. They launched it in Paris at COP21, the UN climate conference.

The ISA promotes solar energy, mainly in countries that get a lot of sunshine. Its headquarters is in Gurugram, India.

The other years match later events. For example, the ISA Framework Agreement opened for signing in 2016 and came into force in 2017. The founding conference was in 2018. These years are not the launch year.

questions.question_md: National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) is under:
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
All India Council for Technical Education
questions.explanation:
The Government of India set up the **National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET)** in 2018. It regulates vocational education and training. It also sets standards for the bodies that award skill certificates.

NCVET works under the **Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)**. It merged two older bodies, the NCVT and the NSDA.

- The Ministry of Education looks after school and higher education.
- UGC and AICTE regulate universities and technical education. They do not control NCVET.

questions.question_md: A section of the Muslim Community opened a number of Azad schools in Uttar Pradesh and led by Maulana Mohammad Ali in 1920 established the Jamia Milia Islamia or Muslim National University in which of the following Indian Cities?
questions.explanation:
During the Non-Cooperation and Khilafat movements (1920), many nationalists left government-aided institutions. Leaders such as Maulana Mohammad Ali then set up the **Jamia Millia Islamia** (Muslim National University). They founded it at **Aligarh** in October 1920.

In 1925, the Jamia moved from Aligarh to Delhi. Today it is a central university in Delhi. This is why Delhi is the most tempting wrong option. But the question asks where the founders set it up in 1920. That place was Aligarh.

Hyderabad and Lucknow have no link to its founding.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following were considered as Vedangas in the ancient education system of India?

A. Metrics

B. Grammar

C. Phonetics

D. Ritual

E. Astrology

Choose the most appropriate answer from the questions given below:
options: A, B, C and E only
A, B, C, D and E
questions.explanation:
The **Vedāṅgas** ("limbs of the Veda") are six subjects. Students studied them to understand and use the Vedas.

- Śikṣā – phonetics (**C**)
- Chandas – metrics (**A**)
- Vyākaraṇa – grammar (**B**)
- Kalpa – ritual (**D**)
- Jyotiṣa – astronomy and astrology (**E**)
- Nirukta – etymology (the origin of words)

All five listed items are Vedāṅgas. Only Nirukta is missing from the list. So the answer is A, B, C, D and E. The other options leave out at least one real Vedāṅga.

questions.question_md: National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) is a competency based framework related to
questions.explanation:
The **National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)** arranges qualifications in levels from 1 to 10. The official notification defines it as a competency-based framework. It organizes qualifications by levels of **knowledge, skills and aptitude**. Learners can reach a level through formal, non-formal or informal learning.

- "Knowledge, Skills and Attitude" (KSA) is a common phrase in training. But the NSQF text uses "aptitude", not "attitude". This option is the main trap.
- Understanding, application, analysis and synthesis are levels of Bloom's taxonomy. They are not the NSQF terms.

questions.question_md:
According to NEP 2020, match the functions of independence verticals of HECI

Match List I with List II

| LIST I (Verticals of HECI) | LIST II (Functions) |
|---|---|
| A. NHERC | I. Accreditation of institution |
| B. NAC | II. Academic standard setting |
| C. HEGC | III. Regulator for higher education |
| D. GEC | IV. Funding and financing of higher education |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
NEP 2020 proposes the **Higher Education Commission of India (HECI)**. It has four independent verticals:

- **A. NHERC – III.** The National Higher Education Regulatory Council is the single regulator for higher education.
- **B. NAC – I.** The National Accreditation Council accredits institutions.
- **C. HEGC – IV.** The Higher Education Grants Council handles funding and financing.
- **D. GEC – II.** The General Education Council sets academic standards and learning outcomes.

So the match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II. The other options mix up the work of HEGC and GEC, or of NAC and GEC.

questions.question_md: What is the western reaction to the things happening in Asia, Africa and Latin America?
options: The West is yet to reach their stage.
The West has the same issues as theirs.
The West does not have the same problems.
The West has plenty of alternatives.
questions.explanation:
The passage gives the Western answer. It says that "developed countries do not have same problems." So the West says it **does not have the same problems**. It therefore does not need the solutions of Asia, Africa and Latin America.

- "The West is yet to reach their stage" is not in the passage.
- "The West has the same issues" is the opposite of what the passage says.
- "The West has plenty of alternatives" is not the Western reaction. The passage only says that the world has many alternatives.

questions.question_md: The West should know that
options: The world is more than what the West understands.
The West should not share knowledge with others.
It is always advisable to keep the world divided.
questions.explanation:
The passage gives a first inference. It says that "the understanding of the world is much broader" than the Western understanding. So the West should know that **the world is more than what the West understands**.

- "Developing nations need western solutions" goes against the passage. The author says other solutions exist.
- The passage does not say the West should keep its knowledge to itself.
- The passage does not ask to keep the world divided. It asks the West to accept other ways of thinking.

questions.question_md:
The diversity of the world is reflected in:

A. Production of goods and leisure

B. Collective organisation of life

C. Conceiving time

D. Relations among human beings

Choose the most appropriate answer from the questions given below:
questions.explanation:
The passage says the diversity of the world includes ways of:

- **conceiving of time** (C),
- the **relations among human beings** (D) and between humans and non-humans,
- facing the past and the future,
- **collectively organizing life** (B),
- the **production of goods and services, as well as leisure** (A).

All four items appear in the passage. So the answer is A, B, C and D. The other options leave out at least one item from the list.

questions.question_md: The Western theories and concepts
options: valorize the knowledge of the South.
support the creation of single knowledge world.
identify the immensity of alternative ways of life and interaction.
questions.explanation:
The passage says that Western theories "do not identify such alternatives". Even when they do, "they do not valorize them" (value them). The West calls the knowledge of the South "outmoded" and "no knowledge at all". So the Western theories **reject the alternative knowledge**.

- "Valorize the knowledge of the South" is the opposite of the passage.
- The passage does not mention a "single knowledge world".
- "Identify the immensity of alternatives" is wrong. The passage says the theories do **not** identify them.

questions.question_md: The author of the passage
options: favors the recognition of alternative thinking and solution.
emphasizes the adoption of Western concepts.
suggests uniformity of problems and solutions.
questions.explanation:
The author says that "an alternative thinking of alternatives" is missing. The author says the West wastes many alternatives because it does not value them. So the author **favours the recognition of alternative thinking and solutions**.

- The author is not critical of alternative thinking. The author is critical of the West for ignoring it.
- The author does not want everyone to adopt Western concepts.
- The author stresses that the diversity of the world is infinite. So uniform problems and solutions go against the author's view.

groups.md:
The following table shows the average speed (in km per hour) of five different trains A-E during six days of a week from Monday through Saturday. Some data is missing in the table ( indicated as '-') that you are expected to calculate, if required. Based on the data in the table, answer the question that follows:

**Train - wise speed (in km/hour) on different Days**

Average Speed (in km/hr) of Trains

| Train | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Saturday |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 72 | 80 | - | 64 | 54 | - |
| B | 88 | - | 80 | 84 | 72 | 90 |
| C | 54 | 70 | 72 | - | 64 | 60 |
| D | - | 120 | 95 | - | 90 | 110 |
| E | 72 | 80 | 84 | 75 | - | - |

Read the following passage and answer the question:

Protection and conservation of forests and wildlife are essential to maintain the earth's health and environment. Forests play a key role in the maintenance of climate, rain-patterns, water and soil conservation.

India has 16 percent of the world's population with only 2.4 percent of its land area. There is much pressure on our natural resources including forests. Due to increasing consumerism and nature- hostile activities, the forest-cover is finishing very fast.

Thousands of snails, frogs, rats, earthworms, cockroaches and other animals are killed for dissection in schools, colleges and laboratories for experiments. This disturbs the ecological balance.

There is mindless destruction of forests for timber, firewood and fuel. Every year there is a loss of about 1.3 lakh hectares of forest area in India because of indiscriminate clearing of forests for cultivation, quarrying and large dams and irrigation projects. Over-grazing has also taken its toll. The result is serious ecological imbalance and environment degradation.

Conservation of forests and wildlife is also important as they make life beautiful and colourful. Their proper protection and conservation also means a continuous and adequate supply of food, fodder, medicines, timber etc.

questions.question_md: For train A, if the average speed on Saturday is 20% more than that on Wednesday and the mean of the average speeds over all the six days is 67 km/hour then what is the average speed on Saturday?
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of train A on Wednesday be x km/h. Then the Saturday speed is 1.2x.

- The mean of six days is 67, so the total is 67 × 6 = 402.
- Known days: 72 + 80 + 64 + 54 = 270.
- So x + 1.2x = 402 − 270 = 132.
- 2.2x = 132, so x = 60 km/h (Wednesday).
- Saturday = 1.2 × 60 = **72 km/h**.

A common error is to give the Wednesday speed (60) or to use the wrong total. 70, 74 and 75 do not fit the total of 402.

questions.question_md: If the mean of the average speeds of train C during all the six days is 25% less than the average speed of train B on Saturday, then the average speed of train D on Tuesday is approximately ___% more than that of train C on Thursday?
questions.explanation:
First find the missing Thursday speed of train C.

- Train B on Saturday: 90 km/h.
- 25 % less than 90 = 0.75 × 90 = 67.5 km/h. This is the mean for train C.
- Total for six days = 67.5 × 6 = 405.
- Known days of C: 54 + 70 + 72 + 64 + 60 = 320.
- Thursday speed of C = 405 − 320 = 85 km/h.

Now compare train D on Tuesday (120 km/h) with 85 km/h.

- Difference = 120 − 85 = 35.
- Percentage = (35 ÷ 85) × 100 ≈ 41.2 %, so about **41 %**.

If you divide by 120 instead of 85, you get about 29 %. Always divide by the value you compare with (train C).

questions.question_md: Train D runs 150 km more on Monday than that on Thursday and times taken by the train on Monday and Thursday are 5 hour and 4 hours, respectively. If the average speed of this train on Monday is 15 km/hour more than that on Thursday, then the mean of the distance travelled by the train on Monday and Thursday is
questions.explanation:
Let the Thursday speed of train D be v km/h. Then the Monday speed is v + 15.

- Thursday distance = 4v (time 4 hours).
- Monday distance = 5(v + 15) (time 5 hours).
- Monday distance is 150 km more: 5(v + 15) = 4v + 150.
- 5v + 75 = 4v + 150, so v = 75 km/h.

Distances:

- Thursday: 4 × 75 = 300 km.
- Monday: 5 × 90 = 450 km. Check: 450 − 300 = 150. ✔

Mean distance = (300 + 450) ÷ 2 = **375 km**.

The table values of train D are not needed here. The question gives all the data.

questions.question_md: If train B covers a total distance of 3400 km during all the six days by taking a total time of 40 hours, then the average speed of this train during all the six days together is ____% less than the average speed of this train on Monday. (Rounded-off to two digits after decimal)
questions.explanation:
Average speed for all six days = total distance ÷ total time.

- 3400 ÷ 40 = 85 km/h.
- Speed of train B on Monday (from the table) = 88 km/h.
- Difference = 88 − 85 = 3 km/h.
- Percentage less = (3 ÷ 88) × 100 ≈ 3.409 % ≈ **3.41 %**.

Divide by 88, the Monday speed, because the question compares with Monday. If you divide by 85, you get 3.53 %, which is not an option.

questions.question_md: For train E, if the ratio of average speed on Saturday and Friday is 5:3, then the average speed on Saturday is ___% more than that on Friday.
questions.explanation:
Let the Saturday speed be 5k and the Friday speed be 3k.

- Difference = 5k − 3k = 2k.
- Percentage more than Friday = (2k ÷ 3k) × 100 = 200 ÷ 3 = **66⅔ %**.

The answer does not need the actual speeds. The ratio alone is enough.

If you divide by the Saturday value (5k), you get 40 %. That would be "less than", not "more than".

questions.question_md: A Social Studies teacher assigns an online collaborative learning project to her students on ancient civilizations. The students are divided into groups of four. One student finds difficulty in exploring relevant information online. What would be the most effective way the student needs to adopt?
options: Ask the teacher to provide the required information.
Rely solely on his own efforts to find the information.
Seek assistance from his group members and discuss possible research sources.
Abandon the project since he cannot find the information online.
questions.explanation:
The project is a collaborative project. In such a project, group members learn from each other and share tasks. So the best step is to **ask the group members for help** and talk about good research sources.

- Asking the teacher for the information makes the student depend on the teacher. He does not learn how to search.
- Working only alone ignores the purpose of group work.
- Leaving the project is a negative step. It does not solve the problem.

Peer support also builds the student's own research skill for the future.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following can be used for virtual field trips?

A. Prezi

B. Kahoot

C. Virbela

D. Flipgrid

E. Second life

**Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:**
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation:
A virtual field trip lets students "visit" a place through a computer. Tools that create 3D virtual worlds are used for this.

- A. Prezi: a tool for presentations. **No.**
- B. Kahoot: a tool for game-based quizzes. **No.**
- C. Virbela: a 3D virtual world for classes and events. **Yes.**
- D. Flipgrid: a tool for short video discussions. **No.**
- E. Second Life: a 3D virtual world. Users move as avatars (digital figures). **Yes.**

So only **C and E** fit. Options with Prezi, Kahoot or Flipgrid include tools that do not create a virtual place.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** Situated cognition is the idea that thinking is located in social and physical contexts. not within an individual's mind.

**Statement II:** Schema is a concept or frame work that exists in a person's mind to organize and interpret information.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct answer** the from the options given below:
options: Both Statements I and Statement II are true.
Both Statements I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
Both statements give standard definitions from educational psychology.

- **Statement I is true.** Situated cognition says that thinking is located in social and physical contexts. It is not only inside one person's mind. So learning depends on the real setting.
- **Statement II is true.** A schema is a mental framework (a mental pattern). It organises and interprets new information. For example, a child has a schema for "dog" and uses it to understand new animals.

So both statements are true.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** The transfer of learning from one situation to another that is conscious and effortful is low-road transfer.

**Statement II:** The automatic, often unconscious, transfer of learning to another situation is high-road transfer.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct answer** from the options given below"
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
The two statements swap the definitions of the two kinds of transfer.

- **Low-road transfer** is automatic and often unconscious. It happens after a lot of practice. An example is typing on a new keyboard.
- **High-road transfer** is conscious and needs effort. The learner thinks about how to use old learning in a new situation.

Statement I calls conscious, effortful transfer "low-road". This is **false**. Statement II calls automatic transfer "high-road". This is also **false**.

So both statements are false.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are the examples of Authentic assessement?

A. Grading

B. Student's self-assessment

C. Portfolios

D. Exhibitions

**Choose the correct answer from the options given below"**
questions.notes: NTA final answer key accepts options 2 and 3.
questions.explanation:
Authentic assessment asks students to do real-world tasks. It checks what they can do, not only what they remember.

- A. Grading: this is a way to report scores. It is not a kind of authentic task. **No.**
- B. Student self-assessment: students judge their own work. Many books list it under authentic assessment. **Yes.**
- C. Portfolios: a collection of a student's work over time. **Yes.**
- D. Exhibitions: students show their work to an audience. **Yes.**

So B, C and D are all examples. No option has all three. "B and D Only" and "C and D Only" are both partly right. For this reason, the official key accepts both options.

The best choice is **C and D**. Portfolios and exhibitions are the most standard examples of authentic assessment.

questions.question_md: As compared to quantitative researchers, qualitative researchers lay more emphasis on
questions.explanation:
Qualitative research studies people in their natural setting. It tries to understand meanings, so it gives great importance to **context**.

The other options are features of quantitative research:

- Measurement: quantitative research turns things into numbers.
- Causality: it tests cause-and-effect links.
- Generalization: it applies results from a sample to a large population.

Qualitative research gives a deep description of a small case. It does not aim mainly at these three things.

questions.question_md: The criterion of 'transferability' in qualitative research is equivalent to which of the following criteria in quantitative research?
questions.explanation:
Lincoln and Guba gave four criteria for trustworthiness in qualitative research. Each one matches a criterion in quantitative research.

- Credibility matches internal validity.
- **Transferability matches external validity.**
- Dependability matches reliability.
- Confirmability matches objectivity.

Transferability asks: can the findings apply to other settings? External validity asks the same question about generalization. So the answer is external validity.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** Content analysis cannot be applied to visual materials.

**Statement II:** It is difficult to ascertain answers to 'why?' questions through content analysis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct answer** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is true.
questions.notes: Option 4 reads "Statement I is true but Statement II is true" in the English source (the Hindi version has "Statement I is false but Statement II is true"). Dropped in the NTA final answer key.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** Content analysis can study visual materials. Examples are photographs, films, TV programmes and advertisements.
- **Statement II is true.** Content analysis counts and codes what a text or image contains. It is hard to find answers to "why?" questions in this way. Research books list this as a limitation of the method.

So the right answer is "Statement I is false but Statement II is true". The Hindi version has this as option (4).

The English version prints option (4) as "Statement I is true but Statement II is true". This wording does not make sense. So no English option gives the right answer. This printing error is the likely reason why NTA dropped the question and gave marks to all.

questions.question_md: In conducting One way analysis of Variance, which of the following test statistics would be used?
questions.explanation:
One-way ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) compares the means of three or more groups. It uses the **F** statistic.

F = variance between groups ÷ variance within groups.

- Z and t tests compare one or two means.
- The chi-square test checks frequencies, for example in a contingency table.

So F is the test statistic for ANOVA.

questions.question_md:
In the text of a research article, if a reference is cited by writing the author name followed by "et al.", which among the following could represent the number of authors involved in the cited study?

A. 1

B. 2

C. 3

D. 4

**Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:**
questions.explanation:
"Et al." means "and others". Writers use it to shorten a list of authors.

- One author: there are no "others". **No.**
- Two authors: APA style always gives both names, for example "Smith and Rao (2020)". **No.**
- Three authors: APA style (7th edition) uses "et al." from the first citation. **Yes.**
- Four authors: also "et al.". **Yes.**

So **C and D** are correct. Options with 1 or 2 authors are wrong. In those cases, the writer names every author.

questions.question_md: In the ritualistic view of communication, individuals exchange understanding for
questions.explanation:
James Carey described two views of communication.

- The **transmission view** sees communication as sending messages over distance to control or inform people.
- The **ritual view** sees communication as sharing and taking part together. It builds a community and a common culture.

So in the ritual view, people exchange understanding for **communion and fraternity** (a feeling of togetherness).

- Accumulation of information fits the transmission view.
- Promotion of self-interest is not the aim of ritual communication.
- "Logocentric presence" is a term from philosophy (Derrida). It is not part of Carey's view.

questions.question_md: Another term commonly used to refer to the medium of communication is
questions.explanation:
In communication models, the message goes from a sender to a receiver through a **channel**. The channel is the medium, for example air for speech, a TV signal or a printed page.

Shannon and Weaver, and also Berlo (in the SMCR model: Source, Message, Channel, Receiver), use the word "channel".

"Carrier", "transporter" and "vehicle" are ordinary words. They are not the standard terms for the medium in communication studies.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following, according to Aristotle, will contribute for a communication's credibility?

A. Personal appearance

B. Peculiar mannerisms

C. Goodwill

D. Trustworthiness

E. Wisdom

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Aristotle said that the credibility of a speaker comes from **ethos** (the character of the speaker). Ethos has three parts:

- Phronesis: practical **wisdom** (good sense).
- Arete: good moral character, so the speaker is **trustworthy**.
- Eunoia: **goodwill** towards the audience.

So C, D and E are correct.

Personal appearance and strange mannerisms are not part of Aristotle's list. Options with A or B are therefore wrong.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** Much of non-verbal communication is based on arbitrary use of symbols by different cultures.

**Statement II**: A great amount of non-verbal communication is iconic and possibly understood universally.

In the light of the above statements, choose the ***most appropriate answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Both statements use careful words: "much of" and "a great amount of". So both can be true at the same time.

- **Statement I is correct.** Many gestures have arbitrary meanings. Each culture decides them. For example, a thumbs-up or a head nod can mean different things in different countries.
- **Statement II is correct.** Many non-verbal signs are iconic. They look like what they mean. Basic facial expressions such as a smile or anger are widely understood across cultures.

So both statements are correct.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** The new means of communication has promoted an 'ideology of limitless' communication.

**Statement II:** The new means of communication are against electronically extended interactivity among individuals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the ***most appropriate answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is correct.** The internet and mobile phones let people communicate at any time and with anyone. Writers call this belief an "ideology of limitless communication".
- **Statement II is incorrect.** The new media do not work against interactivity. They make electronically extended interactivity possible. Examples are chat, video calls and social media.

So Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.question_md: A takes 2 hours more than B to walk P km, but if A doubles his speed, then he can make it in one hour less than B. How much time does B require for walking P km?
questions.explanation:
Let B take t hours to walk P km. Then A takes t + 2 hours.

When A doubles his speed, his time becomes half: (t + 2) ÷ 2.

This time is one hour less than B's time:

- (t + 2) ÷ 2 = t − 1
- t + 2 = 2t − 2
- t = **4 hours**

Check: A takes 6 hours. At double speed, A takes 3 hours. This is 1 hour less than 4. ✔

questions.question_md: Average score of a class of 60 students in an examination is 43. If the average score of the students who have passed is 52 and that of who have failed is 16, then what is the percentage of failed students?
questions.explanation:
Let f students fail. Then 60 − f students pass.

- Total marks of the class = 60 × 43 = 2580.
- Total marks = 52 × (60 − f) + 16 × f.
- 3120 − 52f + 16f = 2580.
- 36f = 540, so f = 15.

Percentage failed = (15 ÷ 60) × 100 = **25 %**.

Check: 45 passed students × 52 = 2340. 15 failed students × 16 = 240. The total is 2580. ✔

questions.question_md: If (a-b) : (b-c) : (c-d) = 1 : 2 : 3 then what is the value of (a + d) : c ?
questions.explanation:
Let a − b = k, b − c = 2k and c − d = 3k.

Write every letter in terms of d and k:

- c = d + 3k
- b = c + 2k = d + 5k
- a = b + k = d + 6k

Now find (a + d) : c.

- a + d = 2d + 6k = 2(d + 3k)
- c = d + 3k

So (a + d) : c = 2 : 1. This result does not depend on the values of d or k.

A quick check: take k = 1 and d = 0. Then c = 3 and a = 6. So (6 + 0) : 3 = 2 : 1.

questions.question_md: In a certain language code, DIAMOND is coded as VQYMKLV. How is CRUELTY coded?
questions.explanation:
Use the position of each letter in the alphabet (A = 1, Z = 26).

In DIAMOND → VQYMKLV, each code letter = 26 − (position of the letter):

- D (4) → 22 = V
- I (9) → 17 = Q
- A (1) → 25 = Y
- M (13) → 13 = M
- O (15) → 11 = K
- N (14) → 12 = L

Apply the same rule to CRUELTY:

- C (3) → 23 = W
- R (18) → 8 = H
- U (21) → 5 = E
- E (5) → 21 = U
- L (12) → 14 = N
- T (20) → 6 = F
- Y (25) → 1 = A

The code is **WHEUNFA**. The other options differ in one or more letters.

questions.question_md: A dealer marks his goods 25% above the cost price and then allows 10% discount on it. What is the cost price of an article on which he gains ₹50 ?
questions.explanation:
Let the cost price be ₹100.

- Marked price = 100 + 25 % = ₹125.
- Selling price after 10 % discount = 125 × 0.9 = ₹112.50.
- Gain = ₹12.50 on a cost of ₹100. So the gain is 12.5 % of the cost.

Now use the real gain of ₹50:

- 12.5 % of cost = 50
- Cost = 50 ÷ 0.125 = **₹400**

Check: 400 × 1.25 = 500. A 10 % discount gives 450. The gain is 450 − 400 = 50. ✔

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following terms in order of increasing intension.

A. Baseball player

B. Ball player

C. Fielder

D. Athlete

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Intension is the set of qualities that a term means. A term with more qualities has more intension. It also covers fewer things.

- Athlete: a person who plays a sport. This is the most general term.
- Ball player: an athlete who plays a ball game.
- Baseball player: a ball player who plays baseball.
- Fielder: a baseball player in a fielding position. This is the most specific term.

So the order of increasing intension is **D, B, A, C**.

C, A, B, D is the reverse order. It shows increasing extension (more members), not increasing intension.

questions.question_md: " I admit that there are people for whom even the existence of God is a big question. My answer is that I do not address them, but that I presuppose a minimum of reason in my readers." Identify the informal fallacy committed in the above statement.
questions.explanation:
A straw man fallacy happens when a speaker changes the opponent's view into a weaker or false form. Then the speaker rejects this weak form.

Here, the speaker does not answer the real doubts of people who question God's existence. Instead, he says that his readers have "a minimum of reason". This suggests that the doubters have no reason. So he paints the opponents as unreasonable people and then ignores them. The examiner treats this as a **straw man**.

- Begging the question is tempting, because the speaker seems to assume that God exists. But the key focuses on how he treats the opponents.
- Slippery slope needs a chain of bad results. There is no such chain here.
- A complex question asks a question with a hidden assumption. There is no question here.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** Inductive arguments can be invalid or valid.

**Statement II:** A strong inductive argument that has all true premises is called a "cogent" argument.

In the light of the above statements, choose the ***most appropriate answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is incorrect.** In standard logic books (for example, Hurley), only deductive arguments are valid or invalid. Inductive arguments are **strong** or **weak**. The premises make the conclusion probable, not certain.
- **Statement II is correct.** A cogent argument is a strong inductive argument with all true premises. It is the inductive partner of a sound deductive argument.

So Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.question_md: "If the plane takes off from the airstrip B then it is south bound. The plane did not take off from the airstrip B, therefore it is not southbound." Identify the formal fallacy in the above argument.
questions.explanation:
The argument has this form:

- If P (the plane takes off from airstrip B), then Q (it is southbound).
- Not P.
- So, not Q.

This form is invalid. It is called **denying the antecedent**. The antecedent is the "if" part (P). The plane can take off from another airstrip and still go south.

- Affirming the consequent has the form "If P then Q; Q; so P". That is a different error.
- Exclusive premises and four terms are errors of categorical syllogisms. This argument is a conditional argument.

questions.question_md: In which of the following arguments the middle term is always positively related to the major term only, there being no negative instance[s] of their agreement in absence?
options: All knowable objects are nameable. The pot is a knowable object. Therefore, pot is nameable.
No non-fiery things have smoke. This hill has smoke. Therefore this hill is not non-fiery.
All things which have smoke have fire. This hill has smoke. Therefore, this hill has fire.
What is not different-from-other-elements has no smell. The earth has smell. Therefore, earth is different from other elements.
questions.notes: The last letter of "instances" is cut off at the page edge in the source.
questions.explanation:
The question describes **kevalānvayī anumāna** in Nyāya logic. In this inference, the middle term (hetu) has only positive agreement with the major term (sādhya). There is no negative example, because the major term is present everywhere.

- Option (1): "nameable" applies to every object. So we cannot find a thing that is not nameable. There is no negative instance. This is kevalānvayī. **Correct.**
- Option (2): this uses negative agreement (no non-fiery thing has smoke).
- Option (3): smoke and fire have both positive examples (a kitchen) and negative examples (a lake). This is anvaya-vyatirekī.
- Option (4): this is kevala-vyatirekī. It uses only negative agreement, because only earth has smell.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** Google Chrome, Microsoft Windows, and Apple Safari are examples of Web Browsers.

**Statement II:** Google, Yahoo, and Bing are examples of Web Search Engines.

In the light of the above statements, choose the ***correct answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** Google Chrome and Apple Safari are web browsers. But Microsoft Windows is an operating system, not a browser. Microsoft's browsers are Edge and Internet Explorer.
- **Statement II is true.** Google, Yahoo and Bing are web search engines.

One wrong item makes Statement I false. So Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.question_md:
Consider the following computer memory hierarchy diagram:

(Pyramid, from top to bottom)

1. Processor Registers
2. Cache Memory
3. Random Access Memory
4. Solid State Storage
5. Magnetic Hard Disk
6. Optical Disk Storage
7. Magnetic Tape

As you travel down the memory hierarchy diagram shown above, then which of the following is true?
options: decreasing cost per bit and decreasing access time
increasing cost per bit and increasing access time
increasing cost per bit and decreasing access time
decreasing cost per bit and increasing access time
questions.notes: The pyramid diagram of the source is given here as a top-to-bottom list (apex = Processor Registers, base = Magnetic Tape).
questions.explanation:
The memory hierarchy has the fastest memory at the top and the slowest at the bottom.

As you go down from registers to magnetic tape:

- **Cost per bit decreases.** Tape and disks are cheap for each bit stored.
- **Access time increases.** The memory becomes slower to reach.
- Capacity also increases.

Registers and cache are very fast but costly, so computers have only a small amount of them.

The options with "increasing cost per bit" are wrong. The option with "decreasing access time" is also wrong, because lower memory is slower.

questions.question_md:
**Match List I with List II**

| List I ( Internet Related Terms) | List II ( Context) |
|---|---|
| A. Service of Internet | I. Microsoft Edge |
| B. Web Browser | II. Microsoft Outlook |
| C. E-mail Client Software | III. Microsoft Bing |
| D. Web Search Engine | IV. World Wide Web |

**Choose the correct answer from the options given below:**
options: A- IV, B- II, C- I, D-III
A- I, B- IV, C- III, D-II
A- IV, B- I, C- II, D-III
A- III, B- I, C- II, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Match each term with a Microsoft example.

- A. Service of the internet → **IV. World Wide Web.** The Web is one service that runs on the internet. E-mail is another one.
- B. Web browser → **I. Microsoft Edge.**
- C. E-mail client software → **II. Microsoft Outlook.**
- D. Web search engine → **III. Microsoft Bing.**

So the match is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Option (1) wrongly pairs Outlook with the browser and Edge with e-mail.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements** regarding MS-Excel:

**Statement I :** Cell E9 contains the value 4 and E10 contains the value 8. You select both the cells and drag the fill handle down to E13. The contents of cells E11, E12 and E13 will be 9, 10 and 11, respectively.

**Statement II:** The formula =A3*$A$1 has the reference to cell A1 set as a relative reference while the reference to cell A3 is an absolute reference.

In the light of the above statements, choose the ***correct answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** Excel uses the step between the two selected cells. The values are 4 and 8, so the step is 4. The fill handle gives 12, 16 and 20 in E11, E12 and E13. It does not give 9, 10 and 11.
- **Statement II is false.** The dollar signs ($) make a reference absolute. So $A$1 is an **absolute** reference and A3 is a **relative** reference. The statement says the opposite.

So both statements are false.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements** with reference to different number systems:

**Statement I:** (D6C1)₁₆ = (54977)₁₀

**Statement II:** (41819)₁₀ = (A35B)₁₆

In the light of the above statements, choose the ***correct answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
Convert hexadecimal (base 16) to decimal. In hexadecimal, A = 10, B = 11, C = 12 and D = 13. The place values are 4096, 256, 16 and 1.

**Statement I:** (D6C1)₁₆

- 13 × 4096 = 53248
- 6 × 256 = 1536
- 12 × 16 = 192
- 1 × 1 = 1
- Total = 54977. **True.**

**Statement II:** (A35B)₁₆

- 10 × 4096 = 40960
- 3 × 256 = 768
- 5 × 16 = 80
- 11 × 1 = 11
- Total = 41819. **True.**

So both statements are true.

questions.question_md: Photovoltaic cells are made up of
options: a combination of p and n type of semiconductor
Neither p nor n type of semiconductor
questions.explanation:
A photovoltaic (solar) cell has a **p–n junction**. This is a layer of p-type semiconductor joined to a layer of n-type semiconductor. Both layers are usually made of silicon.

- The p-type layer has extra "holes" (positive charge carriers).
- The n-type layer has extra electrons.

Light frees electrons near the junction. The electric field at the junction pushes the charges in one direction. This makes an electric current.

One type of semiconductor alone has no junction. So it cannot separate the charges and make useful current.

questions.question_md:
What is the correct sequence of processes involved in particle removal from largest to smallest in waste water treatment?

A. Sedimentation

B. Flocculation

C. Screening

**Choose the correct answer from the options given below:**
questions.explanation:
Wastewater treatment removes the largest particles first and the smallest particles last.

- **C. Screening** removes large objects. Examples are plastic, rags and sticks.
- **A. Sedimentation** lets heavy, settleable particles sink to the bottom of a tank.
- **B. Flocculation** removes very small (colloidal) particles. A chemical makes them stick together into larger "flocs", so that they can be removed.

So the order from largest to smallest particles is **C, A, B**.

Orders that start with sedimentation or flocculation are wrong. Screening always comes first, because large objects can damage pumps.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are used as disinfectant during water treatment.

A. Chlorine

B. Phosphorous

C. Ozone

D. Nitrogen

E. Ultraviolet Rays

**Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:**
questions.explanation:
A disinfectant kills germs (bacteria and viruses) in water.

- A. Chlorine: the most common disinfectant. **Yes.**
- B. Phosphorus: a nutrient. It causes algae growth. It does not kill germs. **No.**
- C. Ozone: a strong oxidising gas that kills germs. **Yes.**
- D. Nitrogen: an inactive gas, and also a nutrient in water. **No.**
- E. Ultraviolet rays: they damage the DNA of germs. **Yes.**

So the answer is **A, C and E**. All the other options include phosphorus or nitrogen.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements**: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

**Assertion A:** Volatile Organic compounds (VOCs) often are measured in the atmosphere as non-methane hydrocarbons.

**Reason R :** Methane is highly reactive in photochemical smog formation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
- **Assertion A is true.** Scientists often measure VOCs (volatile organic compounds) as non-methane hydrocarbons (NMHC). They leave out methane on purpose.
- **Reason R is false.** Methane reacts very slowly in the air. So it plays only a small part in photochemical smog. Smog forms mainly from reactive VOCs, nitrogen oxides and sunlight.

In fact, methane is left out of the VOC measurement *because* it has low reactivity. R says the opposite.

So A is true but R is false.

questions.question_md:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** Flood fringe is the lowest part of the flood plain, where no development is permitted and which is reserved for the passage of flood flows.

**Statement II:** Floodway is an area of floodplain land where filling and development may be permitted subject to land use and building code regulations designed to minimize damage.

In the light of the above statement, choose the ***correct answer*** from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
The two statements swap the meanings of the two flood terms.

- The **floodway** is the river channel and the lowest part of the flood plain next to it. It must stay open for flood water. No building is permitted there.
- The **flood fringe** is the outer part of the flood plain. Filling and building may be permitted there. Rules on land use and building reduce the damage.

Statement I gives the floodway definition to the flood fringe. So it is **false**. Statement II gives the flood fringe definition to the floodway. So it is also **false**.

So both statements are false.

questions.question_md: The Sadler commission (1717-19) recommended the establishment of ____ in Indian universities.
questions.notes: The source prints "1717-19" (the Sadler Commission sat in 1917-19).
questions.explanation:
The Sadler Commission is also called the Calcutta University Commission. It worked from 1917 to 1919. The question prints "1717-19", which is a printing error.

The commission suggested new bodies to run universities:

- A large **Court** in place of the old Senate.
- An Executive Council in place of the Syndicate.
- An Academic Council for academic matters.

So the answer is **the Court**.

The Senate already existed in the old universities, so it was not a new suggestion. Counselling centres and grievance cells are modern ideas. They were not part of this commission's work.

questions.question_md: The Ram Murti Review committee recommended that admission to higher education must be
questions.explanation:
