groups.md:
The following table shows the number of employees working in five different colleges A-E, alongwith the ratio of Males to Females [M : F] among them. Based on the data in the table, answer the questions that follow.

**College-wise Details of Employees**

| College | Number of Employees | Ratio M : F |
|---|---|---|
| A | 3040 | 13 : 6 |
| B | 3360 | 4 : 3 |
| C | 2920 | 9 : 11 |
| D | 2760 | 10 : 13 |
| E | 2840 | 13 : 7 |

Read the passage and answer the questions that follow :

Science and the techniques to which it has given rise have changed human life during the last hundred and fifty years more than it had been changed since men took to agriculture, and the changes that are being wrought by science continue at an increasing speed. There is no sign of any new stability to be attained on some scientific plateau. On the contrary, there is every reason to think that the revolutionary possibilities of science extend immeasurably beyond what has so far been realised. Can the human race adjust itself quickly enough to these vertiginous transformations, or will it, as innumerable former species have done, perish from lack of adaptability? The dinosaurs were, in their day, the lords of creation, and if there had been philosophers among them, not one would have foreseen that the whole race might perish. But they became extinct because they could not adapt themselves to a world without swamps. In the case of man and science there is a wholly new factor, namely that man himself is creating the changes of environment to which he will have to adjust himself with unprecedented rapidity. But, although man through his scientific skill is the cause of the changes of environment, most of these changes are not willed by human beings. Although they come about through human agencies, they have, or at any rate have had so far, something of the inexorable inevitability of natural forces. Whether Nature dried up the swamps or men deliberately drained them, makes little difference as regards the ultimate result. Whether men will be able to survive the changes of environment that their own skill has brought about is an open question. If the answer is in the affirmative, it will be known some day; if not, not. If the answer is to be in the affirmative, men will have to apply scientific ways of thinking to themselves and their institutions.

questions.question_md: What is the total number of male employees taking all the Colleges together ?
questions.explanation:
First find the male (M) and female (F) employees in each college. Divide the total by the sum of the ratio parts.

- A: 3040 ÷ 19 = 160. M = 13 × 160 = 2080. F = 6 × 160 = 960.
- B: 3360 ÷ 7 = 480. M = 4 × 480 = 1920. F = 3 × 480 = 1440.
- C: 2920 ÷ 20 = 146. M = 9 × 146 = 1314. F = 11 × 146 = 1606.
- D: 2760 ÷ 23 = 120. M = 10 × 120 = 1200. F = 13 × 120 = 1560.
- E: 2840 ÷ 20 = 142. M = 13 × 142 = 1846. F = 7 × 142 = 994.

Add the male employees: 2080 + 1920 + 1314 + 1200 + 1846 = **8360**.

The other options are close numbers. They come from small addition or ratio mistakes.

questions.question_md: What is the average number of female employees taking all the colleges together ?
questions.explanation:
First find the male (M) and female (F) employees in each college. Divide the total by the sum of the ratio parts.

- A: 3040 ÷ 19 = 160. M = 13 × 160 = 2080. F = 6 × 160 = 960.
- B: 3360 ÷ 7 = 480. M = 4 × 480 = 1920. F = 3 × 480 = 1440.
- C: 2920 ÷ 20 = 146. M = 9 × 146 = 1314. F = 11 × 146 = 1606.
- D: 2760 ÷ 23 = 120. M = 10 × 120 = 1200. F = 13 × 120 = 1560.
- E: 2840 ÷ 20 = 142. M = 13 × 142 = 1846. F = 7 × 142 = 994.

Add the female employees: 960 + 1440 + 1606 + 1560 + 994 = 6560.

There are 5 colleges. The average is 6560 ÷ 5 = **1312**.

Check: total employees are 14,920. Males are 8360, so females are 14,920 − 8360 = 6560. The answer is the same.

questions.question_md: The number of male employees working in Colleges A and C together is approximately ________% more than the number of female employees working in colleges B and D together.
questions.explanation:
Use the ratio parts from the table.

- Males in A: 3040 ÷ 19 × 13 = 2080.
- Males in C: 2920 ÷ 20 × 9 = 1314.
- Males in A and C: 2080 + 1314 = 3394.
- Females in B: 3360 ÷ 7 × 3 = 1440.
- Females in D: 2760 ÷ 23 × 13 = 1560.
- Females in B and D: 1440 + 1560 = 3000.

The difference is 3394 − 3000 = 394.

Percentage more = 394 ÷ 3000 × 100 ≈ 13.1%. This is about **13%**.

Note: the base is the second group (3000), because the question asks "more than" that group. If you divide by 3394, you get about 11.6%. That is a common mistake.

questions.question_md: What is the ratio of female employees working in College D to that in College E ?
questions.explanation:
Find the female employees in each college.

- College D: 2760 ÷ 23 = 120. Females = 13 × 120 = 1560.
- College E: 2840 ÷ 20 = 142. Females = 7 × 142 = 994.

The ratio is 1560 : 994. Divide both numbers by 2. The ratio becomes **780 : 497**.

780 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 13 and 497 = 7 × 71. They have no common factor, so this is the simplest form. The ratios 7 : 4 and 9 : 5 are not equal to this value.

questions.question_md: The number of employees working in College C is approximately ________% more than that in College D.
questions.explanation:
College C has 2920 employees. College D has 2760 employees.

The difference is 2920 − 2760 = 160.

Percentage more = 160 ÷ 2760 × 100 ≈ 5.8%. This is about **6%**.

The base is College D, because the question asks how much more C has "than" D. The ratios M : F are not needed here.

questions.question_md: An economics teacher wants to create an infographics to explain supply and demand to her students. Which of the following tools would be most suitable ?
questions.explanation:
An infographic is a picture that shows information with charts, icons and short text. **Canva** is an online graphic design tool. It has ready templates for infographics, posters and slides. So the teacher can easily make a supply and demand chart with it.

- Edpuzzle adds questions and notes to videos.
- Quizlet makes flashcards and practice quizzes.
- MindMeister makes mind maps. A mind map can show ideas, but it is not a tool for designed infographics.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Norm referencing is used to interpret a score of an individual by comparing it with those of other individuals.

**Statement II :** Criterion referencing is used to interpret a person’s performance by comparing it to some specified behavioural domain.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are correct
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are incorrect
**Statement I** is correct but **Statement II** is incorrect
**Statement I** is incorrect but **Statement II** is correct
questions.explanation:
Both statements give the standard meanings of the two types of test interpretation.

- **Statement I is correct.** A norm-referenced test compares a person's score with the scores of other people (the norm group). Percentile ranks are an example.
- **Statement II is correct.** A criterion-referenced test compares a person's performance with a fixed standard. This standard is a defined domain of skills or behaviour. For example, "the student can solve 8 of 10 fraction problems".

So both statements are correct.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are the elements of observational learning ?

(A) Production

(B) Attention

(C) Identification

(D) Retention

(E) Motivation

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Albert Bandura described observational learning. This is learning by watching a model. He gave four elements (processes):

- **Attention (B):** the learner must notice the model's behaviour.
- **Retention (D):** the learner must remember the behaviour.
- **Production (A):** the learner must be able to reproduce (do) the behaviour.
- **Motivation (E):** the learner must have a reason to do it.

Identification (C) is not one of the four elements. It is a term from Freud's theory. So the answer is (A), (B), (D) and (E).

questions.question_md: In ‘VARK’ model of learning styles, ‘A’ stands for __________.
questions.explanation:
Neil Fleming made the VARK model of learning styles. VARK means:

- **V** – Visual: learning from pictures, charts and diagrams.
- **A** – **Aural**: learning by listening and talking.
- **R** – Read/write: learning from written words.
- **K** – Kinaesthetic: learning by doing and touching.

"Aural" means "related to hearing". The other options are not part of the model.

questions.question_md: When a very bright light is incident on our eyes, we immediately close our eyelids. This is an example of _________.
questions.explanation:
A reflex action is a fast, automatic response to a stimulus (a signal from outside). The person does not think or plan it. Closing the eyes in a very bright light is a reflex. It protects the eyes in a fraction of a second.

An instinct is different. It is a complex pattern of behaviour, such as nest building in birds. Closing the eyelid is a simple, single response, so it is not an instinct. "Desired instincts" and "intrapersonal instincts" are not standard terms.

questions.question_md:
Identify the disadvantages of open ended questions in survey research.

(A) The questions do not suggest certain kinds of answer to respondents.

(B) They are time consuming for interviewers to administer.

(C) They require greater effort from respondents.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
An open-ended question lets respondents answer in their own words. It has no fixed answer choices.

- **(A) is not a disadvantage.** The question does not suggest answers to the respondent. This is an advantage, because answers are less biased.
- **(B) is a disadvantage.** The interviewer must write down long answers, so it takes more time.
- **(C) is a disadvantage.** The respondent must think and write more, so it takes more effort.

Other disadvantages are that answers are hard to code and compare. So only (B) and (C) are disadvantages.

questions.question_md:
In a reference written in APA style, arrange the information pertaining to the reference in correct order.

(A) DOI number

(B) Volume number

(C) Name of author

(D) Title of the article

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
APA style gives a journal article reference in this order:

Author, A. A. (Year). Title of the article. *Journal Name*, Volume(Issue), pages. https://doi.org/...

So the order of the given parts is:

1. **(C)** Name of author
2. **(D)** Title of the article
3. **(B)** Volume number
4. **(A)** DOI number

The DOI (Digital Object Identifier) always comes at the end. The author name always comes first. The answer is (C), (D), (B), (A).

questions.question_md: A research study is said to have heuristic value if :
options: It leads to no further research
questions.explanation:
"Heuristic" means "helping to discover". A study has heuristic value when it leads to new ideas and new questions. So other researchers start more studies on the topic.

- "Leads to no further research" is the opposite of heuristic value.
- "Results lack consistency" is about reliability.
- "Results lack validity" is about accuracy.

These two are problems of a study, not its heuristic value.

questions.question_md: An entrance examination with objective type questions is conducted. For each correct answer, 1 mark is awarded and for each incorrect answer 0.25 marks are deducted. The number of marks scored by candidates who appeared in the examination, is an example of :
questions.explanation:
A discrete variable can take only separate, countable values. It cannot take every value between two points.

In this test, each answer changes the score by 1 or by −0.25. So a score can only be a multiple of 0.25, such as 10, 10.25 or 10.5. A score like 10.13 is not possible. So the marks form a **discrete variable**.

- It is not continuous, because values between the steps are impossible.
- It is not nominal, because marks are numbers, not names of groups.
- It is not ordinal, because the gap between marks has a fixed size. Ordinal data only shows rank order.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Medical research usually involves pain or distress in animals.

**Statement II :** Psychological research is usually benign and may involve little, if any, discomfort for the animals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are correct
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are incorrect
**Statement I** is correct but **Statement II** is incorrect
**Statement I** is incorrect but **Statement II** is correct
questions.explanation:
This question comes from the ethics of animal research.

- **Statement I is correct.** Medical research often tests drugs, surgery or diseases on animals. This usually causes some pain or distress.
- **Statement II is correct.** Most psychological research with animals studies behaviour, learning or perception. Examples are maze learning and food rewards. These studies usually cause little or no discomfort.

Research methods textbooks make this comparison. They note that ethics rules still apply to both fields. So both statements are correct.

questions.question_md: A photograph constitutes a/an :
questions.explanation:
Umberto Eco divided texts into "open" and "closed" texts.

- A **closed text** guides the reader to one fixed meaning.
- An **open text** allows many readings. Each reader can build a different meaning.

A photograph has no fixed words to explain it. Different viewers read different meanings from the same picture. The meaning depends on the viewer's culture, experience and context. So a photograph is an **open text**.

"Protective text" and "refined text" are not standard terms in communication studies.

questions.question_md: The Buddhist concept of communication is marked by :
questions.explanation:
The Buddhist view of communication comes from the idea of dependent origination (Pratītyasamutpāda). This idea says that every event depends on many causes and conditions. Nothing has only one cause.

Wimal Dissanayake applied this idea to communication. In the Buddhist view, meaning comes from many connected factors at the same time. These factors include the sender, the receiver, the message and the context. So Buddhist communication is marked by **multi-causality**.

- Mono-causality (one cause) fits linear Western models, not Buddhism.
- Dyadic causality (two parts) and skewed causality do not describe this idea.

questions.question_md: At present, cyber communication is a :
questions.explanation:
"Palpable" means "real and easy to feel or notice". Today, people use email, social media, video calls and online banking every day. So cyber communication is a **palpable reality**. It is part of normal life now.

- It is not fictitious, because it actually exists.
- It is not futuristic, because it is already here, not only in the future.
- It is not "conventional", because it is still new compared with older forms such as print and face-to-face talk.

questions.question_md:
The main objectives of public policy sphere communication is to involve citizens in :

(A) Idea generation

(B) Policy critique

(C) Innovative policy practices

(D) Ignoring oppositional views

(E) Promotion of stereotypes

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Public policy sphere communication tries to bring citizens into the policy process. It wants open and active public discussion.

- **(A) Idea generation:** yes. Citizens give new ideas for policies.
- **(B) Policy critique:** yes. Citizens examine and criticise policies.
- **(C) Innovative policy practices:** yes. Citizens help to find new ways to carry out policy.
- **(D) Ignoring oppositional views:** no. Good public communication listens to all views.
- **(E) Promotion of stereotypes:** no. This harms fair public discussion.

So the answer is (A), (B) and (C) only.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Western communication models examined the relationship among communicative elements on an individual basis.

**Statement II :** The Buddhist concept of communication emphasises the contextualisation of each of the communicative elements.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are true
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are false
**Statement I** is true but **Statement II** is false
**Statement I** is false but **Statement II** is true
questions.explanation:
Wimal Dissanayake compared Western and Buddhist ideas of communication.

- **Statement I is true.** Western models, such as Shannon and Weaver's, separate communication into elements. Examples are the sender, the message, the channel and the receiver. They study the links between these elements one by one, usually in a straight line.
- **Statement II is true.** The Buddhist view says that each element depends on its context and on the other elements. Meaning comes from the whole situation, not from one part.

So both statements are true.

questions.question_md: A man, a woman and a boy can do a piece of work in 6, 9 and 18 days, respectively. How many boys should assist one man and one woman to do the work in one day ?
questions.explanation:
Find how much work each person does in one day.

- A man does 1/6 of the work.
- A woman does 1/9 of the work.
- A boy does 1/18 of the work.

One man and one woman do 1/6 + 1/9 = 3/18 + 2/18 = 5/18 of the work in one day.

The work left for one day is 1 − 5/18 = 13/18.

Each boy does 1/18 in one day. So we need 13 boys.

The answer is **13**.

questions.question_md: A family consists of 6 members namely A, B, C, D, E and F. B is the brother-in-law of C’s mother. C is the father of F. D is the father of A and F is the grandson of D. There are two female members in the family. Which of the following pairs represent the female members in the family ?
questions.explanation:
Use each clue one by one.

- C is the father of F, so C is male.
- F is the grandson of D, so F is male. D is the father of A, so D is male.
- F's father is C and F's grandfather is D. So C is the son of D.
- C's mother is the wife of D. The only person left for her is E. So E is female.
- B is the brother-in-law of E, so B is male. B is D's brother.
- A is the child of D. The family has two females, and only A is left. So A is female (D's daughter).

The females are **A and E**.

D, B and C are all male, so the other options are wrong.

questions.question_md:
Find the number that can replace question mark (?) in the series given below.

1.5, 5, 10.5, 18, 27.5, 39, ?, ...
questions.explanation:
Find the difference between the terms.

- 5 − 1.5 = 3.5
- 10.5 − 5 = 5.5
- 18 − 10.5 = 7.5
- 27.5 − 18 = 9.5
- 39 − 27.5 = 11.5

The differences go up by 2 each time. The next difference is 13.5.

So the next term is 39 + 13.5 = **52.5**.

questions.question_md: A child is looking for his father. He goes 100 meter towards east and then turns to his right and goes 30 meters. From there the child again turns to his right and goes for 40 meters. Where he finds his father at his uncle’s place. How far is his uncle’s place from the starting point of the child ?
questions.explanation:
Draw the path step by step. Take the starting point as (0, 0).

- The child goes 100 m east. He is now at (100, 0).
- He turns right. When you face east, right is south. He goes 30 m south to (100, −30).
- He turns right again. When you face south, right is west. He goes 40 m west to (60, −30).

The uncle's place is 60 m east and 30 m south of the start.

Use the Pythagoras theorem: distance = √(60² + 30²) = √(3600 + 900) = √4500.

√4500 = √(900 × 5) = **30√5 m**.

questions.question_md:
In a certain coding language :

(a) 1000 i.e. 10³ is coded as 1331

(b) 125 i.e. 5³ is coded as 216

How 729 will be coded in that language ?
questions.explanation:
Look at the rule in each example.

- 1000 = 10³ is coded as 1331 = 11³.
- 125 = 5³ is coded as 216 = 6³.

So the rule is: take the cube root, add 1, then cube the result.

729 = 9³. Add 1 to get 10. Then 10³ = **1000**.

1728 is 12³ and 2197 is 13³, so they do not follow the rule. 1331 is the code for 1000, not for 729.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements are contradictory to each other ?

(A) All plants are fungi

(B) No plants are fungi

(C) Some plants are not fungi

(D) Some plants are fungi

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Contradictory statements cannot both be true and cannot both be false. In the square of opposition, there are two contradictory pairs:

- A and O: "All S are P" and "Some S are not P".
- E and I: "No S are P" and "Some S are P".

Here:

- (A) "All plants are fungi" and (C) "Some plants are not fungi" are contradictory.
- (B) "No plants are fungi" and (D) "Some plants are fungi" are contradictory.

Only the pair (B) and (D) is in the options.

- (A) and (B) are contraries. They cannot both be true, but both can be false.
- (C) and (D) are subcontraries. They cannot both be false, but both can be true.
- (A) and (D) are in subalternation. (D) follows from (A).

questions.question_md: If the statement - “All trucks are polluting vehicles” is given as false, then which of the following statements can be immediately inferred to be true ?
options: Some trucks are not polluting vehicles.
questions.explanation:
"All trucks are polluting vehicles" is an A proposition. Its contradictory is the O proposition: "Some trucks are not polluting vehicles".

Contradictory statements always have opposite truth values. So if the A statement is false, the O statement must be **true**.

- "Some trucks are polluting vehicles" (I) is undetermined. It may be true or false.
- "No trucks are polluting vehicles" (E) is the contrary of A. When A is false, E is undetermined.
- "No polluting vehicles are trucks" is the converse of E. So it is also undetermined.

questions.question_md: Which of the following statements is equivalent to the statement - “Some philosophers are not idealists.”?
questions.explanation:
The statement is an O proposition: "Some S are not P". Here S = philosophers and P = idealists.

An O proposition is equivalent to its obverse and to its contrapositive.

- Obverse: "Some philosophers are non-idealists".
- Contrapositive: first obvert, then convert, then obvert again.
  - Obvert: "Some philosophers are non-idealists".
  - Convert: "Some non-idealists are philosophers".
  - Obvert: "Some non-idealists are **not non-philosophers**".

So the last option is equivalent.

- "Some philosophers are not non-idealists" means "Some philosophers are idealists". This is a different claim.
- "No idealists are philosophers" is an E proposition. It is much stronger.
- "Some non-idealists are not philosophers" does not follow from the given statement.

questions.question_md: Which fallacy is involved in the following statement “Indian pharmaceutical companies are profitable, therefore, average Indian pharmaceutical company is profitable”?
questions.explanation:
The fallacy of division happens when we say that each part has a property because the whole has it.

Here the argument takes a claim about Indian pharmaceutical companies as a whole group. Then it says the average single company has the same property. The whole industry may be profitable because of a few big firms. So the typical company need not be profitable. This is the **fallacy of division**.

- Hasty generalisation goes from a few cases to a general rule. Here the argument goes from a whole to a part.
- Slippery slope says one step will lead to a chain of bad results.
- Fallacy of accident applies a general rule to an unusual case where the rule does not fit.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** The Aristotelian syllogism is only inductive and formal.

**Statement II :** Nyāya syllogism is deductive - inductive and formal-material.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are true
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are false
**Statement I** is true but **Statement II** is false
**Statement I** is false but **Statement II** is true
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** The Aristotelian syllogism is deductive and formal. The conclusion follows only from the form of the premises. It is not inductive.
- **Statement II is true.** The Nyāya syllogism has five parts (pañcāvayava). The third part, Udāharaṇa (example), gives a general rule with an example. For instance, "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen." So it joins deduction with induction.

Nyāya also cares about the truth of the content, not only the form. So it is formal-material. This makes Statement II true.

questions.question_md: An advantage to a business that uses Intranet capabilities is that it allows employees to share the business’s information with
questions.explanation:
An intranet is a private network inside an organisation. It uses internet technology, but only the organisation's own staff can use it.

So the main advantage is that employees can share the business's information **with each other**. Examples are notices, forms, documents and company policies.

- Customers and competitors are outside the organisation. They cannot use the intranet.
- Former employees no longer have access.

An extranet is the network that gives limited access to outside partners such as suppliers.

questions.question_md:
Consider the following MS-EXCEL screenshot that shows the product code, name of the state which produced the product and Quality of the product :

|   | A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Product Code | State | Quality |  |
| 2 | A1 | HP | A |  |
| 3 | A2 | MP | A |  |
| 4 | A3 | UP | A |  |
| 5 | A4 | UP | B |  |
| 6 | A5 | UP | B |  |
| 7 |  |  |  |  |

Which of the following EXCEL formulae can be typed in Cell D1 to answer the question : How many different product codes form UP are of Grade “A” quality ?

A. = COUNTIFS (B2:B6, "=UP", C2:C6,"=A")

B. = COUNTIFS (C2:C6, "=A", B2:B6,"=UP")

C. = COUNTIFS (B2:B6, "UP", C2:C6, "A")

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
COUNTIFS counts the rows that meet all the given conditions. Its form is COUNTIFS(range1, criteria1, range2, criteria2, …).

- **(A) works.** It counts rows where column B is "UP" and column C is "A".
- **(B) works.** It gives the same two conditions in a different order. The order of the range–criteria pairs does not change the result.
- **(C) works.** The criterion "UP" means the same as "=UP". Without an operator, Excel checks for equality.

All three formulas return 1. Only product A3 is from UP and has grade A. So the answer is (A), (B) and (C).

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** ‘Disk defragmentation’ makes files that are contiguous in a disk as fragmented.

**Statement II :** A device controller that controls a device will deal with the operating system through device driver.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are true
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are false
**Statement I** is true but **Statement II** is false
**Statement I** is false but **Statement II** is true
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is false.** A file becomes fragmented when its parts are stored in different places on the disk. Disk defragmentation does the opposite. It moves the parts of each file together, so they become contiguous (next to each other). This makes the disk read files faster.
- **Statement II is true.** A device controller is hardware that controls a device, such as a disk drive. The operating system does not talk to it directly. It uses a device driver. A device driver is software that understands the controller and gives the OS a standard way to use it.

So Statement I is false and Statement II is true.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements regarding Artificial Intelligence (AI) is/are correct ?

(A) AI systems can be used in email spam filters.

(B) AI systems are capable of analyzing uncertain information.

(C) An AI system is a system for capturing, storing, processing and displaying data related to positions on earth’s surface.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is correct.** Spam filters use AI methods such as machine learning. They learn which emails are likely to be spam.
- **(B) is correct.** AI systems can work with uncertain or incomplete information. They use methods such as probability, Bayesian networks and fuzzy logic.
- **(C) is incorrect.** This is the definition of a GIS (Geographic Information System). A GIS captures, stores, analyses and displays data about places on the earth's surface.

So only (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following features are available in word processing software such as MS-WORD ?

(A) Spell checker and Thesaurus

(B) Page Orientation

(C) Mail Merge

(D) Slide Transitions

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **(A) Spell checker and Thesaurus:** yes. MS-Word has both in the Review tab.
- **(B) Page Orientation:** yes. You can set portrait or landscape in the Layout tab.
- **(C) Mail Merge:** yes. It makes many personal letters or labels from one document and a list of addresses.
- **(D) Slide Transitions:** no. Transitions are effects between slides in presentation software such as MS-PowerPoint.

So the answer is (A), (B) and (C) only.

questions.question_md: Which one of the following is not caused by polluted water ?
questions.explanation:
Cholera, dysentery and typhoid are water-borne diseases. People get them by drinking water or eating food with germs from human waste.

**Tuberculosis** (TB) is different. A bacterium (*Mycobacterium tuberculosis*) causes it. TB spreads through the air. A sick person coughs or sneezes, and another person breathes in the germs. So polluted water does not cause TB.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Toxic chemicals often injure human organs and organ systems.

**Statement II :** Toxicants that damage kidneys are called as Hepatotoxic.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are correct
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are incorrect
**Statement I** is correct but **Statement II** is incorrect
**Statement I** is incorrect but **Statement II** is correct
questions.explanation:
- **Statement I is correct.** Many toxic chemicals damage organs such as the liver, kidneys, lungs and nervous system.
- **Statement II is incorrect.** "Hepato" means liver. So a hepatotoxic substance damages the liver. A toxicant that damages the kidneys is called **nephrotoxic** ("nephro" means kidney).

Other terms of this type are neurotoxic (nervous system) and cardiotoxic (heart).

So Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are related to ‘source reduction’ in integrated solid waste management ?

(A) Reduced Toxicity

(B) Composting

(C) Less Packaging

(D) Landfill

(E) More durable products

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Source reduction means making less waste in the first place. It is the top step in the waste management order. The order is: reduce, reuse, recycle, recover and then dispose.

- **(A) Reduced toxicity:** yes. Products contain fewer harmful substances, so the waste is less dangerous.
- **(B) Composting:** no. It treats waste after it is made. It is a form of recycling of organic waste.
- **(C) Less packaging:** yes. Less material enters the waste stream.
- **(D) Landfill:** no. It is the last step, the disposal of waste.
- **(E) More durable products:** yes. Products last longer, so people throw away fewer things.

So the answer is (A), (C) and (E).

questions.question_md:
Depletion of stratospheric ozone results into

(A) Increase in the ultraviolet radiation

(B) Increase in infra-red radiation

(C) Increase in skin cancer

(D) Significant impact on terrestrial flora and fauna

(E) Decrease in cataract cases

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the sun's ultraviolet-B (UV-B) radiation. When the ozone layer becomes thin, more UV radiation reaches the earth.

- **(A) More UV radiation:** true. This is the direct result.
- **(B) More infra-red radiation:** false. Ozone depletion does not change infra-red radiation much.
- **(C) More skin cancer:** true. UV-B damages the DNA in skin cells.
- **(D) Effect on plants and animals:** true. UV-B harms plants, plankton and animals on land and in water.
- **(E) Fewer cataract cases:** false. More UV radiation causes **more** cataracts (clouding of the eye lens).

So the answer is (A), (C) and (D).

questions.question_md:
Nitrous Oxide (N₂O).

(A) causes acid rain

(B) is laughing gas

(C) is carcinogenic

(D) is a green house gas

(E) is a criterion air pollutant

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Nitrous oxide (N₂O) is different from nitrogen dioxide (NO₂). Do not confuse the two gases.

- **(A) Acid rain:** no. NO₂ and other reactive nitrogen oxides form nitric acid. N₂O is quite stable in the lower atmosphere.
- **(B) Laughing gas:** yes. Doctors and dentists use N₂O as a mild anaesthetic.
- **(C) Carcinogenic:** no. N₂O is not classed as a cancer-causing substance.
- **(D) Greenhouse gas:** yes. It is one of the main greenhouse gases under the Kyoto Protocol. It also damages the ozone layer.
- **(E) Criterion air pollutant:** no. The criteria pollutants include NO₂, not N₂O.

So only (B) and (D) are correct.

questions.question_md: The Michael Sadler commission was constituted to study the problems of :
questions.explanation:
The Government of India set up the **Calcutta University Commission** in 1917. Sir Michael Sadler was its chairman, so people also call it the Sadler Commission.

It studied the problems of Calcutta University. Its suggestions also affected higher education across India. For example, it suggested a 12-year school stage before university. It also suggested a three-year degree course and more teaching universities.

The commission did not study Bombay, Madras or Poona universities.

questions.question_md: The National Education Policy, 1986 recommended the establishment of _________ in the country.
questions.explanation:
The National Policy on Education (NPE), 1986 gave great importance to distance education. It wanted to widen access to higher education. So it supported the open university system. The policy said that the Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU, set up in 1985) would be strengthened. It also wanted more open universities in the states.

- Community colleges became a policy idea much later.
- "Institutions of Eminence" is a much later scheme of 2017.
- Discipline-wise universities were not the main recommendation of NPE 1986.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** Curzon’s university reforms reflected the official attitude towards the spread of higher education in India.

**Statement II :** There was no resistance to the Indian universities Bill piloted by Curzon from any section of Indians.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are true
Both **Statement I** and **Statement II** are false
**Statement I** is true but **Statement II** is false
**Statement I** is false but **Statement II** is true
questions.explanation:
Lord Curzon brought the Indian Universities Act of 1904.

- **Statement I is true.** The reforms increased government control over universities. The government could approve or change senate decisions and affiliation of colleges. This showed the official wish to control and limit the spread of higher education.
- **Statement II is false.** Many Indians opposed the bill. Nationalist leaders such as Gopal Krishna Gokhale spoke against it in the Imperial Legislative Council. They saw it as an attempt to control Indian education.

So Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I (Ancient thinkers) | List - II (Area of study) |
|---|---|
| (A) Panini | (I) Astronomy |
| (B) Jivaka | (II) Grammar |
| (C) Bhaskara | (III) Medicine |
| (D) Kanada | (IV) Physics |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **(A) Panini – (II) Grammar.** He wrote the *Aṣṭādhyāyī*, the classic grammar of Sanskrit.
- **(B) Jivaka – (III) Medicine.** He was a famous physician in the time of the Buddha.
- **(C) Bhaskara – (I) Astronomy.** Bhaskaracharya wrote the *Siddhānta Śiromaṇi* on mathematics and astronomy.
- **(D) Kanada – (IV) Physics.** He founded the Vaiśeṣika school. He gave an early theory of atoms (paramāṇu).

The correct match is A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV. Option (1) wrongly links Panini with medicine. Options (2) and (4) wrongly link Jivaka with astronomy or physics.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I (Name of University) | List - II (Year of Establishment) |
|---|---|
| (A) Bombay University | (I) 1916 |
| (B) Delhi University | (II) 1943 |
| (C) Utkal University | (III) 1922 |
| (D) S.N.D.T. Women University | (IV) 1857 |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **(A) Bombay University – (IV) 1857.** Bombay, Calcutta and Madras universities started in 1857.
- **(B) Delhi University – (III) 1922.**
- **(C) Utkal University – (II) 1943.** It is in Odisha.
- **(D) S.N.D.T. Women's University – (I) 1916.** Dhondo Keshav Karve started it as the first women's university in India.

The correct match is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I. Remember that 1857 is the year of the first three modern universities. That fact removes options (2) and (4) quickly.

questions.question_md: Dinosaurs became extinct because of :
questions.explanation:
The passage says: "they became extinct because they could not adapt themselves to a world without swamps."

So the dinosaurs died out because of **lack of adaptability**. They could not change to fit a new environment.

The passage does not talk about an earthquake, heavy rain or extreme cold. These options come from general knowledge, not from the passage.

questions.question_md: In the scientific age who is responsible for the changing environment ?
questions.explanation:
The passage says: "man himself is creating the changes of environment to which he will have to adjust himself". It also says that man "through his scientific skill is the cause of the changes of environment".

So in the scientific age, **man** causes the changes in the environment.

The passage uses nature only to compare. It says that these man-made changes are like natural forces. But the cause is still human. Natural disasters and wars are not mentioned as causes.

questions.question_md: The main focus of the passage is on :
questions.explanation:
The passage starts with how science has changed human life. It ends with the need to use scientific thinking for human survival. All its ideas link **science and human life**.

- The extinction of species and of dinosaurs is only an example. It supports the main idea.
- The passage does not mention forests. It mentions only drained swamps.

questions.question_md: “If the answer is in the affirmative .......... ” refers to the question related to :
questions.explanation:
Look at the sentence just before the phrase. The passage says: "Whether men will be able to survive the changes of environment that their own skill has brought about is an open question."

Then it says: "If the answer is in the affirmative…". An affirmative answer means "yes". So "yes" is the answer to the question of whether humans will survive.

The question is about **human survival**. Human extinction is the negative side of the same question, not the question asked.

questions.question_md:
According to the passage the following are true :

(A) Science is bringing about rapid changes.

(B) There is every likelihood that a scientific plateau will be reached.

(C) Man will definitely perish like the Dinosaurs.

(D) There are chances that mankind may become extinct due to lack of adaptability.

(E) Changes in the environment made through human agencies have so far shown almost the same inexorable inevitability as that of natural forces.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Check each statement with the passage.

- **(A) True.** The passage says that science causes changes "at an increasing speed".
- **(B) False.** The passage says: "There is no sign of any new stability to be attained on some scientific plateau."
- **(C) False.** The passage calls human survival "an open question". It does not say that man will surely perish.
- **(D) True.** The passage asks whether the human race will "perish from lack of adaptability", like former species. So extinction is a real chance.
- **(E) True.** The passage says that human-made changes "have had so far something of the inexorable inevitability of natural forces".

So (A), (D) and (E) are true.
