groups.md:
Study carefully the table given below and answer the question asked here under.

A college has four programs B.A., B.Sc., B.Com. and B.B.A. The results of the mid-semester and end-semester tests are shown in the table given below.

| Results | B.A. | B.Sc. | B.Com. | B.B.A. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Failed in both tests | 28 | 23 | 17 | 27 |
| Failed in mid-semester test but passed in end-semester test | 14 | 12 | 8 | 13 |
| passed in mid-semester test but failed in end-semester test | 6 | 17 | 9 | 15 |
| Passed in both tests | 64 | 55 | 46 | 76 |

(Column values: Number of students)

Read the following passage and answer the questions :

Organized endeavors directed by people responsible for planning, organizing, leading and controlling activities have existed for thousands of years. The Egyptian pyramids and the Great Wall of China, for instance, are tangible evidence that projects of tremendous scope, employing tens of thousands of people, were undertaken well before modern times. The pyramids are a particularly interesting example. The construction of a single pyramid occupied more than 100,000 workers for 20 years. Who told each worker what to do ? Who ensured that there would be enough stones at the site to keep workers busy ? The answer to such questions is *managers*. Regardless of what managers were called at the time, someone had to plan what was to be done, organize people and materials to do it, lead and direct the workers, and impose some controls to ensure that everything was done as planned.

Another example of early management can be seen during the 1400s in the city of Venice, Italy, a major economic and trade center. The Venetians developed an early form of business enterprise and engaged in many activities common to today's organizations. For instance, at the arsenal of Venice, warships were floated along the canals, and at each stop materials and riggings were added to the ship. Doesn't that sound a lot like a car "floating" along an automobile assembly line while components are added to it ? In addition to this assembly line, the Venetians also used warehouse and inventory systems to keep track of materials, human resource management systems to manage the labor force, and an accounting system to keep track of revenues and costs.

questions.question_md: What is the ratio of number of students in B.Sc. program to the number of students in B.Com. program ?
questions.explanation:
Add the four rows of each column to get the number of students.

- B.Sc.: 23 + 12 + 17 + 55 = **107**.
- B.Com.: 17 + 8 + 9 + 46 = **80**.

The ratio B.Sc. : B.Com. is **107 : 80**. This ratio cannot be made smaller, because 107 is a prime number.

The option 80 : 107 has the right numbers in the wrong order. The number 131 is the total for B.B.A., not B.Com.

questions.question_md: Which program has the lowest passing percentage in end-semester test ?
questions.explanation:
A student passed the end-semester test in two rows. These rows are "failed mid, passed end" and "passed both".

- B.A.: 14 + 64 = 78 out of 112 → about 69.6%.
- B.Sc.: 12 + 55 = 67 out of 107 → about 62.6%.
- B.Com.: 8 + 46 = 54 out of 80 → 67.5%.
- B.B.A.: 13 + 76 = 89 out of 131 → about 67.9%.

**B.Sc.** has the lowest passing percentage. Always divide by the total of each program, because the programs have different sizes.

questions.question_md: How many students are there in the four programs ?
questions.explanation:
First find the total of each program. Add the four rows of each column.

- B.A.: 28 + 14 + 6 + 64 = 112.
- B.Sc.: 23 + 12 + 17 + 55 = 107.
- B.Com.: 17 + 8 + 9 + 46 = 80.
- B.B.A.: 27 + 13 + 15 + 76 = 131.

Total = 112 + 107 + 80 + 131 = **430**.

The value 420 or 330 comes from an error in addition. Each student is in exactly one row, so you must add all four rows.

questions.question_md: If the number of students passing a test be considered a criterion for comparison of difficulty level of two tests, then mid-semester test of which of the following programs was the least difficult ?
questions.explanation:
The test that more students pass is the least difficult test. A student passed the mid-semester test in two rows: "passed mid, failed end" and "passed both".

- B.A.: 6 + 64 = 70 out of 112 → 62.5%.
- B.Sc.: 17 + 55 = 72 out of 107 → about 67.3%.
- B.Com.: 9 + 46 = 55 out of 80 → about 68.8%.
- B.B.A.: 15 + 76 = 91 out of 131 → about 69.5%.

**B.B.A.** has the highest number and the highest percentage of passes. So its mid-semester test was the least difficult. Both ways of comparing give the same answer.

questions.question_md: Which program has the highest failure rate in the mid-semester test ?
questions.explanation:
A student failed the mid-semester test in two rows: "failed both" and "failed mid, passed end". Failure rate = failures ÷ total students.

- B.A.: 28 + 14 = 42 out of 112 → 37.5%.
- B.Sc.: 23 + 12 = 35 out of 107 → about 32.7%.
- B.Com.: 17 + 8 = 25 out of 80 → about 31.3%.
- B.B.A.: 27 + 13 = 40 out of 131 → about 30.5%.

**B.A.** has the highest failure rate. B.B.A. has a large number of failures (40), but it also has the most students. So its rate is the lowest.

questions.question_md:
Complete the following series :

N7V, K9T, H12R, \_\_?\_\_, B21N
questions.explanation:
Look at each part of the terms on its own.

- First letters: N, K, H, ?, B. The positions are 14, 11, 8, ?, 2. Each step is −3, so the missing letter is **E** (5).
- Numbers: 7, 9, 12, ?, 21. The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5. So the missing number is 12 + 4 = **16**. Then 16 + 5 = 21, which matches.
- Last letters: V, T, R, ?, N. Each step is −2 (22, 20, 18, 16, 14). So the missing letter is **P**.

The missing term is **E16P**. E14R and E13Q have the wrong number and last letter. F16R has the wrong first and last letters.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I (Department of Ashram) | List - II (Subject) |
|---|---|
| A. Vishnu Sthana | I. Military Education |
| B. Vivasta Sthana | II. Jyotish |
| C. Garun Sthana | III. Politics |
| D. Mahendra Sthana | IV. Travel and Transport |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
In ancient Indian ashrams, each department (sthāna) had the name of a deity. The subject of the department fits the role of that deity.

- **A. Vishnu Sthana – III. Politics.** Vishnu protects and rules the world, so his department taught politics and statecraft.
- **B. Vivasta Sthana – II. Jyotish.** Vivasvat is the Sun god. Jyotish (astronomy and astrology) studies the sun, moon and planets.
- **C. Garun Sthana – IV. Travel and Transport.** Garuda is the bird that carries Vishnu, so it stands for travel.
- **D. Mahendra Sthana – I. Military Education.** Mahendra (Indra) is the king of gods and the god of war.

Only option (3) has all four pairs.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are not true ?

A. In the argument from ignorance fallacy, something is accepted as true because it is not proven false.

B. In Hasty generalisation fallacy, a general truth is applied to a particular case ignoring its uniqueness.

C. In Begging the question fallacy, an event is wrongly accepted as the cause of some other event.

D. The fallacy of Amphiboly occurs in arguing from premises whose formulations are ambiguous because of their grammatical construction.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Check each statement against the standard definition of the fallacy.

- **A is true.** The argument from ignorance says that a claim is true because nobody has proved it false.
- **B is not true.** It describes the fallacy of **accident**. In accident, a general rule is applied to a special case. Hasty generalisation is the opposite. It draws a general rule from too few or untypical cases.
- **C is not true.** It describes the **false cause** fallacy. Begging the question assumes the conclusion in the premises.
- **D is true.** Amphiboly comes from bad grammar or loose sentence structure. The sentence then has two possible meanings.

The false statements are **B and C**. Options with A or D are wrong, because A and D are correct definitions.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I (Successive discounts) | List - II (Equivalent discount) |
|---|---|
| A. 10% and 15% | I. 28% |
| B. 20% and 30% | II. 32.5% |
| C. 10% and 20% | III. 23.5% |
| D. 10% and 25% | IV. 44% |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
For two successive discounts a% and b%, use this rule: equivalent discount = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

- **A.** 10 + 15 − 1.5 = **23.5%** → III.
- **B.** 20 + 30 − 6 = **44%** → IV.
- **C.** 10 + 20 − 2 = **28%** → I.
- **D.** 10 + 25 − 2.5 = **32.5%** → II.

The answer is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II. A common error is to add the two discounts directly. For example, 20% and 30% do not give 50%. The second discount applies only to the already reduced price.

questions.question_md: The theory that argues that media can have a strong influence in deciding the small number of public problems or issues that people will think about at any given point in time, is :
questions.explanation:
Agenda-Setting Theory comes from McCombs and Shaw (1972). It says that the media do not tell people what to think. But the media tell people what to think *about*. The media give much space to a few issues. People then think that these few issues are the most important ones.

- Knowledge-Gap Theory says that richer and more educated groups gain knowledge from media faster than other groups.
- Limited Effects Theory says that media have only a small direct effect on people.
- Personal Influence Theory says that other people (opinion leaders) influence us more than the media do.

questions.question_md: The smallest unit of information, a computer can understand and process is known as :
questions.explanation:
A **bit** (binary digit) is the smallest unit of data in a computer. A bit has only one of two values: 0 or 1. All data in a computer is made of bits.

- A nibble is 4 bits.
- A byte is 8 bits. It is the smallest unit that most computers use to store one character.
- "Digit" is a general word for a number sign (0–9). It is not a unit of computer information.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following is/are true :

A. The conversion of an O proposition is valid.

B. The conversion of an A proposition is an A proposition.

C. The conversion of an E proposition is conversion by limitation.

D. The conversion of an I proposition is valid.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Conversion swaps the subject and the predicate of a proposition. The conversion is valid only if no term becomes distributed in the converse without being distributed in the original.

- **A is false.** "Some S is not P" (O) cannot be converted. The term S would become distributed in the converse.
- **B is false.** "All S is P" (A) converts only to "Some P is S", an I proposition. This is conversion by limitation.
- **C is false.** "No S is P" (E) converts simply to "No P is S". This is simple conversion, not conversion by limitation.
- **D is true.** "Some S is P" (I) converts validly to "Some P is S".

So only **D** is true.

questions.question_md: As per the recommendations of National Education Policy, 2020, all stand alone teacher education institutions will be required to convert into multidisciplinary institutions by :
questions.explanation:
NEP 2020 wants teacher education to happen inside multidisciplinary institutions. A stand-alone teacher education institution (TEI) teaches only teacher education. The policy says that all such stand-alone TEIs must become multidisciplinary institutions by **2030**.

The year 2030 is also the year when the 4-year integrated B.Ed. becomes the minimum degree for school teachers.

Do not confuse this with the year 2040. By 2040, NEP 2020 wants all higher education institutions to be multidisciplinary.

questions.question_md: Which of the following represents the ontological orientation of qualitative research strategies ?
questions.explanation:
Ontology is about the nature of social reality. Qualitative research usually takes a **constructionist** view. Constructionism says that people create social reality through their interactions and meanings. Social reality is not a fixed thing outside people.

- **Objectivism** is the ontology of quantitative research. It says that social facts exist independently of people.
- **Positivism** is an epistemological position. Epistemology is about how we know things, not about what exists.
- **Deductive** describes how theory and research link (testing a theory). It is not an ontology. Qualitative research is mostly inductive.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I | List - II |
|---|---|
| A. Rhetorical | I. Considering communication to be discursive reflection on hegemonic ideological forces |
| B. Semiotic | II. Considering communication to be the capacity of experiencing otherness through authentic dialogue |
| C. Phenomenological | III. Considering communication to be Practical Art |
| D. Critical | IV. Considering communication to be Intersubjective Mediation via Signs |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
These are four of Robert Craig's seven traditions of communication theory.

- **A. Rhetorical – III.** It sees communication as a practical art of discourse. A speaker uses it to persuade an audience.
- **B. Semiotic – IV.** It sees communication as intersubjective mediation by signs. Signs carry shared meaning between people.
- **C. Phenomenological – II.** It sees communication as the experience of otherness through authentic dialogue.
- **D. Critical – I.** It sees communication as discursive reflection. This reflection questions hegemonic (dominant) ideologies and power.

So the answer is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I. The other options mix up the rhetorical, phenomenological and critical traditions.

questions.question_md: Measurement validity primarily relates to :
questions.explanation:
Measurement validity asks one question: does a measure really measure the concept that it should measure? For example, does an IQ test really measure intelligence?

This idea belongs mainly to **quantitative research**. Quantitative research turns concepts into numbers through indicators and scales. So it must check that these measures are valid.

Qualitative researchers often say that measurement is not their main aim. They use other criteria, such as trustworthiness and authenticity. Interpretivism and constructionism are philosophical positions linked to qualitative research. They are not the main home of measurement validity.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following greenhouse gases in the increasing order of their life time in the earth's atmosphere :

A. SF₆

B. N₂O

C. H₂O vapor

D. CH₄

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The lifetime of a gas is the average time that it stays in the atmosphere. Approximate values are:

- **C. Water vapour:** about 9 days. It quickly falls as rain or snow.
- **D. Methane (CH₄):** about 12 years.
- **B. Nitrous oxide (N₂O):** about 110–120 years.
- **A. Sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆):** about 3,000 years or more.

So the increasing order is **C, D, B, A**.

Option (2) puts SF₆ before N₂O, which is wrong. SF₆ is one of the longest-lived greenhouse gases. Options (3) and (4) start with long-lived gases, so they are wrong.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A) :** The terms validity and invalidity do not apply to inductive arguments.

**Reason (R) :** In an inductive argument, the conclusion does not have sufficient ground in the premises.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation:
Logicians use "valid" and "invalid" only for deductive arguments.

- **(A) is correct.** In a valid deductive argument, true premises guarantee a true conclusion. Inductive arguments never give this guarantee. So we call them strong or weak, or more or less probable, not valid or invalid.
- **(R) is correct.** In an inductive argument, the conclusion goes beyond the premises. The premises give some support, but not sufficient (conclusive) ground. The conclusion can be false even when the premises are true.

(R) gives the reason for (A). The premises never fully support the conclusion. So the terms validity and invalidity, which are about full support, do not apply.

questions.question_md: Which of the following is an example of biological motive ?
questions.explanation:
A biological (primary) motive comes from the needs of the body. People do not learn it. Hunger, thirst, sleep and the need to avoid pain are biological motives.

Achievement, power and affiliation are social (secondary) motives. People learn them through life in society. For example, the need for achievement depends on family, culture and education. McClelland studied these three social motives.

questions.question_md:
Identify the correct mathematical statements :

A. The value of 1/4 + 1/(4×5) + 1/(4×5×6) is equal to 37/120.

B. 1 + 2 ÷ {1 + 2 ÷ (1 + 1/3)} is equal to 4/5.

C. If the average of 6 numbers is 7, the average of 3 numbers of them is 5, then the average of remaining numbers is 9.

D. If 75% of a number is added to 75, then the result is number itself. Then the number is 300

E. Largest fraction from 9/31, 6/23, 3/17, 4/11 is 9/31.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Check each statement.

- **A is true.** 1/4 + 1/20 + 1/120 = 30/120 + 6/120 + 1/120 = **37/120**.
- **B is false.** Start inside: 1 + 1/3 = 4/3. Then 2 ÷ 4/3 = 3/2. Then 1 + 3/2 = 5/2. Then 2 ÷ 5/2 = 4/5. The last step gives 1 + 4/5 = **9/5**, not 4/5.
- **C is true.** The sum of 6 numbers = 6 × 7 = 42. The sum of 3 numbers = 15. The other 3 numbers add to 27, so their average = **9**.
- **D is true.** 0.75x + 75 = x, so 0.25x = 75 and x = **300**.
- **E is false.** 4/11 ≈ 0.364 is larger than 9/31 ≈ 0.290.

The true statements are **A, C and D**. Option (4) wrongly includes E.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A) :** People, who hold views contrary to those dominant in the media, keep those views to themselves.

**Reason (R) :** Such people fear isolation or separation from those around them.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation:
These statements describe the **Spiral of Silence** theory of Elisabeth Noelle-Neumann.

- **(A) is correct.** Some people see that their view differs from the view in the media. These people often stay silent.
- **(R) is correct.** The theory says that people fear isolation. They do not want other people to reject them. So they watch the "climate of opinion" and keep quiet when they think they are in the minority.

The fear of isolation is the cause of the silence. So (R) correctly explains (A). As more people stay silent, the dominant view looks even stronger. This makes a "spiral".

questions.question_md: Which of the following explains the fallacy (hetvābhāsa) of satpratipakṣa correctly ?
options: A fallacy where an inference is contradicted by perception or some other non-inferential prāmāṇa.
A fallacy where one inference is contradicted by another inference.
A fallacy that disproves the very proposition which it is meant to prove.
A fallacy of the irregular middle
questions.explanation:
In Nyāya logic, a hetvābhāsa is a fallacious reason (a reason that only looks valid). **Satpratipakṣa** means "counter-balanced reason". One inference proves a conclusion. Another inference of equal strength proves the opposite conclusion. The two inferences cancel each other.

The other options describe other hetvābhāsas:

- An inference contradicted by perception or another pramāṇa is **bādhita** (also called kālātyayāpadiṣṭa).
- A reason that proves the opposite of what it should prove is **viruddha** (contradictory).
- The irregular middle is **savyabhicāra** (anaikāntika). Here the reason goes with both the presence and the absence of the thing to be proved.

questions.question_md: Two cyclists cover the same distance at 15 km/hr and 16 km/hr, respectively. If one cyclist takes 16 minutes longer than the other, then the distance travelled by each cyclist is :
questions.explanation:
Let the distance be d km. Time = distance ÷ speed. The slower cyclist takes 16 minutes longer. 16 minutes = 16/60 = 4/15 hour.

d/15 − d/16 = 4/15

The left side is (16d − 15d) / 240 = d/240.

So d/240 = 4/15, and d = 240 × 4/15 = **64 km**.

Check: 64/15 h = 256 minutes, and 64/16 h = 240 minutes. The difference is 16 minutes. The other distances do not give a 16-minute difference.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following are application software ?

A. Spreadsheet

B. Word Processor

C. Operating system

D. Database

E. Compiler

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Application software helps the user do a specific task. System software runs and controls the computer itself.

- **A. Spreadsheet** (for example, Excel) – application software.
- **B. Word processor** (for example, Word) – application software.
- **C. Operating system** (for example, Windows) – system software.
- **D. Database** program (for example, Access) – application software.
- **E. Compiler** – a programming tool. It translates code into machine language. Most textbooks list it under system software.

So **A, B and D** are application software. Every other option includes the operating system or the compiler.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I | List - II |
|---|---|
| A. Phishing | I. Act of gaining unauthorized access |
| B. Hacking | II. Unsolicited email sent over the internet to a recipient on a mailing list |
| C. Spam | III. Small file or code stored on user's computer |
| D. Cookies | IV. The creator sends out legitimate-looking emails to target users |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Match each term with its meaning.

- **A. Phishing – IV.** The attacker sends emails that look real, for example from a bank. The aim is to steal passwords or money.
- **B. Hacking – I.** Hacking means getting unauthorised access to a computer or network.
- **C. Spam – II.** Spam is unwanted (unsolicited) email sent to many people on a mailing list.
- **D. Cookies – III.** A cookie is a small file that a website stores on the user's computer.

So the answer is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III. Option (2) wrongly matches spam with cookies.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A) :** A wind mill will be more effective if it is placed at a higher elevation above the ground than a lower one.

**Reason (R) :** Generally, the wind speed increases with altitude above the earth's surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation:
- **(R) is correct.** Near the ground, trees, buildings and hills slow down the wind through friction. Higher up, there is less friction, so the wind is usually faster.
- **(A) is correct.** For this reason, wind turbines stand on tall towers.

The power in the wind depends on the cube of the wind speed. So a small rise in speed gives a large rise in power. For example, double the speed gives eight times the power.

So (R) correctly explains (A). A wind mill at a higher place gets faster wind and makes more energy.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following in the ascending order of adoption in terms of Diffusion of Innovation among the masses :

A. Opinion Followers

B. Opinion Leaders

C. Early Adopters

D. Change Agents

E. Laggards

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The question asks for the order in which groups adopt an innovation, from first to last. This follows the idea of Diffusion of Innovation by Everett Rogers.

- **D. Change agents** come first. They bring the new idea into the community.
- **C. Early adopters** take up the idea soon after.
- **B. Opinion leaders** then accept it. Other people respect them and copy them.
- **A. Opinion followers** adopt it after they see the opinion leaders use it.
- **E. Laggards** come last. They resist change.

So the order is **D, C, B, A, E**. Options that start with opinion followers, or put them before leaders, are wrong. Followers copy leaders, so they cannot come before them.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following in increasing order in terms of their coverage :

A. PAN

B. MAN

C. WAN

D. LAN

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.notes: Dropped in the NTA final answer key.
questions.explanation:
Networks differ in the area they cover.

- **PAN** (Personal Area Network): a few metres, for example Bluetooth.
- **LAN** (Local Area Network): one building or campus.
- **MAN** (Metropolitan Area Network): a city.
- **WAN** (Wide Area Network): a country or the whole world.

So the correct increasing order is **A, D, B, C** (PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN). None of the four options gives this order. This is the likely reason why NTA dropped the question and gave marks to all.

Option (3), A, D, C, B, is the closest choice. It has PAN and LAN in the right places but swaps MAN and WAN. Option (2) has a similar single error, so the choice is open to debate.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I | List - II |
|---|---|
| A. Primary Air pollutant | I. Peroxyacyl nitrate |
| B. Secondary Air pollutant | II. Carbon monoxide |
| C. Ozone depleting substance | III. Aerosols |
| D. Cloud Condensation Nuclei | IV. Chlorofluorocarbons |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **A. Primary air pollutant – II. Carbon monoxide.** A primary pollutant comes directly from a source. Vehicles release carbon monoxide (CO) directly.
- **B. Secondary air pollutant – I. Peroxyacyl nitrate (PAN).** A secondary pollutant forms in the air by chemical reactions. PAN forms in photochemical smog from nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons in sunlight.
- **C. Ozone depleting substance – IV. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).** CFCs release chlorine in the stratosphere. Chlorine destroys ozone.
- **D. Cloud condensation nuclei – III. Aerosols.** Water vapour condenses on tiny particles (aerosols) to form cloud droplets.

So the answer is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.question_md: Journals that prioritize self-interest at the expense of scholarship and are characterized by false or misleading information, deviation from best editorial/publication practices, lack of transparency and and/or use of aggressive and indiscriminate solicitation practices, are known as :
questions.explanation:
This is the consensus definition of **predatory journals**. A group of scholars agreed on it in 2019. Predatory journals take publication fees from authors. But they do not give proper peer review or editing. They often send many spam emails to invite papers.

- **Open access journals** make articles free to read. Many open access journals are honest and high quality. Open access alone does not mean predatory.
- **Proprietary journals** belong to a publisher and usually need a subscription.
- **Professional journals** serve members of a profession.

questions.question_md: The issue related to 'traditional knowledge societies and their livelihood' is addressed in the National Mission for \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.explanation:
India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC, 2008) has eight national missions. The **National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem** protects the Himalayan region. Its topics include glaciers, biodiversity, wildlife, and **traditional knowledge societies and their livelihood**. Many mountain communities depend on this traditional knowledge.

- The Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency deals with energy saving in industry.
- The Mission on Sustainable Habitat deals with buildings, urban transport and waste in cities.
- The Green India Mission deals with forests and tree cover.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A) :** National Education Policy, 2020 (NEP-2020) visualized 'Research-Intensive Universities'.

**Reason (R) :** NEP-2020 envisioned university as a place which lays equal emphasis on teaching and research.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is correct.** NEP 2020 describes three types of higher education institutions. These are Research-Intensive Universities, Teaching-Intensive Universities, and Autonomous degree-granting Colleges.
- **(R) is correct.** NEP 2020 says that Research-Intensive Universities give equal importance to teaching and research.

The idea of a university with equal stress on teaching and research is the basis of the "Research-Intensive University". So (R) explains why NEP 2020 includes this type of university. The examiner treats (R) as the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_md:
Arrange the steps of creative thinking process in correct sequence :

A. Preparation

B. Evaluation

C. Illumination

D. Revision

E. Incubation

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Graham Wallas (1926) gave a four-stage model of creative thinking. Later writers added a final stage of revision.

1. **A. Preparation** – collect information and study the problem.
2. **E. Incubation** – stop working on the problem consciously. The mind works on it in the background.
3. **C. Illumination** – the new idea suddenly appears (the "aha" moment).
4. **B. Evaluation** – test the idea to see if it works. Wallas called this stage verification.
5. **D. Revision** – improve the idea after the test.

So the order is **A, E, C, B, D**. Illumination cannot come before incubation, and evaluation needs an idea first.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following fractions in ascending order :

A. 2/3

B. 7/19

C. 9/11

D. 8/9

E. 7/9

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Change each fraction into a decimal.

- B. 7/19 ≈ 0.368
- A. 2/3 ≈ 0.667
- E. 7/9 ≈ 0.778
- C. 9/11 ≈ 0.818
- D. 8/9 ≈ 0.889

The ascending order (smallest to largest) is **B, A, E, C, D**.

Option (2) puts 7/9 before 2/3, but 7/9 is larger. Option (4) puts 9/11 before 2/3, which is also wrong.

questions.question_md:
Identify the advantages of closed ended questions in survey research :

A. It is easy to process answers.

B. Respondents can answer in their own terms.

C. They are easy for the respondents to complete.

D. They allow unusual responses to be derived.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
A closed-ended question gives the respondent fixed answer choices.

- **A. Easy to process answers – advantage.** The answers are already in categories, so coding and analysis are quick.
- **B. Respondents can answer in their own terms – not an advantage of closed questions.** This is an advantage of open questions.
- **C. Easy for respondents to complete – advantage.** The respondent only ticks a box.
- **D. Unusual responses can come out – not an advantage of closed questions.** Fixed choices cannot capture unexpected answers. Open questions can.

So **A and C** are the advantages. The options with B or D mix in the strengths of open questions.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I (Types Categorical propositions) | List - II (Explanation) |
|---|---|
| A. A proposition | I. Distributes both subject and predicate terms |
| B. E proposition | II. Distributes only predicate term |
| C. I proposition | III. Distributes only subject term |
| D. O proposition | IV. Distributes neither subject nor predicate term |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
A term is distributed when the proposition says something about every member of that class.

- **A (All S is P) – III.** It distributes only the subject.
- **E (No S is P) – I.** It distributes both subject and predicate.
- **I (Some S is P) – IV.** It distributes neither term.
- **O (Some S is not P) – II.** It distributes only the predicate.

A simple memory aid: universal propositions (A, E) distribute the subject. Negative propositions (E, O) distribute the predicate.

So the answer is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I | List - II |
|---|---|
| A. Independent variable in true experimental design | I. Outcome variable |
| B. Dependent variable | II. Control variable |
| C. Intervening variable | III. Spurious variable |
| D. Confounding variable | IV. Stands between independent variable and dependent variable |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
- **A. Independent variable in a true experiment – II. Control variable.** In a true experiment, the researcher controls (manipulates) the independent variable. So the examiner calls it the controlled variable.
- **B. Dependent variable – I. Outcome variable.** It shows the effect, or outcome, of the independent variable.
- **C. Intervening variable – IV.** It stands between the independent and the dependent variable and links them.
- **D. Confounding variable – III. Spurious variable.** It is an outside variable that affects both variables. It can create a false (spurious) link between them.

Note: in many textbooks, "control variable" means a variable that the researcher keeps constant. But B-I and C-IV are certain. Only option (2) has both of them, so the answer is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.question_md: Active Audience Theories focus on assessing what \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.explanation:
Active audience theories say that the audience is not passive. People choose media and use them for their own needs. The best-known example is the **Uses and Gratifications** approach. It asks what **people do with media**. For example, people use media for information, entertainment, or social contact.

The opposite view is found in older "effects" theories, such as the hypodermic needle model. These theories ask what **media do to people**. The other two options are about media administration and regulation, not about the audience.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following pairs of standard deviation (σ) and total number of samples (n) pertaining to different sampling distributions in the decreasing order of their standard error.

A. σ = 1.6, n = 16

B. σ = 1.5, n = 25

C. σ = 0.6, n = 36

D. σ = 1.4, n = 49

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Standard error of the mean = σ ÷ √n.

- **A:** 1.6 ÷ √16 = 1.6 ÷ 4 = **0.40**
- **B:** 1.5 ÷ √25 = 1.5 ÷ 5 = **0.30**
- **C:** 0.6 ÷ √36 = 0.6 ÷ 6 = **0.10**
- **D:** 1.4 ÷ √49 = 1.4 ÷ 7 = **0.20**

The decreasing order is 0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10. That is **A, B, D, C**.

Option (1) puts C before D, but C has the smallest error. Options (3) and (4) give an increasing order, not a decreasing order.

questions.question_md:
Match **List - I** with **List - II**.

| List - I (Type of Development) | List - II (Related with) |
|---|---|
| A. Psycho-sexual Development | I. Identity vs. Role Confusion |
| B. Psycho-social Development | II. Anal Stage |
| C. Cognitive Development | III. Hypothetical-deductive reasoning |
| D. Moral Development | IV. Resolving ethical dilemma |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
Each theory of development has typical stages or ideas.

- **A. Psycho-sexual development – II. Anal stage.** Freud's stages are oral, anal, phallic, latency and genital.
- **B. Psycho-social development – I. Identity vs. role confusion.** This is Erikson's fifth stage, in adolescence.
- **C. Cognitive development – III. Hypothetical-deductive reasoning.** Piaget says that this reasoning appears in the formal operational stage.
- **D. Moral development – IV. Resolving ethical dilemma.** Kohlberg studied moral stages by asking people to solve moral dilemmas, such as the Heinz dilemma.

So the answer is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

questions.question_md: The oxygen consumed in the oxidation of an organic compound by microorganisms in the aquatic ecosystem is called \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.explanation:
**Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)** is the amount of oxygen that microorganisms use to break down organic matter in water. A high BOD means that the water has much organic pollution.

- **Dissolved oxygen (DO)** is the oxygen that is present in the water. It does not measure how much oxygen microbes use.
- **Chemical oxygen demand (COD)** measures the oxygen needed to oxidise matter with a strong chemical, not with microorganisms.
- **Theoretical oxygen demand** is a value calculated from the chemical formula of a compound.

questions.question_md: Which term is NOT related to computer hardware ?
questions.explanation:
Hardware is the physical part of a computer that you can touch. Software is a set of programs.

- **Windows** is an operating system made by Microsoft. It is software, not hardware.
- A **bus** is a set of wires that carries data between parts of the computer. It is hardware.
- A **switch** is a network device that connects computers in a network. It is hardware.
- A **mouse** is an input device. It is hardware.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A) :** The projective techniques offer an approach to the measurement of the personality, which is different from the self-descriptive inventories.

**Reason (R) :** Self-descriptive inventories require the subject to describe himself/herself while assessing personality.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.notes: NTA final answer key accepts options 1, 2.
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is correct.** Self-descriptive inventories (questionnaires) ask direct questions about the person. Projective techniques, such as the Rorschach inkblot test or the TAT, use unclear (ambiguous) pictures or words. The person "projects" hidden needs and feelings into the answers. So the two approaches are different.
- **(R) is correct.** In an inventory, the subject describes himself or herself, for example by answering "yes" or "no".

(R) shows the key point of difference. Inventories depend on direct self-description, and projective tests do not. So (R) can explain (A).

But (R) talks only about inventories. It says nothing about how projective techniques work. So some candidates argued that (R) is not a full explanation. NTA accepted both readings and gave marks for options (1) and (2).

questions.question_md: Which among the following is the most liberal Open Education Resource license ?
questions.explanation:
Creative Commons (CC) licences give rules for reusing open education resources. **CC-BY** (Attribution) is the most liberal (open) of these four licences. Users can copy, change and even sell the work. They must only give credit to the creator.

The other licences add a limit to CC-BY:

- **CC-BY-SA** (ShareAlike): new works must use the same licence.
- **CC-BY-ND** (NoDerivatives): users cannot change the work.
- **CC-BY-NC** (NonCommercial): users cannot use the work for profit.

Each added condition makes the licence less liberal.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following senior functionaries of a central university in the correct hierarchal order :

A. Visitor

B. Dean of the faculty

C. Chancellor

D. Head of Department

E. Vice-Chancellor

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The order of authority in a central university, from highest to lowest, is:

1. **A. Visitor** – the President of India is the Visitor of central universities.
2. **C. Chancellor** – the formal head of the university. The Chancellor presides over the convocation.
3. **E. Vice-Chancellor** – the chief executive and academic head who runs the university.
4. **B. Dean of the faculty** – heads a faculty, which is a group of related departments.
5. **D. Head of Department** – heads one department inside a faculty.

So the order is **A, C, E, B, D**. Option (1) puts the Head of Department above the Dean, which is wrong. Option (2) puts the Chancellor above the Visitor.

questions.question_md: The reader learns from the given passage that :
options: The title of manager is an ancient one.
People directing organised endeavors can be seen down the ages.
The assembly line system was prevalent in China, Egypt and Italy.
questions.explanation:
The passage says that people who plan, organise, lead and control activities "have existed for thousands of years". It gives examples from ancient Egypt, China and 15th-century Venice. So people directing organised work can be seen **down the ages**.

- "Management is a recent creation" is the opposite of the passage.
- The title of manager is not ancient. The passage says: "Regardless of what managers were called at the time". So the title is not the point.
- The passage links the assembly line only to Venice, not to China or Egypt.

questions.question_md: According to the passage, persons responsible for the control, organisation and planning have been directing organised endeavors :
questions.explanation:
The first sentence of the passage gives the answer. Organised work directed by people who plan, organise, lead and control "has existed for **thousands of years**".

The other options take numbers from other parts of the passage:

- The 1400s is the time of the Venice example only.
- 100,000 is the number of workers on one pyramid, not a number of years.
- Twenty years is the time to build one pyramid.

questions.question_md: The passage documents that Egyptions involved in the construction of pyramids had :
options: An inventary system to keep record of the stones.
A plan for what was to be done.
An accounting system to keep the record of money.
A warehouse system to manage materials.
questions.explanation:
About the pyramids, the passage says: "someone had to **plan what was to be done**, organize people and materials… lead… and impose some controls". So the Egyptians had a plan for what was to be done.

The other options describe Venice, not Egypt. The passage says that the Venetians used warehouse and inventory systems and an accounting system. Do not mix the two examples.

questions.question_md: According to the passage, the role of a manager includes all of the following, except :
options: Planning what is to be done
Organising people for the pyramids site
questions.explanation:
The passage lists four tasks of managers at the pyramids. They plan what is to be done, organise people and materials, lead and direct the workers, and control the work.

**Stacking stones** is the physical work of the workers, not of the managers. The passage asks who made sure that there were enough stones to keep workers busy. That was the manager's job. But the workers placed the stones.

Planning, organising people and directing the work force are all manager tasks in the passage.

questions.question_md: According to the passage, the ancient equivalent of the assembly line was used in :
questions.explanation:
The passage describes the arsenal of **Venice** in the 1400s. Warships floated along the canals. At each stop, workers added materials and riggings to the ship. The passage compares this with a car moving along a modern assembly line.

Egypt, Giza and China appear only as examples of large ancient projects, such as the pyramids and the Great Wall. The passage does not link them to an assembly line.
