questions.explanation:
Link each biosphere reserve with its state.

- **A. Nanda Devi** → IV. Uttarakhand. It lies around the Nanda Devi peak in the Himalayas.
- **B. Pachmarhi** → III. Madhya Pradesh. It lies in the Satpura range.
- **C. Simlipal** → I. Odisha. It is in the Mayurbhanj district.
- **D. Nokrek** → II. Meghalaya. It is in the Garo Hills.

So the match is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.question_md:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**.

**Assertion (A) :** VoIP is an acronym that stands for Voice over Internet Protocol.

**Reason (R) :** VoIP is a technology that allows you to make voice calls using a broadband Internet connection instead of a regular phone call.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate answer** from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation:
- **(A) is correct.** VoIP stands for Voice over Internet Protocol.
- **(R) is correct.** VoIP lets you make voice calls over a broadband internet connection. It does not use a normal telephone line. Apps such as WhatsApp calls and Skype use VoIP.

(R) explains what the name in (A) means. "Voice over Internet Protocol" means that the voice travels as data packets over the internet. (R) describes exactly this. So the examiner treats (R) as the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_md: A smart classroom is a :
questions.explanation:
A smart classroom uses ICT (Information and Communication Technology) to support teaching and learning. It has tools such as a projector, an interactive board, a computer, the internet and digital content.

- A smart classroom can be teacher-centric or learner-centric. Technology alone does not decide this.
- Flipped and blended learning are teaching methods. They can use a smart classroom, but they do not define it.

The one feature that every smart classroom has is ICT support.

questions.question_md:
Select the correct statements :

A. Teachers in HEIs must be strict disciplinarian.

B. Teachers in HEIs must motivate her learners to learn independently.

C. Teachers in HEIs must not use any technology.

D. Teachers in HEIs must not interact with students outside classroom.

E. Teachers in HEIs must be an avid reader and a participant in her discipline's discourse.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C, D and E
questions.explanation:
Check each statement against good practice in higher education institutions (HEIs).

- **A. False.** A teacher needs discipline in class, but a "strict disciplinarian" style does not help adult learners.
- **B. True.** A good teacher motivates learners to learn on their own.
- **C. False.** Teachers should use technology where it helps learning.
- **D. False.** Contact outside class, for example mentoring, helps students.
- **E. True.** A teacher must read widely and take part in the debates of the subject.

So only B and E are correct.

questions.question_md: Which of the following University is NOT amongst the first three Universities opened in India in 1857 ?
questions.explanation:
In 1857, the British set up the first three modern universities in India. They were in Calcutta, Bombay and Madras. They followed the model of the University of London. Wood's Despatch (1854) had recommended them.

The **University of Delhi** started much later, in 1922. So it is not one of the first three.

questions.question_md: The capitalist countries perform even better as compared to the socialism because it is based on :
questions.explanation:
The passage says, "the Capitalist system is based on **private property and voluntary exchange**". It also says that capitalist countries show better results.

- "Public property" is the opposite. The passage links government ownership with socialism.
- "Involuntary exchange" also goes against the passage. The passage praises voluntary choice and rejects force.

questions.question_md: The fundamental value in inter-personal human relationships in society is __________.
options: feeling of over dependence on others
respect for the dignity of each person
questions.explanation:
The passage says that a system can be upheld only by "ensuring respect for the dignity and individuality of each person". It then says that gentle urging, reasoning and convincing should replace force. It calls this "the fundamental value in inter-personal human relationships in society".

So the answer is **respect for the dignity of each person**.

- The passage speaks of personal freedom, not collective freedom.
- It does not mention over-dependence on others.
- It does not mention external agencies.

questions.question_md: No socialist country has been able to realise the aims of socialism because :
options: It shows narrow and vested interests only.
People enjoy more freedom and prsoperity in capitalism.
It is made corrupt by incompetent rulers.
Its good and moral qualities are not sustained.
questions.explanation:
The passage says, "No political system can succeed unless its good and moral qualities are sustained". This explains why socialist countries failed to reach their aims.

- The passage rejects the idea that wicked and incompetent rulers made socialism corrupt. So that option is wrong.
- "Narrow and vested interests" is what people wrongly think about capitalism, not socialism.
- More freedom under capitalism is a comparison. It is not the reason why socialism failed.

questions.question_md: The advocates of socialism believe that equality can be ensured through :
options: equal distribution of the profit to all
questions.explanation:
The first line of the passage says, "Socialism aims at equality and social justice through **government ownership** and control over the means of production."

- The passage does not mention a mixed economy.
- It does not mention equal distribution of profit.
- It does not mention a public-private partnership model.

These three options add ideas that are not in the passage.

questions.question_md: According to the passage, the key to success in any political system lies with its __________.
options: people who are always concerned about their rights
people who use criticality to analyse government sponsored schemes and policies
questions.explanation:
The passage says, "No political system can succeed unless its **good and moral qualities** are sustained". So success depends on these qualities.

- "Hard work and perseverance" do not appear in the passage. The word "only" makes this option even weaker.
- The passage talks about respect for each person's rights. But it does not say that success depends on people who always worry about their rights.
- The passage does not talk about criticism of government schemes.

papers.instructions_note: 50 compulsory questions, 2 marks each

source.answer_key_notes: Answers from red-pen annotations on a candidate response sheet (prepp.in); not an official NTA key

groups.md:
Study the following table and answer the questions 01 to 05.

The following table shows the constitution of students' population on the basis of certain demographic variables in four colleges:

| College | Total no. of students | Rural : Urban | Male : Female | Percentage of Post-graduate within females |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 400 | 3:7 | 7:3 | 40% |
| B | 500 | 1:4 | 4:1 | 60% |
| C | 700 | 3:4 | 4:3 | 50% |
| D | 600 | 1:1 | 2:1 | 30% |

The workforce has become increasingly more diverse and this trend toward diversity will continue. This includes increasing diversity along racial, ethnic and gender lines, as well as an increasing percentage of the workforce that is over age fifty-five. Effectively managing diversity has been identified as one of five distinguishing features of organizations that make it onto Fortune magazine's list of 100 Best Companies. Diversity issues have several implications for HRD professionals. First, organizations need to address racial, ethnic and other prejudices that may persist, as well as cultural insensitivity and language differences. Second, with the increasing numbers of women in the workforce, organizations should continue to provide developmental opportunities that will prepare women for advancement into the senior ranks and provide safeguards against sexual harassment. Third, the ageing of the workforce highlights the importance of creating HRD programs that recognize and address the learning-related needs of both younger and older workers. Diversity can be a catalyst for improved organizational performance - though this is far from a sure thing!

questions.question_md: Total urban population of the students in colleges A and B is how much percent of total population of these two colleges?
questions.explanation:
Find the urban students in each college from the Rural : Urban ratio.

- College A: 3:7, so urban = 7/10 × 400 = 280.
- College B: 1:4, so urban = 4/5 × 500 = 400.

Total urban = 280 + 400 = 680.
Total students = 400 + 500 = 900.

Percentage = 680 ÷ 900 × 100 = **75.56%**.

The value 24.44% is the rural share (100 − 75.56). The other values do not come from these numbers.

questions.question_md: What is the total number of urban students in all the four colleges?
questions.explanation:
Use the Rural : Urban ratio for each college. The urban share is the second part of the ratio.

- A: 7/10 × 400 = 280
- B: 4/5 × 500 = 400
- C: 4/7 × 700 = 400
- D: 1/2 × 600 = 300

Total urban students = 280 + 400 + 400 + 300 = **1380**.

The total of all students is 2200. So the rural students are 2200 − 1380 = 820. The option 820 is the rural total, not the urban total.

questions.question_md: What percentage of total number of female students in the colleges B, C and D are post-graduate?
questions.explanation:
First find the female students from the Male : Female ratio. Then apply the post-graduate (PG) percentage.

- B: females = 1/5 × 500 = 100. PG = 60% of 100 = 60.
- C: females = 3/7 × 700 = 300. PG = 50% of 300 = 150.
- D: females = 1/3 × 600 = 200. PG = 30% of 200 = 60.

Total females = 100 + 300 + 200 = 600.
Total PG females = 60 + 150 + 60 = 270.

Percentage = 270 ÷ 600 × 100 = **45%**.

Do not take a simple average of 60%, 50% and 30%. The colleges have different numbers of females, so you must use the actual counts.

questions.question_md: How many female students are post graduate in total students of all the colleges?
questions.explanation:
Find the female students in each college. Then take the post-graduate (PG) percentage.

- A: females = 3/10 × 400 = 120. PG = 40% of 120 = 48.
- B: females = 1/5 × 500 = 100. PG = 60% of 100 = 60.
- C: females = 3/7 × 700 = 300. PG = 50% of 300 = 150.
- D: females = 1/3 × 600 = 200. PG = 30% of 200 = 60.

Total PG females = 48 + 60 + 150 + 60 = **318**.

The value 720 is the total number of female students. The value 2200 is the total of all students.

questions.question_md: The number of female students in college C is how much percent less than the number of male students in this college?
questions.explanation:
In College C, Male : Female = 4 : 3 and the total is 700.

- Males = 4/7 × 700 = 400.
- Females = 3/7 × 700 = 300.

The difference is 400 − 300 = 100.

"Less than the males" means that you divide by the number of males.
Percentage less = 100 ÷ 400 × 100 = **25%**.

If you divide by the females (100 ÷ 300), you get 33.3%. That value is not an option. The value 75% is the females as a percentage of the males.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I (Radionuclide) | LIST-II (Target Tissue) |
|---|---|
| A. Iodine - 131 | I. Spleen |
| B. Strontium - 90 | II. Bones |
| C. Plutonium - 239 | III. Soft tissue |
| D. Caesium - 137 | IV. Liver |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Each radionuclide (radioactive form of an element) collects in a particular tissue of the body.

- **Strontium-90 → bones.** Strontium acts like calcium, so the body puts it into bones.
- **Plutonium-239 → liver.** Plutonium collects mainly in the liver and the bones.
- **Caesium-137 → soft tissue.** Caesium acts like potassium and spreads through muscle and other soft tissue.
- **Iodine-131 → spleen** is the pair that remains.

Iodine-131 really collects in the thyroid gland. The thyroid is not in List-II, so the key pairs iodine with the remaining item.

Only option (1) pairs strontium with bones. So the other options are wrong.

questions.question_md:
The effective implementation of the world ethics will only be possible if it is taken up by all sections of the community. It should include,

A. Parents teaching their children to act with respect for other people and other species.

B. Educators incorporating the world ethics into their teaching.

C. Artists have significant role in it.

D. Technologists must not take part in it.

E. As no legal issues are involved in world ethics, lawyers have no role in it.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
World ethics needs the support of every part of society. Each group has a role.

- **A is correct.** Parents teach children respect for other people and other species.
- **B is correct.** Educators can put the world ethics into their teaching.
- **C is correct.** Artists shape the values and feelings of people.
- **D is wrong.** Technologists make tools that change the world. They must take part.
- **E is wrong.** Lawyers help to turn ethical rules into law. They also have a role.

So only A, B and C are correct. Every other option includes D or E, which exclude a group.

questions.question_md:
Some of the most useful code of ethics in social research have been formulated by -

A. British Sociological Association

B. German Sociological Society

C. Social Research Association

D. Austrian Psychological Association

E. The political & psychological research council

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
The unofficial key says B & E. This looks wrong.

The question uses the words of Alan Bryman's textbook *Social Research Methods*. Bryman says that two of the most useful codes of ethics come from:

- **A. the British Sociological Association (BSA)**, and
- **C. the Social Research Association (SRA)**.

Both are British bodies. Their ethics guidelines are standard references for social researchers.

- B: the German Sociological Society has a code, but the textbook does not name it here.
- D: the "Austrian Psychological Association" is not a standard source of social research ethics.
- E: "The political & psychological research council" is not a known body.

So the best answer is **A & C only**. The red-pen mark may be a mistake.

questions.question_md:
Which among these are the input devices?

A. Touch pad

B. Touch screen

C. Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR)

D. Optical Mark Reading and Recognition (OMR)

E. Monitor

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
An input device sends data into the computer. An output device shows data from the computer.

- **A. Touch pad** is an input device. You move the pointer with your finger.
- **B. Touch screen** is an input device. It also shows output, but you give input by touch.
- **C. MICR** (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) is an input device. Banks use it to read the numbers on cheques.
- **D. OMR** (Optical Mark Recognition) is an input device. It reads marks on answer sheets.
- **E. Monitor** is an output device. It only shows information.

So A, B, C and D are input devices. The options that include E are wrong.

questions.question_md: The teacher is the only source of knowledge. This dictum justifies the teaching method:
questions.explanation:
In the lecture method, the teacher speaks and the students listen. The teacher gives all the content. So the teacher acts as the main source of knowledge. This matches the dictum "The teacher is the only source of knowledge".

The other methods put the learner at the centre.

- In the **project method**, learners find knowledge through their own work.
- In a **learner-centric method**, learners take an active part in learning.
- An **outcome-based method** focuses on what learners can do at the end.

These methods use many sources of knowledge, not only the teacher.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following methods of data collection in terms of the personal involvement of researcher from high to low.

A. Structured interview

B. Unstructured interview

C. Questionnaire

D. Participant observation

E. Observation

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Personal involvement means how much the researcher takes part in the setting and in the data collection.

- **D. Participant observation:** the researcher joins the group and lives its life. This is the highest involvement.
- **E. Observation:** the researcher watches people directly but does not join them.
- **B. Unstructured interview:** a free face-to-face talk. The researcher guides it all the time.
- **A. Structured interview:** face to face, but with fixed questions in a fixed order.
- **C. Questionnaire:** the respondents fill it in alone. This is the lowest involvement.

So the order is D, E, B, A, C. The options that start with A, C or E do not put participant observation first.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following stages of transmission models of news learning mentioned in Denis Mcquil's book from start to end:

A. Comprehension

B. News item display

C. Learning

D. Actual Exposure

E. Recall

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Denis McQuail describes the transmission model of news learning as a chain of steps. Each step must happen before the next one.

1. **B. News item display:** the media show the news item.
2. **D. Actual exposure:** a person actually sees or hears it.
3. **A. Comprehension:** the person understands it.
4. **E. Recall:** the person remembers it later.
5. **C. Learning:** the news becomes part of what the person knows.

So the order is B, D, A, E, C. Option (2) puts recall before comprehension. A person cannot remember a news item correctly before they understand it.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I (Assessment) | LIST-II (Function) |
|---|---|
| A. Norm-Referenced | I. Position of the learner in the class |
| B. Criterion Referenced | II. Cut off marks |
| C. Self Referenced | III. Current behavior compared to earlier behavior |
| D. Competency Based | IV. Measures effective performance of task |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Each type of assessment uses a different point of comparison.

- **A. Norm-referenced → I.** It compares a learner with other learners. It shows the position of the learner in the class.
- **B. Criterion-referenced → II.** It compares a learner with a fixed standard, such as cut-off marks.
- **C. Self-referenced → III.** It compares the learner's present performance with their own earlier performance.
- **D. Competency-based → IV.** It checks if the learner can do a task well.

So the match is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV. The other options mix up norm (other learners) and criterion (a fixed standard).

questions.question_md:
Forms of interpersonal conflicts combine

A. Pervasive communication

B. Innovation Diffusion

C. Hostile episode

D. Agenda-setting model

E. Disagreeable communication

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Interpersonal conflict is a conflict between two or more people. It can take these forms:

- **A. Pervasive communication** is a form of conflict. Here the conflict runs through most of the talk between two people.
- **C. Hostile episode** is a form of conflict. It is a short event full of anger.
- **E. Disagreeable communication** is a form of conflict. The people talk in an unfriendly way.

The other two items are not forms of conflict:

- **B. Innovation diffusion** is a theory about how new ideas spread in a society.
- **D. Agenda-setting** is a mass media theory. It says that the media decide which issues people think about.

So the answer is A, C and E only.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I | LIST-II |
|---|---|
| A. Sin²30° + Cos²30° + Sin 90° | I. 4 |
| B. Sin²45° + Cos²45° + Cos 90° | II. 2 |
| C. 2 Sin²60° + 2Cos²30° + Cos 0° | III. 1 |
| D. 4 Cos 60° + 2Cos²30° + 5 Sin²45° | IV. 6 |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Use these standard values.

- sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2
- cos 30° = sin 60° = √3/2
- sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2
- sin 90° = cos 0° = 1, and cos 90° = 0

Now work out each expression.

- **A:** 1/4 + 3/4 + 1 = 2 → **II**.
- **B:** 1/2 + 1/2 + 0 = 1 → **III**.
- **C:** 2(3/4) + 2(3/4) + 1 = 1.5 + 1.5 + 1 = 4 → **I**.
- **D:** 4(1/2) + 2(3/4) + 5(1/2) = 2 + 1.5 + 2.5 = 6 → **IV**.

So the match is A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

A quick check: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for the same angle. This gives A and B fast.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I (Scheme) | LIST-II (Agenda) |
|---|---|
| A. PRAGATI | I. For faculty development and research upgradation |
| B. SAKSHAM | II. Fellowship for specially-abled students |
| C. QIP | III. Improvement of laboratories and infrastructure |
| D. MODROB | IV. Fellowship for girl students in technical Education |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
These are AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education) schemes.

- **A. PRAGATI → IV.** It gives scholarships to girl students in technical education.
- **B. SAKSHAM → II.** It gives scholarships to specially-abled students.
- **C. QIP → I.** QIP means Quality Improvement Programme. It helps faculty to upgrade their qualifications and research.
- **D. MODROB → III.** MODROB means Modernisation and Removal of Obsolescence. It funds the improvement of laboratories.

So the match is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III. In the other options, PRAGATI and SAKSHAM have the wrong pairs.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I (Forms of message style) | LIST-II (Dialogue, examples) |
|---|---|
| A. Threat | I. I think you are great, would you clean the apartment |
| B. Altruism | II. I will make your favourite dinner if you clean the apartment |
| C. Promise | III. If you will not clean the apartment I am going to be mad |
| D. Linking | IV. For my sake clean the apartment, will you? |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
These are compliance-gaining message styles. A person uses them to make another person do something.

- **A. Threat → III.** "If you will not clean the apartment I am going to be mad." The speaker warns of a bad result.
- **B. Altruism → IV.** "For my sake clean the apartment." The speaker asks for help as a favour.
- **C. Promise → II.** "I will make your favourite dinner if you clean." The speaker offers a reward.
- **D. Liking → I.** "I think you are great, would you clean the apartment." The speaker is friendly first. The list writes it as "Linking".

So the match is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I. The other options mix up promise and altruism.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following in the decreasing order

A. LCM of 15, 20, 75

B. LCM of 25/3, 40/9, 50/6

C. HCF of 600, 150, 675

D. LCM of 4, 6, 9

E. HCF of 0.5, 1.5, 3.5

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.notes: Red-pen mark is a single tick drawn beside option 1 (the chosen option) in the options list.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following steps according to deductive reasoning

A. Data collection

B. Hypothesis

C. General principle (Theory)

D. Specific Result

E. Analysis

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Deductive reasoning goes from the general to the specific. The research starts with a theory and ends with a specific result.

1. **C. General principle (theory)**
2. **B. Hypothesis:** a testable statement that comes from the theory.
3. **A. Data collection:** you gather facts to test the hypothesis.
4. **E. Analysis:** you study the data.
5. **D. Specific result:** the finding.

So the order is C, B, A, E, D.

Option (4) starts with the specific result and ends with the theory. That is the order of inductive reasoning.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following statements correctly explain the fallacy of hasty generalization?

A. It draws a general conclusion from insufficient evidence

B. It is also known as converse accident

C. It relies on large and representative samples

D. It often results in stereotypes

E. Anecdotal evidence is sufficient to justify generalization

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Hasty generalization is a fallacy (an error in reasoning). A person draws a general rule from too few cases.

- **A is correct.** The evidence is not enough for the general conclusion.
- **B is correct.** Logic texts such as Copi also call it "converse accident".
- **C is wrong.** A large, representative sample gives a good generalization. The fallacy uses small or untypical samples.
- **D is correct.** Hasty generalizations often produce stereotypes about groups of people.
- **E is wrong.** Anecdotal evidence (a few personal stories) is not enough. Using it is the fallacy itself.

So the answer is A, B and D only.

questions.question_md:
Which devices are NOT used in a network?

A. DJ45

B. Gateway

C. Modem

D. RJ45

E. Media Access Control (MAC)

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Check each item.

- **A. DJ45** is not a real network device. The real connector is RJ45. "DJ45" is a distractor.
- **B. Gateway** is a network device. It connects two networks that use different protocols.
- **C. Modem** is a network device. It changes digital signals to analog signals and back.
- **D. RJ45** is the standard connector on Ethernet cables. Wired networks use it.
- **E. MAC** (Media Access Control) is not a device. It is a hardware address and a sublayer of the data link layer.

So A and E are not network devices. The options with B, C or D are wrong.

questions.question_md: The sum of two numbers is 20 and the product of their LCM and HCF is 96. Then the sum of squares of these numbers is equal to:
questions.explanation:
For two numbers, LCM × HCF = the product of the numbers.

So the product of the numbers is ab = 96. The sum is a + b = 20.

Use the identity: a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab.

a² + b² = 20² − 2 × 96 = 400 − 192 = **208**.

Check: the numbers are 8 and 12. 8 + 12 = 20 and 8 × 12 = 96. Then 64 + 144 = 208.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I | LIST-II |
|---|---|
| A. Carvak | I. First step in Pabbaja |
| B. Sharantrayi | II. A Upnishad |
| C. Kalesha | III. Nastik school of Indian philosophy |
| D. Mandukya | IV. Asmita-one of five affliction |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Check each pair.

- **A. Cārvāka → III.** Cārvāka is a Nāstika school. It does not accept the authority of the Vedas.
- **B. Śaraṇatraya → I.** Śaraṇatraya (the three refuges) means taking refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Saṅgha. A person recites it at the start of Pabbajjā (the first ordination as a Buddhist monk).
- **C. Kleśa → IV.** Yoga lists five kleśas (afflictions). Asmitā (the sense of "I am") is one of them.
- **D. Māṇḍūkya → II.** The Māṇḍūkya is one of the main Upaniṣads.

So the match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II. Options (1) and (3) do not put Māṇḍūkya with "Upaniṣad".

questions.question_md: Foreign universities can now open campus in India. This is because India is a signatory of :
options: General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS)
questions.explanation:
GATS is the General Agreement on Trade in Services. It is a WTO (World Trade Organization) agreement. India signed it in 1995.

GATS treats education as a service that countries can trade. One way to supply this service is "commercial presence". This means that a foreign provider sets up a campus in another country. So GATS gives the basis for foreign universities to open campuses in India.

- The Dunkel Draft (1991) was a draft text of the Uruguay Round. It is not an agreement on its own.
- The SDGs are UN development goals, not a trade agreement.
- The Incheon Declaration (2015) is about the education goals for 2030. It does not deal with trade.

questions.question_md:
Producing of the following items requires huge amount of fresh water. Arrange them from highest to lowest in order of water-consumption.

A. Bread

B. Car

C. Jeans

D. House

E. T-shirt

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
The water footprint is the total fresh water used to make a product. Typical estimates are:

- **D. House:** the largest. It needs cement, bricks, steel and much more.
- **B. Car:** about 50,000 litres or more, for steel, plastics and paint.
- **C. Jeans:** about 8,000–10,000 litres, mostly for growing cotton.
- **E. T-shirt:** about 2,500–2,700 litres.
- **A. Bread:** about 1,600 litres for a loaf, or much less for a slice.

So the order is D, B, C, E, A.

A pair of jeans uses more cotton than a T-shirt, so jeans come first. Options (1) and (3) put the T-shirt above the jeans.

questions.question_md:
The average test score of a class of m students is 60 and that of n students is 81. When the scores of both classes are combined, then the average is 70. In this context, which of the following statements are correct?

A. (m + n)/(m − n) = 21

B. m/(m − n) = 11

C. n/(n + m) = 10

D. m/(m + n) = 11

E. n/(m − n) = 10

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Use the weighted average.

60m + 81n = 70(m + n)
60m + 81n = 70m + 70n
11n = 10m

So m : n = 11 : 10. Take m = 11 and n = 10. Then m + n = 21 and m − n = 1.

- **A.** (m + n)/(m − n) = 21/1 = 21. Correct.
- **B.** m/(m − n) = 11/1 = 11. Correct.
- **C.** n/(n + m) = 10/21. Wrong.
- **D.** m/(m + n) = 11/21. Wrong.
- **E.** n/(m − n) = 10/1 = 10. Correct.

So A, B and E are correct.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I (Theorist) | LIST-II (Concept/Perspective) |
|---|---|
| A. August Comte | I. Falsification |
| B. Karl Popper | II. Interpretivism |
| C. Max Weber | III. Feminism |
| D. Claire Wallace | IV. Positivism |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Check each theorist.

- **A. Auguste Comte → IV.** He founded positivism. Positivism studies society with the methods of natural science.
- **B. Karl Popper → I.** He said that a scientific theory must be falsifiable. A test must be able to show that it is false.
- **C. Max Weber → II.** He started interpretivism. He used *Verstehen* (understanding the meaning of an action for the actor).
- **D. Claire Wallace → III.** She is a British sociologist. She wrote on feminist perspectives in sociology.

So the match is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III. Option (3) puts Comte with Positivism, but it gives Popper the wrong concept.

questions.question_md:
Green Accounting is a widely prevalent concept both in developed and underdeveloped countries. Which of the following are true related to it?

A. It can be described as number of individuals of a species that it can sustain.

B. It underlines the same concept of sustainable development.

C. It provides us an economic interpretation of both resource base and the environment quality as against the GDP.

D. It gives us a uniform level by converting both natural resource base and the environment quality in monetary terms.

E. The concepts of green accounting and carrying capacity are different.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Green accounting adds the use of natural resources and the damage to the environment to the national accounts. Normal GDP leaves out these costs.

- **A is wrong.** This is the definition of carrying capacity. Carrying capacity is the number of individuals that an environment can support.
- **B is true.** Green accounting supports sustainable development.
- **C is true.** It gives an economic picture of the resource base and the quality of the environment, unlike GDP.
- **D is true.** It changes resources and environmental quality into money values. So you can compare them on one scale.

Statement E is also a true fact, because the two concepts are different. But E only compares green accounting with another idea. B, C and D describe green accounting itself. So the examiner chose B, C and D. No option contains all four true statements.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following events in proper sequence with respect to land degradation cycle arising from opencast mining, mineral dressing and other related activities.

A. Loss of greenery

B. Drying up of land

C. Land degradation

D. Decrease in irrigation potential

E. Desertification

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Opencast mining removes the top layers of land. This starts a chain of damage.

1. **A. Loss of greenery:** mining clears trees and plants.
2. **D. Decrease in irrigation potential:** mining disturbs the water table and the streams. So less water is available for irrigation.
3. **B. Drying up of land:** without plants and water, the soil loses its moisture.
4. **C. Land degradation:** the dry, bare soil loses its fertility and erodes.
5. **E. Desertification:** the degraded land finally becomes desert-like.

So the unofficial key gives A, D, B, C, E. Option (4) is close. But it puts the drying of land before the loss of water. The loss of water causes the drying, so it comes first.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

If a = (√5 − 2)/(√5 + 2), then match the following

| LIST-I | LIST-II |
|---|---|
| A. a + 1/a | I. 8√5 |
| B. 1/a − a | II. 161 |
| C. ½(a² + 1/a²) | III. 18 |
| D. 1/a² − a² | IV. 144√5 |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:

Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I | LIST-II |
|---|---|
| A. A - proposition | I. (Venn diagram I) |
| B. E - proposition | II. (Venn diagram II) |
| C. I - proposition | III. (Venn diagram III) |
| D. O - proposition | IV. (Venn diagram IV) |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.notes: List-II items are Venn diagrams of S and P (see image): I. part of S outside P shaded; II. overlap of S and P shaded; III. x in the overlap of S and P; IV. x in S outside P.
questions.explanation:
In a Venn diagram, shading means "this area is empty". An x means "something exists here".

- **A-proposition** "All S is P": no S is outside P. So you shade the part of S outside P → **I**.
- **E-proposition** "No S is P": nothing is in both S and P. So you shade the overlap → **II**.
- **I-proposition** "Some S is P": something is in both. So you put an x in the overlap → **III**.
- **O-proposition** "Some S is not P": something is in S but not in P. So you put an x in S outside P → **IV**.

So the match is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV. Universal propositions (A, E) use shading. Particular propositions (I, O) use an x.

questions.question_md: A study in which the researcher directly intervenes in and / or manipulates a natural setting in order to observe what happens as a consequence of that intervention is called as:
questions.explanation:
This is the definition of a field simulation. Some textbooks, such as Bryman's *Social Research Methods*, spell the term "field stimulation".

In this method, the researcher changes something in a real, everyday setting. Then the researcher watches how people react to the change. The people usually do not know that they are in a study. For example, a researcher may drop a wallet in a street and record who returns it.

- "Field negotiation" is not a research design. It refers to getting access to a setting.
- "Field disturbance" and "field investigation" are not the standard names for this method.

questions.question_md:
Select the Venn diagram that best illustrates the relationship among the following classes:

(A) Dogs (B) Pets (C) Cats
questions.notes: Options are Venn diagrams (see image): 1. three mutually overlapping circles A, B, C; 2. A and B as separate circles inside C; 3. A, B, C in a chain (A overlaps B, B overlaps C); 4. A and B overlapping, both inside C.
questions.explanation:
Check the relation between each pair of classes.

- **Dogs and pets:** some dogs are pets, and some are not (for example, street dogs). Some pets are not dogs. So the circles overlap.
- **Cats and pets:** they overlap in the same way.
- **Dogs and cats:** no animal is both a dog and a cat. So these circles are separate.

So the right diagram shows Pets in the middle. Dogs overlap Pets, Cats overlap Pets, and Dogs do not touch Cats. This is the chain in Diagram 3.

- Diagram 1 is wrong. It shows that some dogs are cats.
- Diagram 2 and Diagram 4 are wrong. They put all dogs inside another class.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the opening lines of stanzas in Vande Matram

A. Sujalam, Suflam malyaj sheetalam

B. Saptakoti kanth kalkal ninad karale

C. Shubra jyotsna pulkit yaminim

D. Tvan hi durga dashapraharan dharini

E. Tumi vidya tumi dharma, tumi hridi tumi marma

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
*Vande Mataram* is a song by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in his novel *Anandamath*. The stanzas open in this order:

1. **A.** "Sujalam suphalam malayaja shitalam" (the first stanza).
2. **C.** "Shubhra jyotsna pulakita yaminim" (the moonlit nights).
3. **B.** "Saptakoti kantha kalakala ninada karale" (the voices of seven crore people).
4. **E.** "Tumi vidya tumi dharma, tumi hridi tumi marma".
5. **D.** "Tvam hi Durga dashapraharana dharini".

So the order is A, C, B, E, D.

The first two stanzas form the national song. Option (1) and option (2) put "Tvam hi Durga" before "Tumi vidya", which is wrong.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the following stages of personality development sequentially as proposed by Freud

A. Phallic

B. Oral

C. Anal

D. Genital

E. Latency

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Sigmund Freud gave five psychosexual stages of personality development. Each stage has a different focus of pleasure.

1. **B. Oral** (birth to about 1 year): the mouth.
2. **C. Anal** (about 1 to 3 years): toilet training.
3. **A. Phallic** (about 3 to 6 years): the genitals. The Oedipus complex appears here.
4. **E. Latency** (about 6 years to puberty): sexual feelings are quiet.
5. **D. Genital** (puberty onwards): adult sexuality.

So the order is B, C, A, E, D. Option (1) puts phallic before anal, which is wrong.

questions.question_md: In one of the 'Conference of Parties' (COP), an agreement on plans for finance to mitigate the effects of climate change and help developing nations transition to more sustainable energy sources had been signed. Which country hosted that COP?
questions.explanation:
COP29 took place in Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024. People often call it the "finance COP".

At COP29, countries agreed a new climate finance goal. Developed countries will provide at least 300 billion US dollars each year by 2035. This money helps developing countries to cut emissions, to adapt to climate change and to move to cleaner energy.

- COP26 (Glasgow, UK) gave the Glasgow Climate Pact.
- COP28 (Dubai, UAE) started the loss and damage fund. It also called for a transition away from fossil fuels.
- COP30 took place in Belém, Brazil, in 2025.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the steps in hypothetico-deductive model

A. Data analysis

B. Observation

C. Framing hypothesis

D. Data collection

E. Reject/accept hypothesis

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
The hypothetico-deductive model is the classic scientific method. It starts with what you observe and ends with a decision on a hypothesis.

1. **B. Observation:** you notice a fact or a problem.
2. **C. Framing hypothesis:** you suggest a possible explanation.
3. **D. Data collection:** you collect facts to test it.
4. **A. Data analysis:** you study the data.
5. **E. Reject or accept the hypothesis.**

So the order is B, C, D, A, E.

Option (1) puts the hypothesis before observation. Option (3) puts data collection before the hypothesis. In this model, the hypothesis guides the data collection.

questions.question_md:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**

| LIST-I | LIST-II |
|---|---|
| A. 1GB (Gigabytes) | I. 10¹² bytes |
| B. 1KB (Kilobytes) | II. 10⁶ bytes |
| C. 1TB (Terabytes) | III. 10³ bytes |
| D. 1MB (Megabytes) | IV. 10⁹ bytes |

Choose the ***correct*** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
The decimal (SI) units use powers of 1000.

- **B. 1 KB = 10³ bytes** → III.
- **D. 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes** → II.
- **A. 1 GB = 10⁹ bytes** → IV.
- **C. 1 TB = 10¹² bytes** → I.

So the match is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

In binary units, 1 KB = 2¹⁰ = 1024 bytes. But the list uses powers of 10, so use the decimal values. The other options mix up the order of the units.

questions.question_md:
Select CORRECT statements pertaining to phases of teaching

A. Sequential arrangement of content is done during Pre-active phase

B. A quick review of interest, aptitude and ability of learners is a post-active phase

C. Formulation of objectives is a step in pre-active phase

D. Assessment is done in post-active phase

E. Evaluation is done to measure learning progress during Inter-active phase

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and E only
questions.explanation:
Philip Jackson divided teaching into three phases.

- The **pre-active phase** is planning before the class.
- The **inter-active phase** is the teaching in the class.
- The **post-active phase** is the work after the class.

Check each statement:

- **A is correct.** The teacher selects and arranges the content during planning.
- **B is wrong.** The teacher checks the interest and ability of learners during the class or before it, not after it.
- **C is correct.** The teacher writes the objectives during planning.
- **D** is about the post-active phase, but no option contains A, C and D.
- **E is wrong.** In this scheme, evaluation of learning comes in the post-active phase.

Options (2), (3) and (4) contain B, which is wrong. So the best answer is A and C only.

questions.question_md: For the maxim of teaching, from known to unknown, the first thing to be focused by the teacher is -
questions.explanation:
The maxim "from known to unknown" means that new learning must start from what the learner already knows. The teacher connects the new topic to this old knowledge.

So the teacher must first find out the **previous knowledge of the learner**. Only then can the teacher build the new idea on it.

- **Recapitulation** is a summary at the end of a lesson.
- **Presentation** is the step where the teacher gives the new content. It comes after the teacher links it to the known.
- **Content selection** is part of planning. But the known point for the maxim is the learner's knowledge, not the content.

questions.question_md: This term is derived from the French, meaning type or classification. It is used in literature and mostly in cinema to classify as a tragedy, epic, comedy, satire, action etc. What is this term?
questions.notes: Answer left pending: the red-pen cross marks the chosen option (2) wrong, but the correcting tick beside the options list also sits at option 2, so the intended answer is unclear.
questions.explanation:
This question has no key. The red-pen marks are unclear. The suggested answer is **Genre**.

"Genre" is a French word. It means "kind" or "type". In literature and cinema, it is a category of works with a similar form or style. Examples are tragedy, epic, comedy, satire and action.

- **À la carte** is also French, but it means "from the menu". You order dishes one by one.
- **Typecast** means that an actor always gets the same type of role.
- **Guild** is an association of craftspeople or traders.

So only "genre" fits the meaning of type or classification.

questions.question_md: Gyan Vani FM channel is run by:
questions.explanation:
Gyan Vani is a network of educational FM radio stations. IGNOU (Indira Gandhi National Open University) runs it. Gyan Vani broadcasts educational programmes for distance learners and the public.

IGNOU also runs Gyan Darshan, an educational TV channel.

- AICTE controls technical education.
- UGC funds and regulates universities.
- NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling) runs open schooling.

None of these three runs Gyan Vani.

questions.question_md:
Which of the following pertain to the Denotation?

A. Extension

B. Intension

C. Area

D. Limit

E. Aim

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
In logic, a term has two aspects.

- **Denotation** is the set of objects to which the term applies. It is also called **extension**.
- **Connotation** is the set of qualities that the term implies. It is also called **intension**.

So check the items:

- **A. Extension:** another name for denotation.
- **C. Area:** denotation is the range or area that the term covers.
- **D. Limit:** denotation marks the boundary of the class.
- **B. Intension** belongs to connotation, not denotation.
- **E. Aim** has no relation to denotation.

So A, C and D pertain to denotation. Options (2) and (4) include intension, which is wrong.

questions.question_md:
Arrange the steps followed to delete an E-mail permanently:

A. Click on Inbox of your email

B. Click delete, the e-mail will be sent to Trash folder

C. Confirm the clear/delete trash option, folder will get empty

D. Select checkbox corresponding to e-mails you want to delete

E. Click on Empty trash option

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
To delete an e-mail permanently, you must first move it to Trash. Then you empty the Trash.

1. **A.** Open the Inbox.
2. **D.** Select the checkbox for each e-mail that you want to delete.
3. **B.** Click Delete. The e-mail goes to the Trash folder.
4. **E.** Click the Empty Trash option.
5. **C.** Confirm the action. The Trash folder becomes empty.

So the order is A, D, B, E, C.

Option (1) puts the confirmation before the Empty Trash click. That is not possible. Options (3) and (4) click Delete before you select the e-mails.

questions.question_md: Which of the following defines selective exposure?
options: The idea that you are more likely to recall things that support your beliefs, values and attitude
The idea that you are more likely to expose yourself to that which supports your beliefs, values and attitude
The idea that you are more likely to perceive and focus on things that support your beliefs, values and attitudes
questions.notes: Answer left pending: the red-pen cross marks the chosen option (3) wrong, but the correcting tick beside the options list sits at option 3 (its upper end near option 2), so the intended answer is unclear.
questions.explanation:
This question has no key. The red-pen marks are unclear. The suggested answer is the second option.

Selective exposure is the tendency to expose yourself to messages that support your beliefs, values and attitudes. People avoid messages that disagree with them. For example, a person may watch only the news channel that shares their political view.

The other options describe related ideas:

- The first option describes **selective retention**. People remember the messages that agree with their beliefs.
- The third option describes **selective perception**. People notice and interpret messages in a way that fits their beliefs.
- "News selection" is the choice of news by editors. It is gatekeeping, not a process in the audience.

questions.question_md: Organizations should provide developmental opportunities for women so as to -
options: Assist them to move up the hierarchical ladder
questions.explanation:
The passage says that organizations "should continue to provide developmental opportunities that will prepare women for advancement into the senior ranks".

"Advancement into the senior ranks" means moving up to higher positions. So the aim is to help women move up the hierarchical ladder.

- **Recruitment** happens before a person joins. The passage talks about women who are already in the workforce.
- **Childcare** is not in the passage.
- **Visibility** is not the stated aim. The passage talks about promotion to senior posts.

questions.question_md: What does the last line of the passage imply?
options: Diversity has a harmful effect on organizational performance.
There is ambiguity regarding its role for improved organisational performance.
Diversity does not bring change in organizational performance.
Diversity has a negative impact on employees.
questions.explanation:
The last line says: "Diversity can be a catalyst for improved organizational performance - though this is far from a sure thing!"

A catalyst is something that helps a change to happen. So diversity *can* improve performance. But "far from a sure thing" means that this result is not certain. So the role of diversity in performance is uncertain or ambiguous.

- Options (1) and (4) say that diversity is harmful. The passage does not say this.
- Option (3) says that diversity brings no change. This also goes against the word "catalyst".

questions.question_md: The prediction of diversity in the opening line of the paragraph is that the trend will:
questions.explanation:
The opening line says: "this trend toward diversity will continue".

"Continue" means that the trend will go on. The word "persist" has the same meaning.

- "Stop" is the opposite.
- "Transform" means to change into something different. The passage does not say this.
- "Diverge" means to move apart in different directions. The passage does not say this either.

questions.question_md: The specific requirement of an ageing workforce would be related to:
questions.explanation:
The passage says that the ageing of the workforce is important for HRD programs. These programs must "address the learning-related needs of both younger and older workers."

So an ageing workforce needs attention to **learning-related needs**. HRD means Human Resource Development.

The other options come from different parts of the passage:

- **Removal of prejudices** and **racial parity** relate to racial and ethnic diversity.
- **Cultural sensitivity** relates to cultural and language differences.

The passage does not link any of these to age.

questions.question_md: Making it to the Fortune magazine's list of 100 best companies is one of the rewards related to:
questions.explanation:
The passage names five features of the companies on Fortune magazine's list of 100 Best Companies. "Effectively managing diversity" is one of these features.

So a place on this list comes with **effectively managing diversity**.

- The passage does not mention Corporate Social Responsibility.
- Learning-related needs come up only for the ageing workforce.
- Respectful treatment of employees may be a good practice, but the passage does not link it to the Fortune list.

groups.md:
Read the following passage and answer the questions from **46** to **50** :

The thesis of James’ Radical Empiricism is that “There is only one primal stuff or material in the world, a stuff of which everything is composed, and … we call that stuff ‘pure experience.’” James’ Empiricism differs from traditional British Empiricism in his insistence that we remain within concrete experience, his insistence that “conjunctive and disjunctive relations are, when experienced, equally real.” The world of facts as we experience them comprises a mosaic or set of mosaics and some of these directly experienced mosaics of plural facts appear to be connected, while others are experienced as disjunctives. The unity of the universe as a neat set of interconnected relations in an Absolute is false, said James, because direct experience informs us of a discontinuity of facts in a mosaic design. Thus Radical Empiricism claims that data in our experience show the universe to be pluralistic, comprised of facts which form neither a perfect unity nor any absolutely perfect relationship to one another. James termed this Metaphysical Pluralism a “mosaic philosophy.”

questions.question_md: In vedic tradition the movement of earth was regulated by
questions.explanation:
**Ṛta** is the cosmic order in the Vedas. It is the law that keeps nature in its regular course. The sun rises, the seasons change and the earth moves because of Ṛta. Varuṇa is called the guardian of Ṛta.

- **Brahman** is the ultimate reality of the Upaniṣads. It is not the Vedic word for natural order.
- **Īśvara** (a personal God) is a later idea.
- **Sūrya** is the sun god. He also follows Ṛta. He does not create it.

questions.question_md: Which type of ṛṇa in Vedic tradition can be repaid by performing Yajña ?
questions.explanation:
The Vedic tradition speaks of three debts (ṛṇa) that every person has at birth.

- **Devaṛṇa** is the debt to the gods. A person repays it by performing Yajña (sacrifice).
- **Ṛṣiṛṇa** is the debt to the sages. A person repays it by study of the Vedas (svādhyāya).
- **Pitṛṛṇa** is the debt to the ancestors. A person repays it by having children and by offerings to the ancestors.

**Pṛthviṛṇa** (a debt to the earth) is not one of the three classical debts.

questions.question_md: The term ‘Paryāya’ in Jaina thought refers to
questions.explanation:
Jaina thought divides every real thing (dravya) into two parts:

- **Guṇa** (quality): the essential quality. It stays with the substance.
- **Paryāya** (mode): the changing state of the substance. It comes and goes.

So Paryāya is the changing or accidental property, that is, **Āgantuka Dharma**. For example, gold stays gold, but its form changes from a ring to a chain.

- **Nitya Dharma** (permanent property) fits Guṇa, not Paryāya.
- **Manaḥ Paryāya** is a kind of knowledge (telepathy). The word only looks similar.
- **Naya** is a partial point of view in Jaina logic.

questions.question_md:
Given below are an Assertion (A) and a Reason (R). Consider them and select the correct code given below in the context of Cārvāka Philosophy.

**Assertion (A) :** The dead body must be conscious.

**Reason (R) :** Consciousness is an attribute of body.

**Codes :**
options: (A) and (R) both are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) and (R) both are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Cārvāka is the materialist school of Indian philosophy. It accepts only perception as a valid source of knowledge.

- **(R) is true** for Cārvāka. Consciousness is a quality of the living body. It appears when the four elements combine in a special way. In the same way, fermented grain gets the power to make a person drunk.
- **(A) is false.** A dead body still has the elements, but the special combination has stopped. So Cārvāka does not say that a dead body is conscious.

Critics of Cārvāka use the dead body as an objection. Cārvāka answers with the idea of the special combination.

questions.question_md: Who among the following holds that blue colour and the knowledge of the blue colour are one and the same ?
questions.explanation:
This is the view of the **Yogācāra** (Vijñānavāda) school of Buddhism. Yogācāra says that only consciousness is real. An object is not separate from the knowledge of it. Blue and the knowledge of blue always appear together, so they are one. Later Yogācāra logicians call this rule *sahopalambha niyama* (the rule of joint perception).

**Vasubandhu** is a founder of Yogācāra. So he holds this view.

- **Bṛhaspati** is the traditional founder of Cārvāka (materialism).
- **Bhāsarvajña** is a Nyāya thinker. Nyāya is realist and separates the object from the knowledge.
- **Prabhākara** is a Mīmāṁsā realist. He also accepts external objects.

questions.explanation:
Match each group of five with its school:

- **a. Pañcaśīla** (five moral rules: no killing, no stealing and so on) belongs to **Bauddha** → ii.
- **b. Pañcāvayava** (the five-member inference: pratijñā, hetu, udāharaṇa, upanaya, nigamana) belongs to **Nyāya** → i.
- **c. Pañca parameṣṭhī** (five supreme beings: arhat, siddha, ācārya, upādhyāya, sādhu) belongs to **Jaina** → iii.
- **d. Pañca kleśa** (five afflictions: avidyā, asmitā, rāga, dveṣa, abhiniveśa) belongs to **Yoga** → iv.

The code is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv. Option (1) and option (4) wrongly link Pañcaśīla to Nyāya or Jaina.

questions.question_md: According to the Naiyāyikas Samavāya is perceived by the Sannikarṣa known as
questions.explanation:
Sannikarṣa is the contact between a sense organ and its object. Nyāya lists six kinds of contact.

Samavāya (inherence) is the relation between a quality and its substance. Nyāya says that we perceive it through **Viśeṣaṇatā** (the relation of qualifier and qualified). For example, we see "the cloth with colour inhering in it". Here inherence acts as a qualifier of the cloth. Abhāva (absence) also is perceived through Viśeṣaṇatā.

- **Saṁyukta samavāya** is used to perceive a quality, for example the colour of a pot.
- **Samaveta samavāya** is used to perceive a universal in a quality, for example colour-ness.
- "Samavāya" alone is the contact used to perceive sound by the ear. It is not used to perceive inherence itself.

Vaiśeṣika does not accept the perception of samavāya; it infers it.

questions.question_md: In Nyāya Philosophy of language Īśvarecchā is :
questions.notes: Option (1) is printed as ‘sákti’ in the source (font artefact for śakti).
questions.explanation:
Śakti is the power of a word to mean its object. Old Nyāya explains Śakti as **the will of God (Īśvarecchā)**. God wills: "From this word, this object should be understood." This will itself is the Śakti, that is, the primary meaning relation.

- Śakti is not caused by Īśvarecchā. Īśvarecchā **is** Śakti. So "the cause of śakti" is wrong.
- **Lakṣaṇā** (secondary meaning) depends on Śakti. It works when the primary meaning does not fit.
- **Śābdabodha** (verbal knowledge) has many causes, for example word knowledge and expectancy. Īśvarecchā is not called its cause.

Later Navya-Nyāya widened this to any convention (saṅketa), but the classical answer is Śakti itself.

questions.question_md: Which system takes the help of adṛṣṭa to prove the existence of god ?
questions.explanation:
Adṛṣṭa is the unseen moral force of past actions. It produces pleasure and pain in the right way. But adṛṣṭa is unconscious. An unconscious force cannot guide itself.

**Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika** use this point to prove God. A conscious being must guide adṛṣṭa and the atoms. That being is Īśvara. Udayana uses this argument in the *Nyāyakusumāñjali*.

- **Yoga** accepts Īśvara, but it proves God in a different way. It says that knowledge has degrees, so there must be a highest, unlimited knowledge.
- So the options that include Yoga are wrong. "Nyāya only" leaves out Vaiśeṣika.

questions.question_md: Select the code that states the correct sequence :
questions.explanation:
Yoga lists five states of the mind (citta bhūmi). They go from the lowest to the highest:

1. **Kṣipta**: restless. Rajas is strong.
2. **Mūḍha**: dull and sleepy. Tamas is strong.
3. **Vikṣipta**: partly steady but often distracted.
4. **Ekāgra**: fixed on one point. Sattva is strong.
5. **Niruddha**: all mental changes have stopped.

So the correct order is kṣipta, mūḍha, vikṣipta, ekāgra, niruddha.

- Option (2) puts mūḍha before kṣipta.
- Option (3) puts vikṣipta before mūḍha.
- Option (4) mixes the order.

questions.question_md:
Match List – I with List – II and choose the correct answer with the help of codes given below :

| List – I | List – II |
|---|---|
| a. Abhihitānvaya vāda | i. Manḍana |
| b. Anvitābhidhāna vāda | ii. Kumārila |
| c. Sphoṭavāda | iii. Prabhākara |
| d. Apoha vāda | iv. Diṅnaga |

**Codes :**
questions.explanation:
These are theories of sentence meaning and word meaning.

- **a. Abhihitānvaya vāda**: words first give their separate meanings, then the meanings join. This is the view of **Kumārila** (Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṁsā) → ii.
- **b. Anvitābhidhāna vāda**: words give meanings that are already connected. This is the view of **Prabhākara** → iii.
- **c. Sphoṭavāda**: meaning comes from a whole, indivisible sphoṭa. Bhartṛhari is the main thinker. Among the options, **Maṇḍana Miśra** defends it in his *Sphoṭasiddhi* → i.
- **d. Apoha vāda**: a word means "exclusion of others". This is the Buddhist view of **Diṅnāga** → iv.

The code is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv. Option (1) swaps Kumārila and Prabhākara.

questions.question_md:
Match List – I with List – II and choose the correct answer with the help of codes given below :

| List – I | List – II |
|---|---|
| a. Sāṁkhya Darśana | i. Asatkārya vāda |
| b. Dvaita Vedānta | ii. Vivartavāda |
| c. Advaita Vedānta | iii. Sadasatkārya vāda |
| d. Nyāya Darśana | iv. Satkārya vāda |

questions.explanation:
Each school has its own theory of cause and effect:

- **a. Sāṁkhya**: the effect already exists in the cause. This is **Satkārya vāda** → iv.
- **b. Dvaita Vedānta**: Madhva says that the effect exists in the cause in one way and does not exist in another way. This is **Sadasatkārya vāda** → iii.
- **c. Advaita Vedānta**: the world is only an appearance of Brahman, like a snake in a rope. This is **Vivarta vāda** → ii.
- **d. Nyāya**: the effect is a new thing. It did not exist before. This is **Asatkārya vāda** → i.

The code is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i. No other option gives Sāṁkhya its well-known satkārya view.

questions.question_md:
Given below are an Assertion (A) and a Reason (R). Consider them and select the correct code given below in the context of Śaṅkara’s Philosophy.

**Assertion (A) :** Brahman is abhinna nimitto pādāna Kāraṇa of jagat.

**Reason (R) :** There is nothing other than Brahman.

**Codes :**
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
**Abhinna nimitta upādāna kāraṇa** means "the cause that is both efficient and material".

- **(A) is true.** For Śaṅkara, Brahman is the efficient cause of the world, like a potter. Brahman is also the material cause, like clay. The two causes are not different. The *Brahmasūtra* (1.4.23) supports this.
- **(R) is true.** For Śaṅkara, nothing other than Brahman is real. There is no second thing.
- **(R) explains (A).** There is no second thing from which the world could come. So Brahman must be both the maker and the material of the world.

A spider is the usual example. It makes the web and also gives the thread from its own body.

questions.question_md: Select the correct sequence of the gradations of Mokṣa in Madhva Vedānta
questions.explanation:
Some Vedānta schools speak of four grades of liberation (mukti). They go from lower to higher closeness to God:

1. **Sālokya**: living in the same world as God.
2. **Sāmīpya**: living near God.
3. **Sārūpya**: having a form like God.
4. **Sāyujya**: entering God and sharing His joy.

For Madhva, the soul always stays different from God, even in Sāyujya. But it enjoys bliss in God.

- Option (1) gives the order from the top down.
- Options (3) and (4) mix the order.

questions.question_md: In the view of Śaṅkara, the only pramāṇa that imparts knowledge of Brahman is
questions.explanation:
For Śaṅkara, Brahman is beyond the senses and beyond ordinary reasoning. So only **Śabda** (verbal testimony), that is, the Śruti (the Upaniṣads), can give knowledge of Brahman. Sentences like "tat tvam asi" (you are that) teach the identity of the self and Brahman.

- **Pratyakṣa** (perception) knows only objects of the senses. Brahman is not such an object.
- **Anumāna** (inference) needs a perceived mark. Brahman has no such mark.
- **Arthāpatti** (postulation) also works only within experience.

Reason can support the meaning of the Śruti, but it cannot be the source of the knowledge of Brahman.

questions.question_md: The Indian philosopher who makes a distinction between Anupramāṇa and Kevala pramāṇa is
questions.explanation:
**Madhva** (Dvaita Vedānta) divides pramāṇa into two kinds:

- **Kevala pramāṇa**: direct, true knowledge of the object as it is. It is the knowledge itself.
- **Anupramāṇa**: the means that produce such knowledge. Madhva accepts three: perception, inference and testimony (āgama).

- **Patañjali** and **Īśvarakṛṣṇa** (Sāṁkhya) accept three pramāṇas, but they do not use this pair of terms.
- **Śaṅkara** accepts six pramāṇas (in the Advaita tradition). He also does not use this pair.

questions.question_md: One of the steps in Sādhana Caṭuṣṭaya according to Śaṅkara is
questions.explanation:
Śaṅkara says that a student must have four qualifications (**Sādhana Catuṣṭaya**) before the study of Vedānta:

1. **Nityānitya vastu viveka**: telling the eternal from the non-eternal.
2. **Ihāmutrārtha phala bhoga virāga**: no desire for rewards here or in heaven.
3. **Śamādi ṣaṭka sampatti**: six virtues such as calmness and self-control.
4. **Mumukṣutva**: a strong desire for liberation.

So Mumukṣutva is one of the steps.

- **Prakṛti–puruṣa jñāna** is the Sāṁkhya way to liberation.
- **Nityavibhūti** is a term of Rāmānuja's school (the eternal realm of God).
- **Anumāna jñāna** is inferential knowledge. It is not a qualification of the student.

questions.question_md: The teaching common to all the vedāntins is that Brahman is
questions.explanation:
The Vedānta schools do not agree about the qualities of Brahman.

- Advaita (Śaṅkara) says the highest Brahman is **Nirguṇa** (without qualities).
- Viśiṣṭādvaita (Rāmānuja) and Dvaita (Madhva) say Brahman is **Saguṇa** (with good qualities).

So Nirguṇa, Saguṇa or both together are not common to all.

But all schools accept the Upaniṣad text "satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma" (Brahman is truth, knowledge and infinite). So every Vedāntin says that Brahman is **Ananta** (infinite, without limit). This is why the examiner chose Ananta as the common teaching.

questions.question_md:
Given below are some modes of subjectivity :

i. Bodily Subjectivity
ii. Psychic Subjectivity
iii. Spiritual Subjectivity
iv. Religious Subjectivity

Which three modes of Subjectivity are accepted by K.C. Bhattacharya ? Select the correct answer from the codes given below :

**Codes :**
questions.explanation:
K.C. Bhattacharya wrote *The Subject as Freedom*. In it he describes the gradual freeing of the subject from the object. He speaks of three modes of subjectivity:

- **Bodily subjectivity**: the self felt as the body.
- **Psychic subjectivity**: the self as the mind, with images and thoughts.
- **Spiritual subjectivity**: the self as free from all objects.

So the answer is i, ii and iii. "Religious subjectivity" is not one of his three modes. Every other code includes it, so those codes are wrong.

questions.question_md: Which one of the following holds the view that ‘when you deprive truth of its appearance, it loses the best part of reality’ ?
questions.explanation:
**Tagore** says that truth is not opposed to its appearance. The world of colour, form and beauty shows truth to us. If we remove the appearance, truth loses its best part. This fits his poetic and humanist view of reality in works like *Personality*.

- **Vivekananda** follows Advaita. For him, appearance belongs to māyā.
- **Sri Aurobindo** speaks of the evolution of Spirit, not of appearance as the best part of truth.
- **J. Krishnamurti** asks us to see "what is" without images. He does not praise appearance in this way.

questions.question_md: Who among the following holds the view that ‘space, time and causation are not metaphysical realities, they are mere forms’ ?
questions.explanation:
**Vivekananda** explains māyā with the ideas of space, time and causation. He calls them the forms through which the Absolute appears as the world. They are like a glass. When we look at the Absolute through this glass, it appears as the many things of the world. So they are not ultimate realities. They are only forms.

He gives this view in his talks on Jñāna Yoga.

- **Tagore** and **Radhakrishnan** do not state the idea in this form.
- **J. Krishnamurti** does not build a theory of space, time and causation.

questions.question_md: Who among the following holds the view that ‘creation is plunge of the spirit into ignorance’ ?
questions.explanation:
**Sri Aurobindo** describes a double movement:

- **Involution**: the Spirit (Saccidānanda) descends step by step. At the bottom it becomes hidden in matter and Inconscience (total ignorance).
- **Evolution**: the Spirit rises again from matter to life, mind and then supermind.

So for Aurobindo, creation is the plunge of the Spirit into ignorance. He explains this in *The Life Divine*.

- **Tagore** sees creation as the joyful play of the infinite.
- **Gandhi** speaks of God as Truth, not of involution.
- **Vivekananda** explains the world through māyā, not through a plunge into Inconscience.

| b. Puruṣa | ii. Active |

questions.explanation:
In Sāṁkhya:

- **a. Prakṛti** (matter) is **active**. It changes and produces the world → ii.
- **b. Puruṣa** (consciousness) is **passive**. It only witnesses. It does not act → i.
- **c. Mahat** (cosmic intellect, buddhi) is the **first evolute** of Prakṛti → iv.

The code is a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii. Option (1) swaps active and passive. It also swaps the first and second evolute.

questions.question_md:
In the context of Locke’s philosophy, consider the given Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and then mark the correct option as given below :

**Assertion (A) :** All our knowledge is A posteriori.

**Reason (R) :** Knowledge is received through sensation and reflection.

**Options :**
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) does not provide the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true and (R) is false but (R) does not provide the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true and (R) is false but (R) provides the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) provides the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Locke is a classical empiricist (a thinker who says knowledge comes from experience).

- **(R) is true.** For Locke, the mind at birth is a blank tablet (tabula rasa). All ideas come from two sources: **sensation** (outer sense) and **reflection** (awareness of our own mental acts).
- **(A) is true** in the examiner's sense. Locke rejects innate ideas. So all our knowledge depends on experience, that is, it is a posteriori.
- **(R) explains (A).** Knowledge depends on experience *because* all ideas come from sensation and reflection.

Note: Locke accepts intuitive and demonstrative knowledge, for example mathematics. But even these use ideas that come from experience. So the examiner treats both statements as true and linked.

questions.question_md:
Match List – I with List – II and mark the correct code :

| List – I | List – II |
|---|---|
| a. Hume | i. Parallelism |
| b. Locke | ii. Scepticism |
| c. Berkeley | iii. Empiricism |
| d. Spinoza | iv. Idealism |

**Codes :**
questions.explanation:
Match each thinker with his main position:

- **a. Hume** → **Scepticism** (ii). He doubts causation, the self and induction.
- **b. Locke** → **Empiricism** (iii). All ideas come from experience.
- **c. Berkeley** → **Idealism** (iv). "To be is to be perceived."
- **d. Spinoza** → **Parallelism** (i). Mind and body are two attributes of one substance. Their states run parallel.

The code is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i. Option (2) gives parallelism to Locke and empiricism to Spinoza. Both are wrong.

questions.question_md: Sensationism, Empiricism and Representationism are altogether attributed to
questions.explanation:
All three labels fit **Locke**:

- **Empiricism**: all ideas come from experience.
- **Sensationism**: sensation is the main source of ideas about the outer world.
- **Representationism** (representative realism): we do not know objects directly. We know them through ideas that represent them.

- **Berkeley** is an empiricist, but he rejects representationism. For him, there is no matter behind ideas.
- **Hume** is an empiricist and a sceptic. He does not hold that ideas represent outer objects.
- **Kant** combines reason and experience. He is not a representationist in Locke's sense.
